In a statement published on social media, Kick It Out said: “Player welfare should always take precedence over the momentum or flow of a match, and it’s essential that managers and all leaders recognise this and set the tone with their language so that everyone can stand up to discrimination.

“We’re disappointed to hear reports of racist abuse towards Swansea’s Eom Ji-sung during Tuesday’s Championship game at Millwall. Both clubs have condemned the incident, and it’s positive that Millwall and match officials followed the right protocols so that action can be taken to identify any individual responsible.”

The statement added: “Protocols are in place to help match and security officials respond appropriately. That ensures players are protected and key details are captured so that accountability can follow, regardless of how long it takes.”

View image in fullscreen The match referee, Edward Duckworth, speaks to both managers during the break in play. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

Millwall have not responded to the Kick it Out statement, but said on Tuesday: “The club operates a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of discriminatory abuse. Any individual found to have engaged in such behaviour will face the strongest possible action.

“The club is working alongside the relevant authorities to establish the facts and is unable to comment further as tonight’s alleged incident is the subject of an ongoing police investigation, which the club fully supports.”

Swansea won the game 1-0, with Ronald scoring a late winner after the restart, and Neil admitted afterwards: “If we score, I probably don’t feel this way.” The 45-year-old added that the alleged abuse “has been reported and it’s not acceptable.”

The Swansea head coach, Vítor Matos, praised the referee and Millwall’s club staff for their responses to the incident. “The referee followed the protocol for these sort of situations, they did the right thing,” he said.

“Millwall did the right thing by announcing there is no place for this sort of thing. I’m happy with how it was handled, but really sad that it happened.”

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez refuses to apologise as he doubles down on outburst in social media post
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez refuses to apologise as he doubles down on outburst in social media post

Lisandro Martinez has doubled down on his frustrations towards Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox.

The Red Devils defender took an almighty swipe at Wilcox for a lack of squad strengthening following the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday.



3 Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United following the defeat at the Wanda Metropolitano Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Martinez is not the only United star frustrated with the perceived lack of ambition at board level.

He has since explained his actions in a lengthy social media post, insisting the club must maintain 'high standards' and remain ambitious.

What did Lisandro Martinez say in his statement?

"Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel," Martinez wrote.



"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win.



"And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.



"When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it’s us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

3 Wilcox is in the firing line at United following Martinez's comments Credit: Getty



"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Manchester United's summer transfer strategy

This summer presented a prime opportunity for United to strengthen the squad having secured Champions League qualification for the 2026/27 campaign.

But rather than improve across a number of areas, the Red Devils heavily invested in the midfield.

United spent all of their summer transfer budget on Carlos Baleba (£70million), Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m).



The previous summer, more than £200m was spent on forwards Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the first choice backline has remained relatively untouched since 2022.

3 Tielemans has started every Premier League game this season, but Baleba could now end up taking his place Credit: Getty

Manchester United's on-field woes

Martinez's frustrations with United's transfer dealings this summer have been exarcebated by a horror start to the 2026/27 Premier League campaign.



A 1-1 draw with Tottenham on Saturday, in which the Red Devils conceded in the 92nd minute, ensured United had their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Michael Carrick's side have also been eliminated from the EFL Cup, blowing a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 to Brighton in the third round.

United will look to shake off the midweek chaos when they return to Premier League action on Sunday against rivals Leeds.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe surpasses Lionel Messi’s Champions League record that Harry Kane can never break
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe surpasses Lionel Messi’s Champions League record that Harry Kane can never break

Kylian Mbappe became the youngest-ever player to reach 100 Champions League appearances in Real Madrid's thrilling 4-3 victory over Roma.

The Frenchman started at the Stadio Olimpico and brought up his century of games in Europe's premier competition as Jose Mourinho's side staged a stunning late comeback.

5 Mbappe clocked up yet another record in Real Madrid's victory Credit: Getty

Aged 27 years and 298 days, this saw Mbappe become the youngest player in the tournament's history to reach the milestone.

He surpassed the previous record, held by Lionel Messi, who achieved the feat at the age of 28 years and 84 days.

Coincidentally, the Argentine icon also reached his personal landmark against Roma, doing so in a 1-1 draw in September 2015.

Mbappe's record is one that Harry Kane, who has battled the ex-PSG star for the European Golden Boot in each of the last three seasons, can never break with the Bayern Munich marksman already 33.

How did Mbappe perform against Roma?

Mbappe was tasked with leading the line for Real against Roma, as manager Mourinho returned to face his former club.

And the Ballon d'Or contender marked his record-breaking night with a goal, as he pulled Los Blancos level after falling behind to Martin de Roon's opener.

He slammed home with an empathic finish from the edge of the box in the 25th minute.

In doing so, Mbappe achieved another milestone as he brought up his 72nd Champions League goal by scoring against Roma.

Before Wednesday's game, the France megastar had been tied in fifth place on the Champions League's all-time scoring charts on 71 goals, level with former Real legend Raul.

But his latest strike has now moved him into outright fifth in the leaderboard.

5 Mbappe rifled home Real Madrid's equaliser in the first half to mark his record-breaking 100th Champions League appearance Credit: Getty

5 Lionel Messi brought up his century of Champions League games after winning the competition three times Credit: AFP

Mbappe is also 18 behind another Real legend, Karim Benzema, who sits in fourth on the list with 90 European goals.

Real Madrid edge thriller

After making history in the first half, Mbappe's teammates took centre stage from then on as a quite thrilling game unfolded.

With the scoreline 1-1 at half time, Donyell Malen grabbed a quick-fire brace shortly after the break to put Roma 3-1 up.

This left the 15-time European champions staring at a shock defeat, before an incredible turn of events unfolded.

Carlos Espi pulled one back on 83 minutes to give Real hope, before Endrick equalised just two minutes later with his first goal of the season.

Antonio Rudiger then completed a stunning seven-minute turnaround when he turned home from a corner in the 90th minute.

5 Rudiger grabbed the winner in a classic game, but refused to celebrate after spending the 2016/17 season at Roma Credit: Getty

5 Mbappe and his teammates mobbed the ex-Chelsea defender after his astonishing late winner Credit: Getty

This sparked pandemonium among Real Madrid's fans, while the German refused to celebrate against former club Roma.

Victory for Real saw them keep up their 100 per cent record in Europe this season, having beaten Inter Milan 2-1 in their opening game.

The record-breaking Mbappe also struck in this game, with his goal against Roma taking his tally to two goals in the competition so far.

It continues his excellent form in front of goal, with Mbappe having bagged seven in eight La Liga appearances.

He will have to keep up goalscoring exploits too, after Vinicius Junior was given a four-game LaLiga ban for pulling an opponent's hair during Real's victory over Villareal at the weekend.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to miss El Clasico with Real Madrid star handed lengthy ban
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr has been handed a four-game ban which will cause him to miss the first El Clasico of the season.

The Real Madrid star was shown a straight red card for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair in Saturday's 1-0 win against Villarreal.



3 Vinicius Jr angrily confronted the referee after receiving a straight red card Credit: Getty

Vini Jr was introduced in the 52nd minute against Villarreal and thought he had scored his side's second goal.

Why was Vinicius Jr sent off?

However, a VAR review of the goal then clearly showed the Brazilian to have pulled Saliba's hair in the build-up before scoring.

After being sent to the pitchside monitor, referee Isidro Diaz de Mera then brandished a red card to Vinicius Jr's disgust.



The forward was left fuming by the decision and angrily approached the referee, before then having to be dragged away by his teammates.

His angry response to his dismissal has now landed him in more trouble, with authorities taking a dim view to his reactions.



The 26-year-old's 'aggressive attitude' after being sent off was deemed worthy of an extended four-game suspension.

According to the to the disciplinary report from the eighth round of LaLiga fixtures, the committee have handed down a two-match ban for the red card and a further two games for his protests afterwards.



The Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee suspended Vinicius Jr for two games for 'behaving violently (while) not being in a position to challenge for the ball' and a further two matches for 'protests' to the officials.

This is set to have a huge impact on Real Madrid in the coming weeks, starting with their next LaLiga clash against Sevilla on Saturday.

Worse still, Vinicius Jr will then miss his side's trip to Barcelona on October 25.

3 Vinicius Jr will now miss next weekend's clash with Sevilla and El Clasico after that Credit: Getty



He will then remain suspended for further games against Racing Club (November 1) at home and Valencia away (November 7).

With an international break coming immediately after Vinicius Jr's ban ends, this means the earliest he can return to LaLiga action is at home to Celta Vigo on November 22.

Despite this, reports in Spain suggest that Real want to appeal their star man’s ban.

Vinicius Jr has started all but one of his side's matches this season, chipping in with three goals and one assist during this time.



While he is now set to miss over a month of LaLiga action, the winger is still allowed to play in Champions League matches and started in Real's 4-3 away win at Roma on Wednesday night.

His antics against Villarreal marked the fourth straight red card of his senior career and his third since joining Real Madrid in 2018.

3 Vinicius Jr is now set to miss five weeks of LaLiga action Credit: Getty

Following the match, Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho did not attend the post-match news conference.



Vinicius Jr also later apologised when he posted a message on social media, saying he was 'sorry to the team and the [Real Madrid] fans'.

While he has established himself as one of the world's best players at the Bernabeu, he has struggled for consistency since starring at the World Cup.

The forward's recent performances for Brazil during the international break even prompted a bizarre 'body double' theory to emerge.

Sports.title: Man City suffer worst Champions League home defeat in history in front of shell-shocked Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Manchester City suffered their worst home defeat in Champions League history - with Gianluigi Donnarumma singled out for criticism.

The Citizens gloveman watched the ball fly past him a whopping three times in the opening half against Paris Saint-Germain, who ran out 4-2 victors at the Etihad Stadium.



4 Donnarumma had an evening to forget against his former employers Credit: AFP

City's nightmare start marked the first time they'd shipped three goals in the first half at home since 2015, while it was the first time they had trailed by three goals at half-time of a home game since against Manchester United in the FA Cup in January 2012.

And legendary talkSPORT broadcaster Adrian Durham, who was at the Etihad Stadium to call the action alongside Andy Gray, believed Donnarumma's display would give plenty of verbal ammunition to the PSG supporters, who once chanted his name.

What did Durham say about Donnarumma?

"A word about Donnarumma, he's let in three," Durham said at half-time.



"Man City have never let in three in the first half of a Champions League tie here ever.

"Donnarumma has got to go up the other end in front of the PSG fans in the second half and they're going to give him, their former keeper, a lot of grief, and he probably deserves it.



"That first one, (Desire) Doue's hit it, it's not exactly a rocket, he can't let that pass to me.

"He's ginormous, his reach is huge, he can't let that go in."

Andy Gray reacts to Gianluigi Donnarumma's display

Gray agreed with Durham's assessment, especially when it came to Doue's strike.



He remarked: "Listen, if he's beat far-side with one bent into the top corner like [Jeremy] Doku could do, then you hold your hands up and say, 'What a finish.'

"But that one in that side, near post, you should not be beaten.

4 City hadn't trailed by three goals by half-time at home since January 2012 Credit: Getty

"And you're right, Doue hit it OK, but he didn't hit the back of it crisply, he didn't fire it in past him and the pace beat him.

"It was just bad positioning from the goalkeeper who should have done better."



It was a first half to forget for City, who had former manager Pep Guardiola watching on in the stands.

Doue opened proceedings in the 13th minute before Ousmane Dembele doubled the visitors' advantage just two minutes later with a close-range header.

Vitinha completed the first half rout in the 32nd minute with a fine strike from outside the box.

Erling Haaland sets Manchester City record

Erling Haaland pulled one back for the hosts early in the second half, cementing himself as City's outright top scorer in the Champions League with 37 goals in 41 games.



4 Guardiola returned to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since he left at the end of last season Credit: AFP

4 His smiles before the match were soon gone as PSG smashed City in the first half

But it proved to be little more than a consolation as summer signing Maghnes Akliouche restored PSG's three-goal advantage just ten minutes later courtesy of another Donnarumma error.

It appeared Donnarumma made a strong save to keep out Akliouche's long-range strike, only to then palm the ball into his own net.



The Italian's late fumble had Gray scratching his head.

"I looked away and was about to say, 'What a save,'" Gray said.

"I can't believe that. Maybe he should have tipped it over. That's game over."

Haaland added a second to take his Champions League tally to 38 goals, before Donnarumma somewhat redeemed himself after saving Ferran Torres' penalty in the closing stages.

Sports.title: FIFA seeking rule change to avoid repeat of Folarin Balogun World Cup scandal
Sports.content:
FIFA are poised to amend its rules to prevent suspensions from automatic one-match bans.

The tweak is being made to avoid a repeat of the Folarin Balogun scandal that rocked the World Cup.

2 Balogun scored three goals at the World Cup Credit: Getty

What happened with Folarin Balogun at the World Cup?

Balogun was sent off during the United States' round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, which triggered an automatic one-game suspension.

However, the decision was overturned following an intervention from the White House and the forward was permitted to play in the USMNT'S last-16 tie against Belgium, which they lost.

The motion is set to be discussed at the first session of the 37-member FIFA Council on Thursday.

talkSPORT understands the proposal is viewed as FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who claims he played no role in the decision, addressing the Balogun scandal.

It is also understood the wording was rushed through on Tuesday evening and Infantino's critics still want all correspondence shared from the incident.

Balogun's reprieve sparked significant reaction from several sporting bodies, including UEFA, of which Belgium is a member.

"Yesterday's decision to suspend for a probationary period of a year the implementation of the one-match automatic suspension following the red card issued to the player Folarin Balogun crossed a read line," a UEFA statement read.

"Football, like any other sports, relies on rules, which are the basis for fair, honest and transparent competition.

"Sometimes rules are open to interpretation. In this case not.

"A minimum automatic suspension of one match following a red card is not a discretionary option and does not require the decision of a competent body to be enacted.

2 Infantino's decisions throughout the summer have put him under serious pressure to keep his job Credit: Getty

"It is a principle embedded in regulations, which cannot be made subject to exceptions, let alone in the middle of a tournament where several other players have been in the same situation and regularly served their suspension."

UEFA additionally labelled it an 'unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision.'

Gianni Infantino's nightmare summer

Thursday's meeting marks the first time the council has gathered following Infantino's controversial plan to sell the World Cup was revealed.

The scheme was met with widespread condemnation, as the FA, UEFA and CONCACAF all released strongly-worded statements in response.

Infantino's controversial summer has now left him facing a serious battle to be re-elected as FIFA president.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega is the only other confirmed candidate, while Arsene Wenger was endorsed by former Arsenal pupil Emmanuel Petit for the role.

The deadline for candidates to be nominated is November 18, with elections to take place at the 77th FIFA Congress in March.

Sports.title: Fans wanting Arsenal star dropped are crazy – there’s a vendetta against him
Sports.content:
Darren Bent has launched into a passionate defence of Bukayo Saka -insisting fans have wrongly made him a scapegoat for club and country.

Saka's form has come under scrutiny this season, but he delivered the perfect response to his critics in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Lille as he scored and assisted in a stellar 25-minute cameo.

4 Saka opened his Champions League account for the season against Lille Credit: Getty

Ahead of Tuesday's Champions League victory, the winger faced criticism over a perceived slow start to the campaign, despite having scored three goals in eight games up to that point.

This came to a head after Arsenal's win over Leeds on Saturday afternoon, where he managed just two shots and attempted one dribble at the Emirates.

It prompted club legend David O'Leary to question Saka's displays, who claimed he wasn't justifying his £300,000-a-week contract.

Illness saw the 25-year-old drop to the bench against Lille, with Noni Madueke starting in his place before coming on in the 65th minute.

And he made an instant impact - assisting Eberechi Eze's strike to make it 2-0 and then rolled in his side's third goal four minutes later.

This took Saka's tally to four goals in nine games this season, and led ex-Tottenham striker Bent to leap to his defence.

What has Darren Bent said about Bukayo Saka?

Speaking on talkSPORT Drive, Bent insisted Saka has taken unfair flack this term, and claimed criticism of him would've been more justified last season.

In the 2025/26 campaign, the England star managed just seven Premier League goals, with question marks over his fitness at times.

On Saka, Bent said: “I thought he’s looked quite sharp this season, if I'm honest. There were times last season where he maybe wasn't at his best.

"He played a lot of games last season, but still, seven in the Premier League for someone like Saka and three in the Champions League - he's better than that.”

4 Saka looked back to his best against Lille as he also opened his Champions League assist account this term Credit: Getty

Bent then highlighted Saka's importance to Arsenal by comparing his impact against Lille with positional rival Madueke.

He continued: “Last night was a clear indication about his levels. Madueke obviously started, struggled again."

The talkSPORT pundit argued: "Madueke, not good enough, not really creating anything. Saka comes on, it's an instant impact.

“I think a lot of the work that Saka does as well goes unnoticed, because the amount of times Arsenal players will give him the ball when he's got two people on his back and he manages to hold onto it, hold someone off and then at the last minute find the pass.

“He literally takes us up the pitch, he holds onto possession. I think he's top drawer, I really do."

Continuing to defend Saka, Bent insisted criticism of him is nothing new, pointing to previous calls for him to be dropped by England during Euro 2024.

4 Saka penned a new five-year deal with Arsenal in February, before going on to win the Premier League Credit: Getty

“For whatever reason, people are always looking for reasons to doubt him, whether it be for England [or Arsenal].

“I remember at the last Euros people were talking about, 'We need to change something, this performance hasn't been good enough, get Saka out.'

“There always seems to be a kind of a vendetta against him.”

Bukayo Saka's career at a glance

While his impact has been questioned, Saka has established himself as a mainstay for both club and country in recent years.

He was a regular starter for England at both Euro 2020 and 2024, having also hit double figures in goals for Arsenal in the seasons of the major tournaments.

At the 2026 World Cup, Saka began the tournament on the bench amid an Achilles injury, before recovering to start four games as the Three Lions claimed a third-place finish - scoring a hat-trick in the bronze medal clash with France.

4 Saka managed three goals and an assists in seven appearances at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

Having also been named England's Men's Player of the Year in 2022 and 2023, Bent insisted there should be no question marks about the forward's ability.

Rounding off, he said: “The guy's won England Player of the Year twice. It's crazy!

"But for Arsenal, he looks sharp, he looks hungry."

Sports.title: Liverpool create Champions League history as Bradley Barcola achieves 134-year club first
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola made Liverpool history as his hat-trick inspired a thrilling 6-3 victory over LASK in the Champions League.

The 24-year-old scored his first goals since his big-money summer arrival to get the Reds back to winning ways in Austria - becoming the first Frenchman to net a treble for the club.

3 Barcola got on the score sheet for Liverpool for the first time since joining from Paris Saint-Germain Credit: Getty

Heading into the clash off the back of Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Manchester City, Andoni Iraola's side quickly put this behind them with a dominant first-half display.

They raced into a 3-0 lead, with Barcola opening his Reds account with a quick-fire double after Ronald Araujo headed in the opener.

The Frenchman grabbed his first goal for the club in his seventh appearance as he swept home after good work from Rio Ngumoha, before lashing home his second to make it three.

What Champions League record have Liverpool achieved?

In truth, the scoreline could have been even greater at half-time, with Liverpool recorded a staggering 19 shots on goal.

This was the most shots by an away team on record in the first half of a UEFA Champions League away match since statistics began being tracked in the 2002/03 campaign.

The second-half brought even more goals, with Jeremie Frimpong making it 4-0 before Robert Ljubicic pulled one back for the hosts.

Barcola then took centre stage on 66 minutes, sealing his hat-trick on by finishing off a slick team move to tap home Frimpong's cross.

The winger's treble saw him break multiple records, as he became the first Frenchman in Liverpool's 134-year history to bag three in a game.

This was also the first Champions League hat-trick from a Reds players since Luis Diaz did so against Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, and a first away from home since Mohamed Salah's at Rangers in 2022.

And the drama didn't stop there, with a chaotic final 20 minutes then unfolding which yielded three more goals.

3 Barcola had come under criticism following his slow start at Liverpool before stealing the show in Austria Credit: Getty

3 Liverpool were one goal off equalling the record for the most goals in a Champions League game (10) against LASK Credit: Getty

Lewis Koumas then got on the score sheet in the 72nd minute to score his first-ever European goal for Liverpool and make it 6-1, with Frimpong once again the provider.

But LASK then threatened a late fightback, as Florian Flecker then netted a quick-fire brace to pull the scoreline back to 6-3.

It's a result which sees Liverpool make it two wins from two in the Champions League, and Barcola's display will no doubt delight manager Iraola.

Having joined the Reds from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106million, rising to £123m, the France star had failed to hit the ground running.

He started in the goalless draw with Fulham and the 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, and again in the City defeat at the weekend.

However, Barcola failed impact any of the three games, and was without a goal contribution in his first six appearances in all competitions.

But with the highly-rated Frenchman ending his drought in spectacular fashion against LASK, he will now be looking to open his Premier League account against Brentford on Saturday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told he could be sacked this weekend as potential replacement options emerge
Sports.content:
Manchester United line up three-man shortlist with Michael Carrick told he could be sacked this weekend

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler is one potential option for Manchester United should Michael Carrick be sacked, talkSPORT understands.

It is understood that Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte also have admirers among Old Trafford bosses.



3 Hurzeler could become the first German to manage the Red Devils on a permanent basis Credit: Getty

Why is Michael Carrick under pressure at Manchester United?

Carrick finds himself under pressure following a 2-0 loss against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night, a result that prompted Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox for a lack of squad strengthening.

The result extended United's winless run to a fifth match across all competitions, which included a 1-1 draw against Spurs that condemned the Red Devils to their worst start to a Premier League campaign in 40 years.

Carrick will be desperate to avoid letting that figure rise to six when United return to Premier League action on Sunday with a trip to historic rivals Leeds.



Worryingly, talkSPORT's chief live football anchor Adrian Durham predicts Leeds 'could do a number' on the Red Devils, which could expedite Carrick's axing.

What has been said on Michael Carrick's future?

"Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go," Durham said on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"It feels like it's something that he can't stop unless they turn around those results.

"Elland Road will be fierce on Sunday, Leeds hate Manchester United.

"They would love nothing more at Elland Road to put that dagger in.

"I think that Leeds could do a number on Manchester United."

Earlier in the show, Durham had remarked: "You've got to look at the players, absolutely.



3 No team picked up more league points than Carrick in his 17 games last term, but he has overseen just one win this season Credit: Getty

"And you have to ask the question, is Michael Carrick going to be good enough to manage Manchester United?

"Let's analyse that, because he made some changes yesterday, tactically, that absolutely baffled and floored me and they proved to be their undoing."

Who could take over Carrick should he be sacked?

Of the three names on United's shortlist, Nagelsmann and Conte are both available to start straight away.



Conte departed Napoli via mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann resigned from his post as Germany boss after they were eliminated by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup.

It is understood United director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is pushing Nagelsmann's case internally should Carrick depart.

As for Hurzeler, he is tied down to Brighton until 2029 having signed an extension in May.

3 Nagelsmann has been out of club football since he was sacked by Bayern in March 2023 Credit: Getty



The German, who is understood to be favoured by Wilcox, has the Seagulls sitting third in the Premier League this term thanks to four wins from their opening six fixtures.

Hurzeler also masterminded a Brighton comeback to dump United out in the third round of the EFL Cup in September.

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as former Man United star plays in England for the first time in over FOUR years - after Old Trafford career unravelled following rape arrest
Sports.content:
Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as former Man United star plays in England for the first time in over FOUR years - after Old Trafford career unravelled following rape arrest

Mason Greenwood was booed repeatedly on his first appearance in an English football stadium since 2022.

Greenwood joined the Turkish giants for £36million from Marseille last summer after being cut from the United first team when he was arrested and charged with attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour in October 2022, before charges and the case were dropped in February 2023 when key witnesses withdrew. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The former Manchester United player was one of Fenerbahce’s highest-profile signings last summer and he has history with Aston Villa.

Greenwood’s name was booed when the teams were announced and Villa supporters targeted him with chants and catcalls whenever he touched the ball in the early stages.

Operating on the right of Fener’s attack, Greenwood was facing his former Manchester United team-mate Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who had switched to left-back with Ian Maatsen and Matteo Ruggeri injured.

There were tussles with Wan-Bissaka in the early exchanges, with Greenwood occasionally dropping much deeper to receive the ball. In the 19th minute, after a burst by the lively Oguz Aydin, Greenwood steered a shot from 20 yards straight at Zion Suzuki.

Mason Greenwood (pictured) was roundly booed by Aston Villa fans tonight

He has a solitary England cap, from a Nations League meeting in Iceland in September 2020. He is also eligible for Jamaica but last year he decided against accepting the call from then-boss Steve McClaren. Before tonight, Greenwood had six goals in 14 appearances for the Istanbul giants.

He played 69 minutes in total as his side were humbled at Villa Park, losing 3-0.

This was not the first time Greenwood had crossed swords with Villa, having been hurled to the ground by Tyrone Mings during a pre-season friendly against Marseille in August 2025, following an altercation with Villa midfielder Amadou Onana. Greenwood, 25, was perhaps grateful that the 6ft 5ins Onana missed this match due to injury.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez admits he 'spoke out of anger and frustration' during bombshell interview criticising Man United hierarchy - as Argentine insists he 'believes in everyone' but fails to say sorry in 271-word statement
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez admits he 'spoke out of anger and frustration' during bombshell interview criticising Man United hierarchy - as Argentine insists he 'believes in everyone' but fails to say sorry in 271-word statement

Lisandro Martinez took to social media in a late bid to dilute his scathing comments 24 hours on from his blistering criticism of club bosses.

United’s players had Wednesday off after flying straight back from Spain following Tuesday’s Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid and Martinez’s bombshell television interview in which he accused the Old Trafford board and director of football Jason Wilcox of failing in the transfer market last summer.

United remained tight-lipped on what action – if any – was to be taken against the Argentina international ahead of a return to training, but it the defender took matters into his own hands by explaining – but crucially not apologising – what he meant.

‘When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club,’ Martinez said, in part of his statement.

‘To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.’

He added: ‘We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top. I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward.

Lisandro Martinez has broken his silence after Tuesday night's extraordinary post-match rant

‘I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment. My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge.’

The impact of Martinez’s initial statement is still likely to be felt through until Sunday’s trip to face Leeds United at Elland Road, while team-mate Amad Diallo is also in the spotlight after he added more fuel to the fire with a message on social media which read ‘f***ing disgrace, I have no words’, although it’s unclear what the Ivorian was referring to.

United will likely need to call on Martinez at Leeds with a number of injuries in defence. Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui have been out of action, and Matthijs De Ligt only returned on the bench as an unused substitute in Madrid after nearly a year out with a back injury.

Martinez’s long-term future is more uncertain, however. He is out of contract at the end of June, although United can extend it by another year.

They are unlikely to let a 28-year-old World Cup winner leave as a free agent five years after his £57million move from Ajax, but could trigger the extension so they can demand a transfer fee for him.

Martinez took aim at the United hierarchy in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games in Madrid when he was asked if the club have backed Michael Carrick enough. ‘I don't think so,’ he said. ‘He does his best. You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager.

‘What about other areas? Tonight it is easy to say the coach and easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.

‘I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

‘I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.’

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola returns to Manchester City: Legendary former boss attends PSG clash after insisting he will 'always be behind' former club following Premier League's bombshell cheating verdict
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since his emotional farewell in the summer, with his former club marooned in the biggest scandal in English football history.

The Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles during his ten-year stint in Manchester, threw his support behind his former side as they took on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Guardiola was sat in Manchester City's directors' box for the tie, seated two rows behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

The 55-year-old watched on as his former side fell 3-0 down to reigning European champions PSG in the first half and ultimately succumbing to a 4-2 defeat despite a spirited display in the second.

Guardiola has been replaced by Enzo Maresca, with the new boss now having to contend with the explosive fallout of the Premier League bombshell verdict, in which City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them.

The era covering the charges - from 2009 to 2018 - laid the foundations for Guardiola's huge success at the Etihad Stadium, and has called into question the legendary manager's legacy as a result.

City have strenuously denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict, while Guardiola took to Instagram in the wake of the findings to publicly back his former club.

Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since leaving the club

Guardiola was seated two rows behind Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano

Man City chairman Khaldoon warmly embraced PSG chief executive Nasser Al-Khelaifi before the match

'I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

'Let me be clear: we will get through this together.

'I love you all.'

City received an overwhelmingly positive reception in their first match back at the Etihad following the seismic verdict, with supporters rallying around the club despite the sheer volume of charges found against the Premier League leaders.

Prior to kick-off, Man City fans created a tifo reading 'CTID', meaning 'City 'til I die'.

Maresca's side were treated to an altogether more hostile welcome by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, in their first competitive fixture since the guilty findings.

But the visitors rode the early storm to run away with a convincing 3-0 victory, with their jubilant celebrations the subject of criticism from the watching football world.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all scored in the space of 13 second-half minutes, with wild scenes in front of an exuberant away end.

Maresca danced down the touchline and stuck fingers in his ears, with staff and players branded arrogant by their detractors.

Maresca hit back at critics before their Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad.

'Criticised for what?' he said. 'We won 3-0 at Anfield! What do you want us to do? And even if it was 0-1, it would be exactly the same.

'I'm here today, and the players are here today, to win tomorrow's game. And we work every day to win games. It's the only thing, again, that we can think and be focussed.

'The rest? It's just things from outside that we need to deal with, but we were so, so, so happy inside the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.'

Maresca added: 'We were very happy, sharing time with our fans. Probably it's been more tough for our fans than our players or for me.

Guardiola watched on as his former side went 3-0 down to European champions PSG in the first half

Man City players huddled on the pitch after going 3-0 down and ultimately suffered a 4-2 loss

Man City fans made a display reading 'CTID' - City 'til I die - before the Champions League tie

'It's more complicated for them because if I am an Arsenal fan or Utd fan, I look at City fans and say 'hey my friend, you are a cheat'. Inside the changing room we were very happy because we knew how difficult Anfield is. Anfield was unbelievable.'

City skipper Ruben Dias stood behind Maresca's words – and claimed they will continue to celebrate with passion.

'We'll celebrate however we feel in the moment,' Dias said. 'It'll be a show of how much things mean to us.

'Yes there is a lot of noise and it's almost impossible to not see something – even us being so private. But I feel like we're also very good at focusing on ourselves.

'You build yourself against any kind of noise. I feel like I speak for the whole group when I say we're very calm. We trust the club. We know the team we've got and want to win. It's the same noise as before because people don't love us.'

Sports.title: Man City 2-4 PSG: This was some way for Enzo Maresca's side to lose - PSG continue to be the standard bearers, but City are not going to be shunted into irrelevance, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Man City 2-4 PSG: This was some way for Enzo Maresca's side to lose - PSG continue to be the standard bearers, but City are not going to be shunted into irrelevance, writes IAN LADYMAN

Maybe nothing will be simple and straightforward for Manchester City ever again. Not the future, not the present. Not the politics and maybe not even the football.

Here against the Champions of Europe, with Pep Guardiola watching on from beneath his flat cap in the directors' box, Enzo Maresca's City threatened to follow the adrenaline shot of Sunday's win at Anfield with a complete flatline at the Etihad.

This for a while looked and felt like the night reality dawned. When all the noise and celebration and defiance of the weekend faded to grey. When the impact of playing the next weeks and months under the shadow of crushing uncertainty began to feel too much.

Three down to Luis Enrique's rampant PSG side after 31 minutes, City were on the verge of being embarrassed in front of their former coach and their own supporters. It was three and it could have been five. Goals for Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha had ripped a hole in City's hearts.

Yet somehow, from the canvas, City found a pulse. They found a reaction, some adrenaline and – in the second-half – a comeback that did not quite serve as another two-fingered salute to the world but indicated at least that a coach and a group of players who have done absolutely nothing wrong are not going to be shunted into irrelevance as meekly as many would like.

City couldn't pull this off. To do so would have been quite ridiculous. But they terrified PSG in a second period played in an atmosphere of utter frenzy.

Vitinha (left) and Desire Doue (right) were both on the scoresheet for PSG in a rampant first half-hour

But Manchester City showed they will not fade into oblivion as they showed second-half fight

Erling Haaland scored twice for City in that spell and also hit the bar. Late on, with the score at 4-2, he almost slid one in at the far post. Heaven knows where that would have taken us all had it gone in.

A goal in between Haaland's brace from PSG's Maghnes Akliouche had ensured that City never quite got to within smelling distance. At the death, meanwhile, former City forward Ferran Torres, on as a substitute, missed a penalty for the French team.

At full-time, though, this huge modern stadium was still almost full. Maresca's team were applauded off after a lap of honour. How many teams get to do that having conceded four? These are strange and vaguely terrifying times for English football's most successful recent club but if and when City do tumble down the leagues, it appears they will do so together.

Even without the events of the last fortnight, this would have represented the biggest night of their season so far. After all their years of trying, PSG have finally established themselves as the standard bearers of European football.

For a while City merely flunked it. They were wretched without the ball during a first-half in which the game was ultimately lost. They were slow and lacking intelligence to the degree that the French team found far too much space in which to play.

As usual, PSG moved the ball devastatingly as they sought to exploit it. Even so, the way Doue was able to shoot low past two City defenders and in at Donnarumma's near post from 20 yards in the 13th minute was criminal from the point of view of the home team.

PSG's celebrations served as a tribute to the calibre of the opposition. This was a big night for Enrique's team too. Two minutes later they were dancing again.

This time the danger flowed down the right into space. Dembele's floated pass across goal to Doue was well judged and the way it was returned to him on the first-time half volley was sublime. As Dembele headed the ball down and in, it felt already like this game was over. It wasn't. Not quite.

Pep Guardiola watched on as his former side showed their credentials under Enzo Maresca

City tried to get a foothold. They hustled in midfield and tried to stretch PSG by using wingers Jeremy Doku and Antoine Semenyo whenever possible. All the while, though, PSG carried that latent threat.

The speed at which they carried the ball upfield was as alarming as it was thrilling. Just after the half hour, right-back Achraf Hakimi headed a Doue cross back across goal and against the post but it didn't matter. From the next phase of play his team scored anyway.

Donnarumma's clearance came back towards City on halfway and every PSG player who touched the ball in the ensuing passage did so at their own apparent leisure. Only when it was moved to the edge of the City penalty area did the pace quicken.

Warren Zaire-Emery's back heel flick to Vitinha was perfect and the Portuguese international drilled the ball in from 16 yards.

City's choice options were now clear. Shrivel and die or find something from within. It was to their credit that they took the latter. Twice before half-time they threatened, through Doku and Haaland. Then, in a frantic and quite extraordinary second-half, they persistently threatened to claw their way back.

Three times in five early minutes, City could have scored. A Semenyo shot was deflected over, Enzo Fernandez headed wide and then substitute Iliman Ndiaye was denied point blank by Matvei Safonov at his near post.

With the crowd energised, City rode a wave of fresh adrenaline. In the 53rd minute, Ndiaye crossed and Haaland scored with a flick header. Briefly something truly extraordinary was on. It was PSG's turn to look a little lost.

After further flurries of City attacking activity, Akliouche turned well to shoot high from 18 yards and Donnarumma could only watch as the ball flew up off his outstretched hand and landed back down over the goal line. Once again the outcome felt settled. Once again City came back.

Josko Gvardiol had a header cleared off the line by Nuno Mendes as the hosts battled

City showed despite the loss that if and when they fall down the leagues they will do so together

Josko Gvardiol saw a header cleared from the line before Haaland landed one on the bar. And then, with 15 minutes still remaining, Haaland side footed in his team's second goal from inside the area.

City kept surging forwards. This was gripping, crazy playground football and chances came on the back of it. Maresca's team ended the night having taken 27 of the night's 42 shots. It was some way to lose.

Sports.title: Footballer Antoine Semenyo 'was racially abused by wheelchair-using Liverpool fan who also threw chewing gum at him'
Sports.content:
Footballer Antoine Semenyo 'froze' after he was racially abused by a Liverpool fan before the man then threw chewing gum at him, a court has heard.

Semenyo, who was playing for Bournemouth at the time, was allegedly racially abused by Mark Mogan, 47, as he went to take a throw-in 30 minutes into the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year.

Simon Jones, prosecuting, told Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Wednesday that the footballer saw Mogan, a wheelchair-user, to the right of him and heard him shout: 'Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black b******.'

He said: 'That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

'Mr Semenyo briefly froze as he couldn't believe what the male had said.'

Mogan then shouted 'I'm talking to you, you c***', the court heard.

Mr Jones said: 'He looked straight at Antoine Semenyo when directing this abuse to him.

'Antoine Semenyo didn't say anything back to him and went to take the throw-in, however he was clearly hurt and upset with the racial abuse that had come his way.'

Footballer Antoine Semenyo, then playing for Bournemouth, 'froze' after he was racially abused by a Liverpool fan during a match at Anfield on August 15 last year (pictured during the match)

Semenyo could be seen turning to his right and speaking with the Liverpool fan after allegedly being racially abused by the man during the match

Mark Mogan, who denies racially aggravated behaviour, suffered a seizure during the lunch break in proceedings and was taken to hospital by ambulance

The footballer, who now plays for Manchester City, reported the incident to match referee Anthony Taylor when the ball next went out of play and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half time, the court was told.

Two short video clips of the incident were shown to the court, in which Mr Jones said the defendant could be seen in an 'agitated and angry state'.

He said witnesses saw Mogan take chewing gum from his mouth and throw it at Semenyo, striking him on the right side of his shorts.

Mr Jones said: 'We say that was plainly an unsavoury action from an angry man.'

In a statement read to the court, fellow Liverpool fan Neil Sherratt said he saw Mogan, who sits next to him at matches, leave his bay in the disabled section of the Main Stand and approach the pitch as Semenyo came to take the throw in.

He said he heard Mogan shout something along the lines of 'hurry up' and saw Semenyo turn towards him.

He said: 'Semenyo had a shocked look on his face and I believe he has replied back by saying "you what?"'

Another fan, Nicholas Collins, said after the incident Mogan became 'very cocky and brazen' and said: 'If the bizzies (police) come I'm going to deck them. I'm not going anywhere.'

Semenyo, pictured with his wife Jordeen, now plays for Manchester City

Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, was interviewed by police the following day and told officers he had shouted at Semenyo to 'hurry up'.

'His account was that Antoine Semenyo called him a cripple which upset him,' Mr Jones said.

'He said he then threw some chewing gum onto the floor but not at Antoine Semenyo.

'The prosecution say Mr Mogan clearly lied in that police interview.'

In the aftermath of the incident, Semenyo thanked everyone for the 'overwhelming messages of support'.

He wrote in a statement on X: 'Last night at Anfield will stay with me forever - not because of one person's words, but because of how the entire football family stood together.

'To my @afcbournemouth teammates who supported me in that moment, to the @LiverpoolFC players and fans who showed their true character, to the @premierleague officials who handled it professionally - thank you. Football showed its best side when it mattered most.

'Scoring those two goals felt like speaking the only language that truly matters on the pitch. This is why I play - for moments like these, for my teammates, for everyone who believes in what this beautiful game can be.

'The overwhelming messages of support from across the football world remind me why I love this sport. We keep moving forward, together.'

Semenyo had been expected to give evidence over a videolink on Wednesday afternoon, having had a work commitment which prevented him from appearing in the morning.

But Mogan, who the court previously heard has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair, suffered a seizure during the lunch break and was taken to hospital by ambulance.

An application to proceed with the trial in his absence was refused by District Judge Mary Dowrick. The trial is expected to continue at a later date.

Mogan, of Dovecot, Liverpool, denies racially aggravated behaviour.

Sports.title: Unai Emery's 'no excuses' culture finally pays off and how Nicolas Jackson proved he was signed for more than just goals, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - as Villans hit Fenerbahce for SIX
Sports.content:
No North Stand, no problem. Aston Villa delivered their most emphatic European win and their first home victory of the campaign as Mason Greenwood made an anonymous return to an English stadium.

The former Manchester United winger, who last played in England in January 2022, was barracked throughout by the home fans.

Greenwood was dropped from the United first team when he was arrested and charged with attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour in October 2022, before charges and the case were dropped in February 2023 when key witnesses withdrew. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The 25-year-old was one of Fenerbahce’s highest-profile signings last summer but struggled in the duel with former United team-mate Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

By contrast, Villa excelled against the desperately poor Turkish giants, with Johan Manzambi and a double from Nicolas Jackson making the game safe before half-time. Ross Barkley added two more – one from the spot – in the second half and substitute Tammy Abraham made it a record win.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the main talking points from Villa’s second straight Champions League win, achieved with the Prince of Wales watching from the directors’ box.

Aston Villa made history with their most emphatic win in Europe against Fenerbahce

Tammy Abraham was the last of the goal scorers with Ross Barkley and Johan Manzambi among the scorers

Villa's most famous fan Prince William was in high spirits as he took in the night at Villa Park

No excuses culture pays off

Villa boss Unai Emery will never allow his side to blame poor results on external factors. That means he rejects the idea that Villa will suffer by playing in a three-sided ground.

The club hope to take their capacity beyond 50,000 in time for the start of next season but in the meantime, one end of the ground is a building site. Villa need a bigger ground to make more money and that means shutting one end of it for a minimum one season.

Before this clash Villa had lost to Arsenal and Nottingham Forest and drawn with Brentford here but Emery would not allow players or fans to dwell on their quieter ground.

‘Not ideal, but never an excuse,’ said Emery. ‘We must accept the sacrifice of being without the North Stand, but we also understand it is for the greater good.

‘Because next season, and for years to come, Villa Park will be a stadium with greater capacity, improved facilities and an even more extraordinary atmosphere.

‘It is like when we have an injured important player. We must accept, not cry, and everyone has to deliver their best to overcome this situation.’

As weak as Fener were, Villa were sharper than they have been all season here. Johan Manzambi is growing with every match and deserved his goal, which took a huge deflection off Milan Skriniar. Wan-Bissaka looked comfortable and Boubacar Kamara looked much more like himself.

Nobody said it would be easy playing in front of fewer fans and there were less than 35,000 at this one. Just don’t let Emery hear you moaning about it.

Unai Emery has not wanted to place the blame for Villa's sluggish start on anything other than what he can control

Nicolas Jackson offers Emery more than just goals - although he bagged a 10-minute brace on the night

All-Action Jackson

We have questioned many of Villa’s transfers in these pages so it is only fair we applaud them when they get one right.

Many online were quick to mock Emery when he paid £65million for a player who had struggled towards the end of his career at Chelsea, when he seemed to collect more yellow cards than goals.

But Emery had worked with Jackson at Villarreal and knew exactly what he could offer. The Senegal forward now has five goals in all competitions – bear in mind Ollie Watkins, the man he replaced, did not reach that tally last season until December 27.

Jackson is about more than the goals. His pace stretches defences but his link play is solid too, meaning he is developing a nice understanding with Manzambi.

His goals were similar – clean right-footed efforts from just outside the box that found the bottom corner, though former Manchester City pair Ederson and Nathan Ake should have done much better with Jackson’s second.

Jackson was probably aggrieved to be denied the chance of a hat-trick when Barkley took the ball for the penalty but he could be very happy with his night’s work.

Mason Greenwood's return to English soil was a disappointment in a dire Fenerbahce side

Dire Fenerbahce

If Ederson and Ake had played like this when they were at City, they would not have won so many trophies.

The Brazil goalkeeper was so sluggish in trying to save Jackson’s strike and Ake was even worse. He made little attempt to block Jackson’s shot and like the rest of his team, looked barely interested for most of the game.

Fener have signed too many players whose best days are behind them. Happily for Villa fans, their team have gone the opposite way. In Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Jackson, Villa have serious pace, skill and unpredictability in attack and they can trouble many teams in this European campaign.

Sports.title: Plenty to smile about, your highness! Prince William celebrates wildly as his beloved Aston Villa score SIX goals in Champions League clash against Fenerbahce
Sports.content:
Plenty to smile about, your highness! Prince William celebrates wildly as his beloved Aston Villa score SIX goals in Champions League clash against Fenerbahce

A delighted Prince William was seen celebrating in the stands as Aston Villa earned a dominant 6-0 victory in their Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

The Prince of Wales – who has supported Villa since his school days – was watching on as Unai Emery's side took on the Turkish giants in their second league phase match.

Prince William punched the air in delight as Aston Villa took an early lead through summer signing Johan Manzambi.

Aston Villa doubled the advantage on the half hour mark through Nicolas Jackson, with the forward adding a third before half-time.

The home side's dominance continued in the second half with Ross Barkley scoring twice, the first from the penalty spot, before Tammy Abraham added a last sixth.

The result saw Aston Villa continue their perfect start in the league phase of the Champions League, with Emery's side having won their opening two fixtures.

Prince William celebrated as Aston Villa made a superb start to the Champions League tie

Prince William watched on as Aston Villa raced into a 3-0 lead before half-time against Fenerbahce

The Prince of Wales continued his wild celebrations as Aston Villa score three in the second half

Aston Villa continued their perfect start to the Champions League by thrashing Fenerbahce

Prince William has been a regular presence at Villa Park in recent years and attended matches throughout their run to winning the Europa League last season.

He had joined players and staff following their triumph in the final in Istanbul back in May, after Emery's side claimed the club's first European trophy in 44 years.

Aston Villa's Europa League success saw the club qualify for their year's Champions League, where Prince William will be hoping for a similarly successful European run.

A die-hard Villa supporter since his school days, William once explained how he chose the club while studying in Berkshire, resisting the pull of more popular teams.

'A long time ago at school I got into football big time. I was looking around for clubs. All my friends were either Man United fans or Chelsea fans and I didn’t want to follow the run-of-the-mill teams,' he told the BBC in 2015.

'I wanted to have a team that was more mid-table that could give me more emotional rollercoaster moments.

'Aston Villa’s always had a great history. I have got friends of mine who support Aston Villa and one of the first FA Cup games I went to was Bolton v Aston Villa back in 2000. Sadly, Villa went on to lose to Chelsea (in the final),' he said

'It was fantastic, I sat with all the fans with my red beanie on, and I was with all the Brummie fans and had a great time.

'It was the atmosphere, the camaraderie and I really felt that there was something I could connect with.'

Sports.title: Mike Tyson admits he suffered near-fatal overdoses at lowest point of his crippling drug issues... and reveals unusual remedy that saved him
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson admits he suffered near-fatal overdoses at lowest point of his crippling drug issues... and reveals unusual remedy that saved him

Mike Tyson has claimed he was saved by a powerful psychedelic from the toxin of a toad after suffering near-fatal drug overdoses.

The legendary boxer, 60, opened up on the terrifying health scares in a new Netflix docuseries, TYSON.

The former heavyweight champion detailed how he nearly died after battling alcohol and drug addiction, claiming: 'When I think about a low point, I think about this — OD'ing. I'm bleeding out, my nose is bleeding and I'm hysterical. I'm sweating.

'I OD'd, I've done it plenty of times but this one was a little more extreme than others.'

But Tyson survived after a shaman gave him 5-MeO-DMT, a substance found in the secretion of the Bofu alvarius toad. Early studies suggest it could help treat anxiety and depression.

The boxer claimed he has used the psychedelic 'over 100 times' and it helped him come off cocaine and alcohol.

Mike Tyson has claimed he was saved by a powerful psychedelic from the toxin of a toad

The legendary boxer, 60, opened up on near-fatal drug overdoses in a new Netflix docuseries

A shaman gave him 5-MeO-DMT, a substance found in the secretion of the Bofu Alvarius toad

'At the time we had this friend, he knew a shaman who does this thing called 5-MeO-DMT, it comes from the Bufo alvarius toad,' his third wife, Lakiha 'Kiki' Spicer, explained.

'Whatever kind of addictions or things that you're going through, it helps level them in your mind.'

According to the UC Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics, 5-MeO-DMT - which is also known as 'Bufo' or 'God molecule' or 'The Toad' - is 'usually inhaled through vaporizing or snorting.'

The drug, which is illegal to use recreationally in the United States, 'induces feelings of awe, visual and auditory hallucinations, and other sensations' with effects 'starting just a few seconds after ingestion and lasting about twenty to thirty minutes.'

In the new series, the 60-year-old is filmed smoking the drug at a treatment center.

'It blew my mind. I’ve done it over 100 times,' Tyson claimed. 'Any time I have to make a big decision about anything, I take the toad. I haven’t used cocaine and drink since.'

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez reiterates 'anger and frustration' in follow-up to bombshell interview
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez reiterates 'anger and frustration' in follow-up to bombshell interview

Lisandro Martinez has come out with a fresh statement in the aftermath of his fiery interview, where the Manchester United defender took aim at senior figures over a lack of ambition

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez has attempted to explain his rant on Tuesday night

Lisandro Martinez's post-match rant on Tuesday has split the Manchester United squad with players divided as the defender released a fresh statement admitting he spoke in "anger and frustration" - but doubling down on his desire for more.

‌



‌



In the aftermath of another loss for the Red Devils, who went down 2-0 at Atletico Madrid, their Argentine defender let rip at the hierarchy, specifically director of football Jason Wilcox, regarding a lack of investment in the summer.

‌



Martinez was keen to make the point that, whilst the players and manager Michael Carrick need to take some responsibility of the run of poor results, he feels they have not been suitably equipped to fight on all fronts after an impressive period of results last season.

‌



United's return to Europe, coupled with the domestic competitions, was always going to place more onus on resources and Martinez said in a bombshell interview: "I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Tonight it is easy to [blame] the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Martinez came out late on Wednesday night and put out some words on his social media account, explaining his comments and his reaction.

He admits he "spoke out in anger and frustration" but added: "When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

‌



"I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment."

View 2 Images Man Utd's players have been divided over whether to back Lisandro Martinez

The Sun reports that some players have appreciated Martinez's willingness to be so honest, with his comments ultimately him defending his manager, who is under mounting pressure.

‌



Other teammates have been reluctant to side with the defender however. One senior player feels Martinez’s comments changed the coverage of United’s loss to Atletico with many feeling as if they played well despire the loss. Another believes the absence of certain teammates has affected the harmony in the squad.

It was well documented that United did miss out on a host of targets in the summer. Several of those, including the likes of Elliot Anderson, were players they chose not to pursue due to their sky high valuations.

Midfield was ultimately the only area that was strengthened with no forwards or defenders coming in, which already looks a poor move with Carrick having to work with a backline that has had no new arrivals for several summers.

Sports.title: Man City's shameless defiance lasts just 13 minutes as PSG dish out their own punishment
Sports.content:
Man City's shameless defiance lasts just 13 minutes as PSG dish out their own punishment

MANCHESTER CITY 2-4 PSG: The European champions produced a frightening first-half onslaught to put City to the sword in front of former boss Pep Guardiola

View 3 Images PSG ran riot in the second half (Image: David Blunsden/Action Plus/Shutterstock)

Manchester City's shameless act of defiance lasted less than 13 minutes. That's all it took for Paris Saint-Germain to inflict their own punishment on rivals who could well have a lot more of the stuff to come.

‌



‌



Three goals before half-time from Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha helped Luis Enrique's men give City a good kicking when they're down.

‌



At least Pep Guardiola got to see a fireworks and laser show before kick off, as his former club attempted to pretend life was normal, despite being found guilty of industrial financial cheating.

‌



Guardiola returned to the scene of the crime, to lend his support to his former club in their hour of need. He probably wished he hadn't bothered.

The harsh truth appeared to be that he hadn't been missed since stepping down at the end of last season. Enzo Maresca had made the perfect start to succeeding the Spaniard, winning his first six games in charge.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

But making it seven at the expense of the best side in Europe was a different ball-game altogether. Quite literally, as PSG would go on to prove. PSG arrived in town as reigning, back-to-back Champions League holders.

A team which could afford to leave Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the bench. One hell-bent on making it a hat-trick of titles. Warren Zaire-Emery tested Gianluigi Donnarumma from long range, while Ruben Dias had to intervene with Dembele poised to strike.

‌



PSG had made an impressive start. But it became a stunning one when the French giants ripped City to pieces to score twice in as many minutes.

Doue finished off a quicksilver move covering the length of the pitch, by drilling a low shot into the bottom corner to make it 1-0 to the visitors inside 13 minutes. And before City could process what had happened, the deficit had been doubled.

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola watched on from the stands

‌



Doue turned provider this time, taking a cross from Dembele before returning the favour for Dembele to plant a header past Donnarumma from close range.

Erling Haaland tried to respond, but was snuffed out by a superb challenge from Willian Pacho. Haaland then wasted a headed chance as the nightmare continued.

Vitinha drew a sharp save from Donnarumma, while Achraf Hakimi hit the post, as PSG went in search of a third which arrived moments later thanks to Vitinha's clinical finish.

‌



It was the first time since 2015 City had conceded three first-half goals. It was also at times reminiscent of watching the same football that great Barcelona team used to produce under a certain Guardiola.

Enzo Fernandez's mistake almost gifted PSG a fourth. It was becoming embarrassing. Maresca made a triple change at the start of the second half.

View 3 Images Haaland scored twice for City after the break (Image: (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images))

‌



But it was Haaland who offered a glimmer of hope when he headed past Matvei Safonov to give City a lifeline. Maresca's men looked like a different team, with more passion and energy. Enzo Fernandez headed wide and PSG looked slightly rattled for a spell.

But when Donnarumma failed to keep out stinging strike from Akliouche just after the hour mark, the game was done and dusted.

Donnarumma appeared to have kept out the curling shot with a sublime save, but when the ball landed it spun back across the line, despite the scrambling efforts of the Italian.

Article continues below

All that was left was for Maresca's men to limit the damage - which Haaland helped them do with his second of the night. But it was all in vain. PSG could even afford to miss a late penalty.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland instantly breaks Enzo Maresca rule TWICE in Man City vs PSG thriller
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland instantly breaks Enzo Maresca rule TWICE in Man City vs PSG thriller

Enzo Maresca went against his own clear rules with a bold Erling Haaland Manchester City decision in their Champions League defeat to PSG

View 2 Images Manchester City star Erling Haaland broke Enzo Maresca's rules twice in the Champions League defeat to PSG (Image: (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images))

Erling Haaland broke a long-standing Enzo Maresca rule by celebrating his goals against Paris Saint-Germain while being Manchester City captain. The striker scored twice in the second half of his side's thrilling 4-2 defeat to Luis Enrique's charges, with PSG three goals in front at half-time.

‌



‌



Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha had all found the back of the net in a thrilling 19-minute spell at Etihad Stadium. Maresca subsequently rung the changes at half-time with club captain Ruben Dias among those replaced.

‌



That decision saw Haaland given the armband with the 26-year-old a surprising selection given Maresca's own thoughts on having his striker be the captain.

‌



"At Leicester and Chelsea, I had a rule that when we scored, the captain had to come to the bench for instructions and not celebrate," he admitted during the club's pre-season tour of Asia.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"But if he scores, then he can celebrate. If Erling is the captain, f------ hell -- we have a problem, can you imagine?" I think even if it is two or three minutes, there is always something to adjust.

"At the moment, we have three or four [captains] and we are missing one [Rodri is recovering from back surgery]. In the case of Rodri, see what happens."

The Spaniard would have been part of Maresca's leadership group with the exit of Bernardo Silva also requiring fresh considerations for captaincy. With Dias off the pitch, Haaland was seemingly the next choice but he had no plans to follow Maresca's rule.

‌



Rather than heading over to the touchline, he fist-bumped the air before having a brief conversation with Josko Gvardiol on his way back to the halfway line after a superb glancing header.

View 2 Images Erling Haaland was Manchester City captain for the second half of their Champions League clash against PSG (Image: Getty Images)

With City three goals down prior to his strike, Maresca's rule may not apply with the City boss walking slowly around his technical box, arms folded, as opposed to giving out instruction.

‌



In the immediate aftermath of his second goal - which came after PSG had restored their three-goal lead - Haaland simply ran back to the halfway line.

While not covered specifically, Maresca almost certainly meant that the rule largely applies when City score either first or to extend their advantage with the celebrations lasting longer than Haaland's two against PSG.

In addition to the 60,000 supporters treated to a superb clash, Pep Guardiola was also in attendance with the former City boss jetting in from Barcelona to show his support following the club's guilty verdict over 114 financial charges.

Article continues below

City have appealed against the outcome of the independent panel's findings and continue to insist they are innocent.
