World.title: PSG beat Manchester City 4-2 away in Champions League
World.content:
Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland (2R) misses with this header during the UEFA Champions League, league phase football match between Manchester City and Paris Saint Germain at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 14, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP)

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain staved off a second-half comeback to win 4-2 away to Manchester City in their Champions League showdown on Wednesday.

PSG were 3-0 up in the first half with goals by Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha, but Erling Haaland scored twice after the break for City. Maghnes Akliouche got PSG’s fourth before Ferran Torres had a late penalty saved.

World.title: 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu
World.content:
Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe.

Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday.

He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls.

Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance.

In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern.

In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership.

Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.”

He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies.

The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance.

“From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.”

Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear.

“The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued.

According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular.

“He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.”

Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.”

He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term.

World.title: Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists
World.content:
Tinubu

By Dickson Omobola

National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Felix Muoka, has insisted that Nigeria and Nigerians are better off than ever before, saying the party will win the 2027 presidential election based on its positive records.

Muoka said the APC was working hard to secure voters’ support, adding that the party would not take Nigerians’ votes for granted.

Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Thursday, he said the party’s preparations and campaign efforts were aimed at securing as many votes as possible in the next general elections.

He said: “Qualitatively speaking, our country is better. Nigerians are better today than they have ever been. Is there a country that has transited from this depressed economy, like we have had for decades, to that level of prosperity that didn’t go through these stages?

“Nigerians also understand that. So what the president has done is to give this country a fighting chance, not just at recovery, but at building the prospects for sustainable prosperity.”

On the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, he said: “What you saw today and what we’ve been up to is really taking ourselves seriously. If we thought this was all said and done, we wouldn’t put in this level of energy and work in an effort to really get to the last vote within the electorate. We are not taking this for granted. We’re taking it very seriously. I’m sure that if our party was docile and we were doing nothing to campaign or put out our information, you would also bring me here to say that we had been very docile. We’re a political party.

“We are a party for a reason. We are in this to compete with other political parties and to win the support of Nigerians. Since 2023, there’s a reason that our party has been very successful. Since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically all elections in which we have contested. There’s a reason for that. It’s because we prepare. We do our homework.

“Nigerians bought in and voted for our party massively in 2023. We won that election, even though there are elements who want to claim that they won without evidence. But we won that election without question. As I said a few minutes ago, in every other

election that has been called since then, Nigerians voted, not Indians. Nigerians voted in all the other elections since 2023. We won by upwards of 90 per cent.

“Let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. Already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election in which the APC is governing, not just at the centre, but in so many states in our country.”

On the APC’s chances in 2027, he said: “We will win the election. We are working hard to win the election. I think that Nigerians are going to stand tall, shoulder to shoulder with the APC to win the next election.”

World.title: FG fixes August 2027 deadline for WAEC, NECO results
World.content:
By Joseph Erunke

The Federal Government has proposed a new examination timetable that will see candidates sitting the 2027 West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO) and other major external examinations receive their results by August, ahead of the September admission process into tertiary institutions.

Under the proposed schedule, the government is seeking to end delays in the release of examination results that could disrupt candidates’ transition from secondary schools to universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.

A statement on Wednesday night by the Director, Press and Public Relations of the Federal Ministry of Education, Boriowo Folasade, said the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, disclosed the plan during a meeting with heads and representatives of examination bodies at the Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja.

“The meeting focused on harmonising examination schedules, preventing clashes among major examinations and ensuring that results are processed and released within agreed timelines, “the statement said.

According to the proposed timetable, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) will conduct the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) from March 15 to 25, with results expected in the same month.

NECO’s Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) is scheduled to hold from April 1 to May 14, while WAEC’s West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) will run from May 11 to June 18.

Both NECO and WAEC are expected to release their results in August 2027.

The National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examination is proposed for June 1 to July 5, while the National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS) examination will hold from June 10 to July 9. Results from both examinations are also expected in August.

The proposed schedule places the examination bodies under pressure to complete their respective processes in time to meet the government’s August results-release target.

The Federal Ministry of Education said the initiative was part of the education reform agenda of the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, under the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), which seeks to improve efficiency, coordination and educational outcomes.

It added that engagement with examination bodies would continue to ensure compliance with the proposed timelines, strengthen accountability and align the release of results with tertiary admission schedules.

The government, under President Bola Tinubu, said it remained committed to reforms that would improve the efficiency of the education system and expand timely access to tertiary education.

However, the timetable remains proposed, with the success of the plan depending on effective coordination among the

examination bodies and their ability to meet the agreed deadlines.

If implemented as planned, the initiative could give candidates and their parents greater certainty over the transition from secondary school examinations to tertiary admissions, while reducing disruptions caused by late results.

World.title: Transcorp Group Advocates Investment in Girls’ Rights
World.content:
Transnational Corporation Plc, through its power subsidiaries, Transcorp Power Plc, Ughelli, and Transafam Power Limited, Afam, hosted girls from Transcorp Power School, Ughelli, and Transafam Power Schools, Afam, to advocate for investment in girls’ rights as the world commemorates the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child. In line with this year’s theme,

“End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights”, the session linked girls’ rights to education, confidence, ambition, leadership, and opportunity. Around the world, about one in five girls is married before her 18th birthday. West and Central Africa is described as the global centre of child marriage, with nearly 60 million women and girls in the region married as children, and Nigeria accounts for the largest share. An earlier United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) estimate put the country’s number of child brides at about 22 million. For each of these girls, early marriage too often means an end to schooling, risky early pregnancy, and a future decided by others. Speaking during the session, President/Group Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Group,

Owen D. Omogiafo, OON, told the girls that there is no limit to what they can achieve. Drawing on her own journey, she shared that she was not born with a silver spoon but rose to lead one of Africa’s foremost business groups through tenacity, focus and determination. “You are not too young to have a voice, and you are not too young to have a dream. Nobody should decide your future for you. You have a right to choose your own path, so start painting the portrait of where you want to be in the future; and then work hard to get there.”

World.title: NSCIA Felicitates CAN at 50, Says Milestone Important for Nigeria
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), led by its President-General and Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar has felicitated the leadership of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and the entire Christian community in Nigeria on the occasion of the Association’s 50th anniversary.

In a statement y by its Secretary-General, Prof. Is-haq Oloyede, NSCIA said it regarded the 50th anniversary of CAN as a significant milestone not only for the Christian community but also for the Nigerian nation.

The Council noted that while the nation had

transited through various challenges and difficult moments, religious leaders and institutions had continued to play crucial role in promoting peace, dialogue, mutual understanding and peaceful coexistence among the diverse peoples and faith communities of the country.

The NSCIA maintained that it recognised the importance of the relationship between Muslims and Christians in Nigeria,

noting that the two communities constituted the overwhelming majority of the Nigerian population and shared a common responsibility to promote peace, entrench justice, advance security, contribute to responsible citizenship and the development of the country.

“The challenges confronting our nation, particularly injustice, insecurity, poverty, unemployment, social inequality and the need for accountable and responsive governance, require the collective efforts of all Nigerians.

“It is in this regard that the NSCIA attaches great importance to sustained inter-faith dialogue and cooperation. The Council particularly appreciates the platforms that have enabled leaders of the two faith communities to engage constructively on issues affecting the peace, unity and development of Nigeria, including the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council (NIREC),” NSCIA said.

It described the 50th anniversary of CAN as an opportunity to reflect on the responsibility of religious leadership in strengthening national unity and promoting peaceful coexistence.

The Council stressed that it believed that religious differences should never be allowed to become sources of division, hatred or violence, noting that respective faiths should continue to inspire the nation towards justice, compassion, peaceful coexistence and service to humanity.

NSCIA congratulated the President of CAN, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the National Executive Committee (NEC), the various Christian denominations and associations under its umbrella as well as Christians across the 36 states of the federation and the FCT on the

golden milestone and wished the association greater wisdom in the discharge of its onerous national and sacred responsibilities.

World.title: Nigeria’s Sacrifices for Peace in Sierra Leone Will Never Be Forgotten, Says Former VP
World.content:
*Calls for Africa’s Economic Independence

Linus Aleke in Abuja

Former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Samuel Sam-Sumana, has expressed profound gratitude to Nigeria for its sacrifices in restoring peace to his country, saying the contributions of Nigerian troops will remain indelible in Sierra Leone’s history.

The former Vice-President also called for Africa’s economic independence to discourage young people from migrating to Europe and America in search of better opportunities and living conditions, often at the risk of their lives, owing to a lack of opportunities at home.

Sam-Sumana made these remarks when the leadership of the Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja.

He said Nigeria had played a pivotal role in supporting Sierra Leone during its conflict by providing troops and other forms of assistance that helped restore peace and stability.

He acknowledged that military personnel and civilians had paid the ultimate price in the struggle, stressing the need to ensure that their sacrifices were never forgotten.

“As a Sierra Leonean, I wish to express my profound gratitude for the role Nigeria and other countries played in helping Sierra Leone regain peace and stability,” he said.

The former Vice-President described Nigeria as a big brother in West Africa, stressing that the country’s stability and prosperity had far-reaching implications for the subregion.

“When Nigeria catches a cold, the rest of us sneeze,” he said, underscoring the interconnectedness of West African countries.

Sam-Sumana also urged DECAN to sustain its engagement with the military and strengthen professional cooperation between defence correspondents and security institutions.

He described journalists as indispensable partners in governance, accountability and national development, warning against the tendency of political leaders to regard critical reporting as an act of hostility.

“Constructive criticism is essential to improving public institutions and ensuring that those entrusted with public responsibilities remain accountable,” he said.

According to him, public officials should not fear criticism when it is fair, accurate and intended to promote the greater public good.

Reflecting on Sierra Leone’s civil war, Sam-Sumana said the conflict, influenced by the spillover of the war in neighbouring Liberia and competing interests in diamond resources, had resulted in enormous losses of lives and property.

He said the painful experience should strengthen collective efforts to prevent the recurrence of violent conflicts across West Africa.

“We must never forget those experiences. Rather, we should use them to strengthen our collective commitment to peace and prevent similar tragedies in the subregion,” he said.

Sam-Sumana further cautioned political leaders against allowing personal ambition to undermine national stability, insisting that peaceful political competition remained essential to democratic development.

He said peace was a collective victory that transcended political parties and individual ambitions.

On Africa’s development, the former Vice-President called for a fundamental shift from dependence on foreign assistance towards mutually beneficial partnerships, industrialisation and greater economic self-reliance.

He argued that African countries must move beyond exporting raw materials and importing finished products by investing in local industries, adding value to natural resources and creating employment opportunities for young people.

Sam-Sumana said the continent’s inability to harness its vast resources fully had contributed to economic hardship and forced migration, including dangerous journeys across the Mediterranean Sea.

In his remarks, DECAN President, Mr Odita Sunday, said the courtesy visit was intended to express the association’s appreciation to Sam-Sumana for accepting its invitation and participating in the DECAN Conference and Awards 2026.

World.title: APDC MD Explains How FCT Residents Can Access Homes Through Mortgages
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Acting Managing Director of Abuja Property Development Company (APDC) Akeem Aderogba has shed light on how residents of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), particularly civil servants and low- and middle-income earners, can benefit from mortgage facilities to acquire homes without paying the full cost upfront.

He made the clarification Wednesday at the 20th anniversary symposium of APDC held in Abuja

Aderogba said the mortgage arrangement allowed prospective homeowners to pay an initial deposit of between 10 and 20 per cent of the cost of a house, while the outstanding balance is financed through mortgage institutions, making homeownership more accessible to residents.

Speaking on APDC’s efforts to address the housing deficit in the FCT, he said the initiative was designed to ease the financial burden on prospective homeowners who might not have the resources to pay for a house in a single transaction.

He explained that through mortgage financing, beneficiaries could secure their homes after paying the required deposit, with the balance spread over an agreed repayment period.

“For us, we take these issues into consideration before arriving at the prices of our houses. You do not need to look for all the money before you can move in. You can deposit maybe 10 to 20 per cent, and the balance will be financed by the mortgage institutions,” he said.

He disclosed that APDC had also collaborated with the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria through the National Housing Fund (NHF) to provide civil servants with access to affordable housing.

According to him, the arrangement, alongside support from the Federal Government Housing Board, enables eligible civil servants to access homes by facilitating payment of the outstanding balance to APDC.

He said the initiative was particularly beneficial to civil servants, who could otherwise find it difficult to raise the full cost of acquiring a house amid rising construction costs and inflation.

The acting MD noted that APDC had continued to expand its housing developments to help bridge the housing deficit in the FCT, adding that its estates were designed to serve different categories of residents, including low- and middle-income earners.

He disclosed that the organisation’s estates covered about 50 hectares of land, with more than 800 families moving into the development, while additional projects were expected to accommodate hundreds of other households.

Among the projects, he said, were Abuja APDC Homes in Karsana, expected to accommodate at least 200 families, and another development at APDC Homes, Ido Gwari, in Life Camp, projected to provide housing for at least 150 households.

He, however, identified the rising cost of building materials and infrastructure as major challenges affecting housing affordability and the timely completion of some developments.

He explained that the increasing prices of cement, sand and other construction materials, alongside the rising cost of infrastructure, had significantly increased the cost of housing development.

He urged the government to support housing developers by providing land and essential infrastructure, noting that infrastructure accounts for between 30 and 40 per cent of the total cost of housing development.

According to him, government intervention in infrastructure provision would reduce development costs and enable developers to offer homes at more affordable prices, particularly to civil servants and other residents of the FCT.

In her remarks the Group Managing Director Abuja Investments Company Limited (AICL) Amb. Maureen Tamuno, said APDC had operated for the past two decades as a subsidiary of AICL.

She said that APDC’s role of expanding housing opportunities remains critical because a house is the most important investment of a lifetime for ordinary citizens and households.

World.title: Falana Urges States to Utilise N267bn UBEC Funds for Basic Education
World.content:
Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana (SAN), has called on governors of the 36 states and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to utilise N267 billion in released intervention funds for basic education and access over N65 billion in counterpart funding yet to be accessed by states.

Falana, who is the Chair of the Alliance on Surviving Covid 19 and Beyond (ASCAB), made the call in a statement titled “Abandonment of Primary School Education for the Children of the Poor.”

He said the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) revealed that as of August this year, about N267 billion in released intervention funds was yet to be utilised, while over N65 billion counterpart funding was yet to be accessed by states.

The Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr. Aisha Garba, made the disclosure at the opening of a month-long technical capacity-building workshop organised by the World Bank-assisted HOPE-GOV Programme in Abuja.

The workshop is aimed at strengthening budget planning and execution for basic education and primary healthcare in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Falana recalled that on November 28, 2025, the Federal High Court ruled in the case of Femi Falana & Anor v Attorney-General of the Federation & 36 Ors (Suit No. FHC/L/CS/142/24) that the Federal Government, all 36 state governments and the FCT have a binding legal obligation to provide free, compulsory and universal basic education for every Nigerian child of primary and junior secondary school age.

“In spite of the clear terms of the above judgment,” he said, the funds meant for basic education remained unutilised or unaccessed.

“As a matter of urgency, the governors of the 36 states and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory should utilise the N267 billion in released intervention funds and access the over N65 billion counterpart funding in the UBEC Account,” he said.

Falana urged the authorities to “perform their statutory duties and respect the right of every Nigerian child to free and compulsory basic education from primary school to junior secondary school guaranteed by the Free, Compulsory Universal Basic Education Act.”

He also called on the Federal Government to provide a meal for schoolchildren per day to boost enrolment and nutrition in line with the National Social Investment Programme Agency Act.

“In view of the ongoing political campaigns, we call on the mass media to challenge all registered political parties and their candidates to bring out their programmes with respect to the implementation of the relevant laws on free and compulsory basic education for every child in Nigeria as well as the school feeding programme,” he said.

Falana added that, “Having regard to the enormous resources of the country, the removal of children of school age from the streets in all states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory must be carried out without any further delay.”

World.title: Makinde Demands Audit of N15trn Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has demanded a comprehensive audit of the N15 trillion Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project, accusing the Federal Government of raising fresh questions about its planning, procurement and cost following the recent realignment of the route.

It further said Nigerians deserved to know why the route was changed, how much had been spent and whether the Federal Government would reduce the contract sum, warning that the controversy had deepened concerns over accountability in the handling of public funds.

Briefing newsmen, APM Director-General, Felix Hassan Hyat, also urged Nigerians to reject President Bola Tinubu in 2027 and support Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement, APM.

Hyat faulted the explanation by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, that climate change and environmental challenges necessitated the realignment, arguing that the development raised questions about whether adequate technical and environmental assessments had been conducted before the project was awarded.

“The vague reasons of climate change and environmental challenges adduced by Minister Umahi at this point, beg the question,” Hyat said.

The organisation also alleged that the contract was awarded in 2024 without an approved engineering design, an open and competitive bidding process or budgetary provision and statutory appropriation by the National Assembly.

It further questioned the relationship between the contractor’s corporate group and another firm whose board allegedly includes individuals linked to the Presidency, raising concerns about possible conflicts of interest.

The group also alleged that the project was designed as a conduit for financing the All Progressives Congress’ election expenses. The statement provided no supporting evidence for the allegation.

Demanding full disclosure, the organisation called for the publication of procurement and payment records, an independent engineering assessment of the Ondo realignment and a comprehensive audit of the project’s total cost, expenditure to date and execution plan.

“We demand that the President Tinubu-led government should publish the relevant engineering assessment, alternative-route analysis, accompanying cost implications and comprehensive audit of the work and amount so far spent,” the organisation said.

It maintained that it was not opposed to road construction but questioned the priority given to the coastal highway while several existing federal roads remained in poor condition.

“Nigeria is in dire need of infrastructure, no doubt, but not opaque contracts and expensive excuses!” Hyat declared.

The organisation urged Nigerians to vote against the President in 2027 and rally behind Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda.

It described Makinde as an alternative capable of building consensus across party and regional divides, insisting that the country’s future should take precedence over the President’s political ambition.

“The future of Nigeria must take precedence over President Tinubu’s personal ambition,” Hyat said.

World.title: FG Launches D30 Platform to Unlock Nigeria’s Creative Economy Potential
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The federal government has taken a bold step towards unlocking the economic potential of the creative and tourism industries by launching the D30 Platform (Destination 2030) to strengthen access to sectoral data, research, mapping and economic intelligence.

Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy Hannatu Musa Musawa, said the platform will provide a more structured understanding of Nigeria’s creative and tourism assets, helping government institutions, investors and entrepreneurs identify opportunities, address industry challenges and make better-informed decisions.

She emphasized that the launch of D30 aligned with the ministry’s broader strategic ambition to generate more than three million jobs and contribute $100 billion to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product by 2030.

According to her, achieving these targets would require sustained investment, effective policies, improved infrastructure and stronger collaboration between government and private-sector stakeholders.

She stressed the need to move beyond recognising the country’s creative potential to systematically measuring, understanding and developing its economic value.

The minister enunciated several challenges facing the sectors, including the absence of sufficiently reliable, accessible and comprehensive data to establish the scale of opportunities available, identify infrastructure gaps and guide investment decisions.

She explained that the D30 Platform is designed to help address this challenge by bringing relevant information together to support more coordinated planning and economic development.

She said improved access to such intelligence could also contribute to a more transparent and predictable investment environment, encouraging greater private-sector participation in Nigeria’s creative and tourism economy.

The minister highlighted the importance of participation by government agencies, the National Bureau of Statistics, state governments, industry associations, private-sector operators and research institutions.

She stated that through collaboration, the platform could help reduce information gaps, improve the quality of sectoral intelligence and support more coordinated policy decisions.

Musawa acknowledged its technology development partner, Cavista Holdings, led by its Vice President, Olumide Olayomi for its role in developing the platform and project team who contributed to bringing the initiative to launch.

In his remarks, Olayomi said Cavista committed private funding and technical expertise to build D30 in partnership with the ministry.

“We saw an opportunity to contribute to an important national priority by providing an essential digital foundation for the sector’s development. D30 brings together information on creative and cultural industries, tourism infrastructure and sector intervention,” he said.

World.title: G27 Questions Mbah’s 2023, 2027 INEC Credentials, Defends Nnaji
World.content:
The G27 for Uche Nnaji support group has questioned the alleged decision of Governor Peter Mbah to submit a Senior School Certificate Examination (WAEC) certificate as his highest educational qualification to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The group made its position known in a statement signed by its spokesman, Chief James Ogbodo, in reaction to a publication questioning why Chief Uche Nnaji submitted his WAEC certificate as his highest qualification to INEC.

Chief Uche Nnaji is the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State for the 2027 election. His name is also among the candidates contained in the final list recently published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the Enugu State governorship election.

G27 described the publication as an attempt to shift attention from questions surrounding the qualifications Governor Mbah submitted to INEC during the 2023 general election.

According to the group, the governor should first address questions concerning the consistency of the qualifications he presented to INEC before questioning another candidate’s choice of credentials.

The group alleged that during the 2023 election, Mbah reportedly presented a Law degree as his highest qualification, alongside an NYSC discharge certificate. It further recalled the controversy that subsequently surrounded the authenticity of the NYSC document, noting that the matter has been disputed by relevant parties.

G27 therefore questioned why the governor chose to present WAEC as his highest qualification for the 2027 election rather than retain the same academic qualification he presented to INEC in 2023.

The group said the change had raised questions that, in its view, required clarification from the governor and the relevant institutions.

“Before asking Chief Uche Nnaji why he chose to submit his WAEC certificate, Governor Peter Mbah should explain why the qualification he presented to INEC in 2023 is different from the qualification he is presenting in 2027,” the group said.

G27 further argued that the controversy surrounding the NYSC document remains an issue that should be addressed through appropriate legal and institutional channels. It alleged that the matter was compounded by an oath concerning the disputed certificate, adding that the governor should clarify the circumstances surrounding the document and the declarations made concerning it.

The group stressed that its position was not intended to prevent scrutiny of any political candidate, saying that all public officials and candidates should be prepared to answer legitimate questions about credentials submitted to electoral authorities.

The group also responded to comments attributed to Mr. Daniel, who reportedly questioned Nnaji’s academic credentials while presenting himself as a first-class journalism graduate.

G27 said academic distinction should ordinarily be reflected in the quality of journalism produced by its holder, arguing that responsible journalism requires independent verification rather than hurried reproduction of allegations.

“A first-class degree should ordinarily produce first-class journalism; not a hurried copy-and-paste report built on recycled claims,” the group said.

It urged journalists and media organisations to independently verify allegations concerning candidates, particularly when such allegations involve academic records, court proceedings and official documents.

According to G27, Nnaji contested the 2023 election with the same basic academic credential he is presenting for the 2027 election.

The group said Nnaji’s reliance on his WAEC certificate should not, in itself, be treated as evidence of wrongdoing, noting that WAEC remains a recognised qualification.

G27 also dismissed suggestions that Nnaji’s interest in the governorship was primarily motivated by the desire to obtain constitutional immunity.

The group described the allegation as unfounded, maintaining that Nnaji’s stated political objective was to address what it described as economic hardship, taxation concerns, unemployment and inadequate industrial development in Enugu State.

It said Nnaji’s agenda was focused on rebuilding the state’s economy, attracting investment, promoting industrialisation and creating employment opportunities, particularly for young people.

The group said these policy questions should form part of the substantive debate ahead of the 2027 election rather than allowing political discourse to be dominated by personal attacks and disputed credential controversies.

G27 also took exception to what it described as a misrepresentation of Nnaji’s court action concerning his academic records.

According to the group, Nnaji did not admit that he had never received his university degree certificate, as allegedly suggested in the publication.

Rather, the group maintained that the substance of the complaint concerned the university’s failure to release his academic transcript.

G27 said the distinction was fundamental because a degree certificate and an academic transcript are separate academic records serving different purposes.

It therefore urged journalists reporting on the matter to obtain and examine the actual court processes before drawing conclusions about what Nnaji did or did not admit.

“A journalist has a duty to verify such a fundamental distinction before rushing to publication,” the group said.

The group maintained that Nnaji’s decision to seek judicial clarification was motivated by his desire to protect his reputation and establish the facts surrounding his academic records.

According to G27, “a good name is a legacy that belongs not only to a man but also to his children and generations yet unborn.”

The support group called for a fact-based political debate ahead of the 2027 elections, saying that candidates should be judged on their records, policies, qualifications and capacity to govern rather than through unverified allegations or personal attacks.

Rachel Kolisi watched the Stormers match, and her ex Siya Kolisi, over the weekend. Images via IG

RACHEL KOLISI SUPPORTS SIYA’S STORMERS HOMECOMING

World.title: Angelique Gerber to DIVORCE ex-Bok Jacques Potgieter
World.content:
Angelique Gerber will reportedly proceed with her divorce to former Springbok, Jacques Potgieter, four years after their marriage separation.

This comes as the ex 7de Laan actress reportedly had a brief reconciliation with her ex, who is the father of her three children.

During the time apart, Jacques had a relationship with another woman, whom he recently split from.



ANGELIQUE GERBER TO DIVORCE EX JACQUES POTGIETER

According to reports, Angelique Gerber is proceeding with her divorce from Jacques Potgieter after allegedly giving him a second chance.

Sadly, their recent reconciliation was short-lived, with Angelique’s lawyer confirming that the second split was in the best interests of their three children.

The actress and influencer reportedly had enough of Jacques’s lifestyle and is now ready to close the chapter.



The news that Jacques and Angelique are still legally married, despite their messy relationship split, came as a surprise to many followers.

On her social media platforms, Jacques had liked comments urging the couple to rekindle their romance. When one follower commented, “You know you two can marry again”, Jacques responded, “We were never divorced”.

TIMELINE OF MESSY MARRIAGE SPLIT

Take a look at this relationship timeline between Angelique Gerber and Jacques Potgieter…



2014: Angelique and Jacques begin dating. At the time, the red-haired actress appeared as the character “Clara” on SABC 2 soapie, 7de Laan, which her rugby player boyfriend played for both the Waratahs and the Munakata Sanix Blues

2016: Angelique and Jacqued married at a Durbanville estate.

2016-2018: The couple would welcome their three children.



2021: Jacques Potgieter denies posting several Instagram Stories confessing to cheating on his wife, Angelique. He claims his account was “hacked”. On her IG, Angelique posted the cryptic message “The truth always comes out”. The couple again deny posting the messages. They claim they are happier and more in love than ever.

2022: The couple appeared in public separately and deleted all images of themselves together. Jacques goes public with a woman named Lizane “Lalla” Wagner.

2023: Angelique Gerber puts Jacques Potgieter on blast over a dispute over financial support for their children. She also expressed her annoyance at his posts praising his girlfriend as a stepmother.



June 2026: Jacques and Lizane Wagner split after their four-year relationship. Lizane denied allegations that she had been responsible for the breakdown of Jacques’s marriage.

July – September 2026: Jacques and Angelique appear to rekindle their romance. Jacques likes comments from the public encouraging the couple to give their marriage a “second chance”

October 2026: Jacques deletes all of his new images with Angelique, who also allegedly accuses him of “betraying” his family in various cryptic IG reposts.

World.title: ‘The R2 400 is just an insult’: Pensioner speaks out on SASSA grant
World.content:
A pensioner in Limpopo who receives the Older Person’s Grant says his monthly SASSA payment does not cover his household’s basic needs.

The grant recipient, who asked not to be named in this article, has received the grant for three years. He lives in a shared family home where three to five people depend on his income, and he uses his grant for a mix of essential expenses.

Despite this, he regularly struggles to make ends meet. He runs out of money before the month ends.



SASSA grant falls short for pensioner

The pensioner said the cost of living and rising food prices are his biggest financial concern. When asked what he would change about SASSA, he chose an increase in the grant amount.

“SASSA must stop harassing and stopping us when we try to find other income streams because the R2 400 is just an insult, period,” he said.

The Older Person’s Grant increased by R80 to R2 400 per month in April 2026, following Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s Budget Speech.

The grant recipient has experience in administrative and office work. He is currently unemployed and not looking for work.

Payment problems and poor communication

The pensioner said he has experienced a late or missing grant payment. He rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very poor.

He receives his grant through a bank deposit. He has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available.

World.title: ‘A star is needed here in Naturena’: Moloisane on Kaizer Chiefs’ trophy target
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Thabo Moloisane has set his sights on winning trophies and helping Amakhosi end their long wait for league glory following his arrival at Naturena in July.

The 26-year-old was one of five new signings brought in ahead of the season and has already featured in the majority of the club’s matches.

Speaking ahead of Chiefs’ clash against Stellenbosch FC on Tuesday, Moloisane made it clear that winning silverware is a major priority in his first season with the Soweto giants.



The defender believes Amakhosi have an opportunity to challenge for the league title and is determined to play his part in ending the club’s lengthy wait for another Premiership crown.

“A star, guys, it is needed here at home. We have an opportunity to see if we can do it this season, and the league, of course. It is one thing that has gone past us for a long time and, for me, in my first season, I just want to get as many trophies as I can. That’s where the ambition is, and the rest can follow,” he said.

Kaizer Chiefs last won the league title in the 2014/15 season, and Moloisane is eager to help restore the club’s status as one of South African football’s leading forces.



Beyond his ambitions at club level, the defender is also hoping to work his way back into the Bafana Bafana setup.

Kaizer Chiefs star wants Bafana return

Moloisane acknowledged that returning to the national team will not be easy, given the competition for places, but believes hard work and consistent performances at a high-profile club like Kaizer Chiefs could improve his chances.

“We should give credit to the guys, you know. I was speaking to Mdu (Shabalala) last week, saying the line is long to get back into Bafana, but at the same time, I’m at a big institution watched by everyone. For me, it’s just to continue working hard. The journey is still long,” he told media.



For Moloisane, the immediate focus remains on delivering for Amakhosi and helping the club compete for honours, while keeping his hopes of a Bafana Bafana recall alive.

Will he win a star?

World.title: ‘Spirit of lust’: Bernard Parker hints at struggles?
World.content:
Bernard Parker has reposted several telling Instagram posts, hinting at infidelity, lust and a “miserable marriage”. This comes as the former Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player – now coach of TS Galaxy – announced his split from his baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, in a social media post.

The 40-year-old has not disclosed when or why he separated from his wife, Wendy Parker, whom he married in 2012.

BERNARD PARKER’S CRYPTIC REPOSTS

On his Instagram account, Bernard Parker has reposted several telling faith-based Reels about men who seemingly struggle with monogamy.



One was about “the spirit of lust” and featured a preacher warning Christians about “sex with demons”. Others were warnings about lust and “staying away from bad women”

Another was a segment of a message from a preacher, which was titled: “What to do when your marriage is miserable”. A different message featured another preacher calling on individuals to ask their families and partners for forgiveness after “destroying” a marriage.

‘PERSONAL ADDICTIONS’

In his statement posted on Monday, 12 October, Bernard Parker alluded to being unfaithful to his former partner, Kacha Stepanovic, who is allegedly the mother of his baby daughter.



He shared: “I want to be honest about my part in our journey. I have made mistakes and struggled with personal addictions that have affected my life and the people I love.

“Kacha, I’m truly sorry for the times I hurt you, let you down, and caused you pain. You gave me love, support, patience and kindness that I’ve never received before. I take responsibility for my mistakes, knowing that some things cannot simply be undone with an apology”

On her social media account, Kacha Stepanovic reposted Bernard Parker’s statement.



She also hinted at his alleged infidelity.

She shared on her IG Stories: “Lust and addiction will strip you of your family, your work, your name and everything you built.

“If betrayal was so easy, the devil would be next seated at the throne. Make sure whatever you do is worth losing it all”.

World.title: South Africa will host race by 2029 - McKenzie
World.content:
PRETORIA - Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie insists South Africa did not miss out on hosting Formula 1.

Despite Rwanda getting the rights to host the African Grand Prix in the 2030s, McKenzie remains upbeat that the country is still on track to host the event in the near future.

He was addressing the media in Pretoria on Wednesday.

World.title: State claims Sibiya's lawyers interfered with witnesses
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The legal team for former Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya has wrapped up its bail argument.



Sibiya's lawyer, Estelle Killian, has argued that he is not a flight risk or a threat to witnesses, emphasising that they have not interfered with the complainants.



She urged the court to grant Sibiya bail because his health was at risk.



The State has opposed bail for Sibiya, accusing his defence team of attempting to secure a statement from a witness.



Prosecutors argued that this alleged interference provides plausible grounds for the court to deny his release.



eNCA reporter Pule Letshwiti-Jones has more details in the video above.

World.title: AKA's photographer testifies at murder trial
World.content:
DURBAN - The murder trial of rapper AKA and his friend, Tebello 'Tibz' Motsoane, has been adjourned until Thursday in the Durban High Court.



Four witnesses testified on Tuesday, including AKA’s manager and a DJ who was with them on the night of the murders.



On Wednesday, AKA’s photographer Thotloetso Mogotsi took the stand.



eNCA senior reporter Dasen Thathiah was at court and filed this report in the video above.

World.title: Three CIT robbery suspects shot and killed in KZN
World.content:
UMLAZI - Three suspected cash-in-transit robbers have been killed in a shootout with police and private security in Umlazi, KZN.

Initially, police had reported that four suspects were shot and killed, however, this number has since been revised to three by KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda.

Netshiunda said a manhunt for other suspects involved in this alleged robbery has been launched.

"We know with experience that there are getaway vehicles and there are those who were not at the crime scene. So, we don't know how many of them were at the crime scene, but a manhunt is on for those that we saw, which we are pursuing now," Netshiunda said.

He said four firearms were found at the scene and in one abandoned vehicle, officials found cash believed to be that which was stolen.

Stay informed in just a few minutes with ⁠News Bite⁠, your fast, reliable update on South Africa’s top stories.

⁠Mike Shingange⁠ has been elected ⁠COSATU president⁠, defeating Mabutho Cele by 973 votes to 836. Susan Khumalo is the federation's first deputy president. The vote followed a disrupted congress and continuing leadership disputes.

⁠Four people⁠ have died after seven were shot in ⁠Katlehong⁠, ⁠Ekurhuleni⁠. Two died at the scene and two later in hospital. Three remain in treatment, while a suspect has handed himself over to police. The motive remains under investigation.

⁠SASSA⁠ says it does not pay social grants to undocumented foreign nationals. ⁠Spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi ⁠says qualifying refugees may receive grants, rejecting misleading online claims about asylum seekers following a ⁠Constitutional Court⁠ ruling.

The murder case involving ⁠former boxing champion Zolani Tete⁠ has been postponed to 8 December for further investigation. A friend alleges Tete feared for his life before he was killed in ⁠Mdantsane⁠. The allegations have not been established by the court.

⁠Pope Leo XIV⁠ is recovering after an operation to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. The Vatican says the surgery was successful, with further tests under way.

A Saudi national has been arrested over an alleged hidden recording device at an OpenAI office in San Francisco. Authorities say there is no evidence that customer information was stolen; the recording allegations remain before the courts.

⁠Nobel Peace laureate Navi Pillay ⁠condemns US sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court, warning of the threat to international justice.

SPORT

⁠Formula One⁠ plans a return to Africa, with ⁠Rwanda ⁠expected to host a Grand Prix in the early 2030s, the first on the continent since 1993.

⁠Australia⁠ beat the Proteas by 214 runs in the opening Test in Durban. ⁠Captain Temba Bavuma⁠ points to soft dismissals as South Africa assesses the defeat.

The Bulls prepare to face Stade Français at Loftus in the Champions Cup, with Elrigh Louw anticipating a physical contest up front.

That's how we wrap today's ⁠News Bite⁠. For developments on these stories and more, keep an eye on ⁠eNCA.com ⁠and DStv Channel 403.

World.title: Government vows to protect political rights following Katlehong shooting
World.content:
EKURHULENI - The Justice Department and police are joining forces to protect South Africans' political rights ahead of the local government polls.

This is according to Deputy Justice Minister, Andries Nel.

His comments follow the Katlehong drive-by shooting in which four people have died and three others hospitalised.

The victims were returning from a political party member's memorial service when the shooting happened on Tuesday evening.

READ | Katlehong shooting death toll rises to four

Nel said everyone must be able to exercise their political rights, to campaign freely, openly and to go and cast their votes.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Is South Africa's Middle Class Paying Twice To Survive? Xhanti Payi | 14 October 2026
World.content:
The Hidden Cost Of Paying Privately For Public Services In South Africa

A household can afford to pay its taxes and still find itself buying essential services all over again. The wider consequences reach beyond family budgets.

A salary increase should, in theory, leave a household with more room to breathe. There might be money available to save, improve a home, take a holiday or invest in

a small business. But for many South Africans, additional income does not necessarily translate into greater financial freedom. It may simply create an opportunity to purchase privately what the public system has failed to provide reliably.

Consider the decisions facing a household that relies on a salary to meet its obligations. Parents may pay school fees because they believe a particular school offers their children better opportunities. A family might maintain medical cover for greater certainty about access to healthcare. Private security, backup electricity and dependable internet connectivity can all become regular expenses. These choices differ across households, and public provision is not uniformly inadequate. Yet the underlying question remains: how much income is left for building financial security once essential needs have been met?

This is the often-overlooked cost of unreliable public provision. Citizens contribute through taxation, but some also spend additional money securing alternatives. The result is not necessarily literal double billing for an identical service. It is a second layer of expenditure that can reduce disposable income and leave families more vulnerable when unexpected costs arise.

The issue becomes particularly revealing when transport is considered. A private vehicle is frequently discussed as a lifestyle purchase, but for some workers it is also a practical response to the limited availability, convenience or reliability of alternative transport. Owning a vehicle can offer independence, yet it comes with financing costs, fuel, maintenance and insurance. A household may therefore be spending heavily just to maintain reliable access to work.

Official statistics illustrate how significant transport already is. Statistics South Africa's Income and Expenditure Survey for 2022/23 found that transport accounted for 15.3% of household consumption expenditure, making it the third-largest spending category. The National Household Travel Survey of 2020 also recorded substantial dependence on minibus taxis and long journeys for many public-transport users. These surveys cover different periods, but together they show why transport deserves attention as an economic issue rather than merely a commuting problem.

There is a further complication: the middle class cannot be defined only by a salary band. Two people earning similar incomes may have very different levels of financial security. One could have manageable housing costs and relatively few dependants. The other might support an extended family, service debt and pay privately for several essential services. Their earnings may look similar on paper, while their ability to save or absorb an emergency differs considerably.

Economist Xhanti Payi raises this wider problem in a CheckPoint: The Podcast conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, describing the middle class as an economic shock absorber. It is a useful metaphor because the pressures do not stop with the individual household. When people devote more income to maintaining basic stability, they have less available for other purchases, investment and supporting new enterprises.

This does not mean that every private alternative is evidence of government failure. Families make choices based on preferences, geography, convenience and affordability. Nor does it mean that public services can be improved simply by increasing expenditure. Reliability, management, maintenance and accountability matter as much as budget allocations.

The practical question for policymakers is what improvements would produce the greatest financial relief for households. A reliable transport system could lower commuting expenses. Better-maintained infrastructure could reduce the need for

private backup services. More dependable public institutions could make some household expenditure a matter of genuine choice rather than perceived necessity.

For households, the measure of economic progress cannot be salary growth alone. It must also include how much of that salary remains available after the essential costs of everyday life have been paid. A stronger middle class is not simply one that earns more. It is one that needs to spend less of its income compensating for systems that ought to work.

References:

· CheckPoint: The Podcast, 14 October 2026. Nkepile Mabuse in conversation with economist and strategist Xhanti Payi. Episode transcript.

· Statistics South Africa. *Transport Month: Key Data and Sector Insights* (2025), drawing on the Income and Expenditure Survey 2022/23.

· Statistics South Africa. *National Household Travel Survey 2020*, published 4 March 2021.

World.title: ‘They will not be forgotten’ - Boxer reacts to 3 employees gunned down at Eshowe.
World.content:
ESHOWE - Discount retailer Boxer has confirmed the deadly shooting of three of its employees at its Eshowe store in KwaZulu-Natal.

In a statement, Boxer said the employees were murdered on 10 October in what it called a ‘horrific act of violence’.

“Today, Boxer teams across the country observed a moment of remembrance before beginning their shifts, standing together in honour of our fallen colleagues,” the statement read in part.

CCTV footage of the incident has since circulated widely on social media.

The footage appears to show a man dressed in black clothing speaking to three employees inside an office before pulling out a gun and opening fire.

READ | Discount retailer Boxer announces profits and a new CEO

The three employees tried to take cover, but the alleged gunman continued to fire shots.

Details surrounding the circumstances that led to the incident were not disclosed in the statement; however, the retailer confirmed they are communicating with police.

“We are working closely with the SAPS and relevant authorities, providing our full cooperation and assistance with the ongoing investigation.”

The store has offered its condolences to employees' families.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
