World.title: Cameroon Succession Rules: Who Takes Over If Biya Goes
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

A street in the Ngoa-Ekellé district of Yaoundé, the Cameroonian capital where a vacancy at the top would be settled, photographed in April 2018. (Photo: gtankam, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

EXPLAINER · CAMEROON

Key Facts — The country Cameroon is a Central African country with six neighbours, led by Paul Biya, now 93, since 6 November 1982.

— Why it matters Cameroon succession rules now hand the rest of the presidential term to an appointed vice president. The post has stood empty since April.

— Why now On Tuesday 13 October, opposition lawmaker Cabral Libii warned of “chaos” if Biya became permanently unable to serve before naming a vice president.

— What happened Parliament approved the amendment on Saturday 4 April by 200 votes to 18, with 4 abstentions. It was promulgated on Tuesday 14 April.

— The numbers If no vice president is in office, an election must follow between 20 and 120 days after the vacancy opens.

— What it means for you Washington rates Cameroon at Level 2 and warns that unrest can turn into political violence. A contested handover would test travel, aid and investment plans.

— Still open Who may ask the Constitutional Council to declare a vacancy while no vice president exists, and whether Biya will fill the post.

Cameroon succession rules changed in April, when parliament created an appointed vice president to finish the term if the presidency falls vacant. Six months later, President Paul Biya, 93, has not filled the post.

That gap leaves a country bordering Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic with disputed rules for its next handover. For US readers, it shapes travel risk, aid programmes and the outlook for investors in Central Africa.

How Cameroon Succession Rules Worked Before April

Until this year, a vacancy at the top triggered a caretaker period and then a fresh vote. The president of the Senate served as interim head of state until a new president was elected.

The amended text spells out tight limits on any interim leader. He may not change the constitution or the government, call a referendum, or stand in the election.

One narrow exception remains in the bill text quoted by the business daily EcoMatin. The interim president may change the government if the election requires it, after consulting the Constitutional Council.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Cameroon Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the April 2026 Amendment Changed

Parliament, meeting as a joint Congress of both chambers in Yaoundé, took up the bill on Thursday 2 April. It approved the text on Saturday 4 April by 200 votes to 18, with 4 abstentions.

Biya promulgated it on Tuesday 14 April as Law No. 2026/002, the news site Journal du Cameroun reported. According to EcoMatin, the reform rewrote Articles 5, 6, 7, 10, 53 and 66 of the constitution.

The core is the new Article 6, which covers death, resignation or permanent incapacity “duly established by the Constitutional Council.” In those cases, in our translation, “the Vice-President completes the President’s term.”

A vacancy therefore no longer leads automatically to an early election. The government’s explanatory memorandum said this avoids a vote whose cost to the state budget “is generally significant.”

Who the Vice President Is and Who Picks Them

The vice president is not elected but appointed by the president, like the prime minister and other ministers. The president sets the holder’s duties, may delegate powers and can end the appointment at any time.

The term cannot run beyond the president’s own seven-year mandate. The vice president faces the same incompatibilities as the head of state and must declare assets on entering and leaving office.

In normal times the post would deputise for the president, represent the country abroad and take on specific files. The memorandum calls this a “presidential tandem” meant to make government more efficient.

The reform met unease inside the Cameroon People’s Democratic Movement (RDPC), the ruling party that Biya leads. Senate dean René Zé Nguélé objected that a president could appoint a deputy one day and remove him the next.

The Empty Post and the Legal Dispute

If the vice president is also unable to serve, or the post is not filled, voters choose a new president. The amended text sets that ballot “20 days at least and 120 days at most” after the vacancy opens.

The harder question is who may ask the Constitutional Council to declare a vacancy in the first place. A companion law of 14 April amended Article 38 of the 2004 law that governs the council.

Cabral Libii, a lawmaker who leads the opposition Cameroonian Party for National Reconciliation (PCRN), says that law gives the power only to the vice president. “As long as a vice president is not appointed, the vacancy cannot be established,” he argued in August.

Christian Bomo Ntimbane, a lawyer who heads the Héritage party, rejects that reading, Cameroun Actuel reported on Monday 10 August. He says the 2026 law did not repeal the older rule letting the speaker of the National Assembly refer a vacancy.

The argument began after Hiram Samuel Iyodi, leader of the MP3 party, asked speaker Théodore Datouo to bring a vacancy case before the council. No public ruling by the council on who holds that power has been reported.

On Tuesday 13 October, Libii renewed his warning of “chaos” if Biya could no longer serve before naming a deputy. Our news report Cabral Libii Urges Biya, 93, to Name a No. 2 covers that statement in full.

What It Means for US Readers

The US State Department rates Cameroon at Level 2, “exercise increased caution,” in an advisory dated Thursday 14 May 2026. It warns that civil unrest is common, with “the potential for political violence.”

A sudden vacancy with no vice president would open a 20 to 120 day election window under contested procedures. Aid programmes, contracts and travel plans could pause until the Constitutional Council settles who acts.

The stabiliser is that the rules are written down and the institutions that apply them already exist. A named vice president would give a clear chain of command, although critics say it would bypass voters.

What Is Not Known

Biya has not said publicly whether or when he will appoint a vice president. Names that circulate in Yaoundé are speculation, not an official shortlist.

It is also unclear who would act as interim president while the post stays empty. Only the Constitutional Council can settle the competing readings of the April texts.

Connected Coverage

For the wider background, read Cameroon Explained 2026: Biya’s Long Rule, Two Crises, the Economy and What to Watch. Cameroon’s place among its neighbours and partners is mapped in Cameroon Geopolitics Explained 2026.

Our earlier report Paul Biya Reintroduces Vice President Role as Cameroon Succession Fight Intensifies covers the first round of the debate. This explainer sets out the legal rules that sit behind it.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are Cameroon’s succession rules now?

Since April 2026, an appointed vice president completes the term if the presidency falls vacant. If that post is empty, an election must follow within 20 to 120 days.

Who appoints Cameroon’s vice president?

The president appoints the vice president, sets the holder’s duties and can end the appointment at any time. The office is not elected by voters.

Has a vice president been named?

No vice president had been appointed by Wednesday 14 October 2026. President Paul Biya has not said publicly when he will fill the post.

Who acted as interim president before the reform?

The president of the Senate served as interim head of state until a new president was elected. The interim leader could not stand in that election.

Why is the vacancy procedure disputed?

A law of 14 April changed who may ask the Constitutional Council to declare a vacancy. Lawyers disagree on whether the National Assembly speaker keeps that power while no vice president exists.

World.title: Two Belize City teenagers remanded to prison on firearm and ammunition charges
World.content:
Two Belize City teenagers remanded to prison on firearm and ammunition charges

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two 19-year-old Belize City men have been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after police linked them to an unlicensed 9mm handgun and 12 live rounds of ammunition.

Elijah Willoughby and Aaron Smith were jointly charged with keeping a firearm without a gun licence and keeping ammunition without a gun licence following a police discovery on Saturday, October 10, 2026.

According to court reports, police recovered a black Jericho 9mm pistol bearing a serial number, along with 12 live rounds of ammunition.

The two appeared unrepresented before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2 at the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, October 13, where they both pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Due to the nature of the offences under the Firearms Act, both teenagers were remanded to the Belize Central Prison until their next court appearance on December 14, 2026.

World.title: International News: Pacific breaks record for powerful, long-lasting hurricanes
World.content:
International News: Pacific breaks record for powerful, long-lasting hurricanes

By Zoila Palma: The eastern and central Pacific has broken a record for accumulated cyclone energy, as powerful hurricanes continue to develop and last longer than usual.

Scientists say a strong El Niño, warmer ocean temperatures and favorable atmospheric conditions are contributing to the unusually active hurricane season.

Colorado State University researcher Phil Klotzbach said the activity has intensified since Hurricane Odalys formed on September 20.

The region surpassed its previous accumulated cyclone energy record, set in 2018, on Sunday, while Hurricane Simon continued affecting the area off Mexico’s western coast. Klotzbach said the Pacific was also approaching a record for the number of days with a hurricane spinning.

Scientists attribute much of the activity to El Niño, which weakens wind shear in the Pacific, allowing storms to strengthen and survive longer. Ocean temperatures are also several degrees Fahrenheit above normal in parts of the Pacific, providing additional energy for storm development. Atmospheric scientist Kim Wood said both the eastern and central Pacific have been unusually active simultaneously this year.

The last five Pacific hurricanes—Nolo, Odalys, Polo, Rachel and Simon—have all reached major hurricane status, with winds of at least 111 miles per hour.

Meanwhile, the Atlantic hurricane season has been unusually quiet, with accumulated cyclone energy below 18 percent of normal for this time of year.

World.title: Soil Doctors train 20 farmers in practical soil management in Hopkins
World.content:
Soil Doctors train 20 farmers in practical soil management in Hopkins

By Zoila Palma: Certified Soil Doctors Sedella and Augustine of the Stann Creek District conducted their first farmer-to-farmer training at the Hopkins Cooperative, reaching 20 farmers as part of the rollout of the National Soil Doctor Training Programme.

The programme is implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) under the Global Soil Partnership, in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Enterprise (MAFSE).

Building on their Training of Trainers at Central Farm, the Soil Doctors used hands-on demonstrations and Soil Doctor kits to teach farmers practical soil diagnostic techniques.

The training covered soil texture, pH and organic matter, along with sustainable soil management and climate-smart agricultural practices.

World.title: Ben apologizes following weekend incident; expresses gratitude to family and friends for encouragement
World.content:
Ben apologizes following weekend incident; expresses gratitude to family and friends for encouragement

By Zoila Palma: Social media influencer Benjamin Garcia has issued a statement following the incident that occurred over the weekend.

Garcia says that this incident has given him time “to reflect, not only on the events themselves, but also on the people who matter most to me, the responsibilities I carry, and the importance of the trust others have placed in me.

I recognize the seriousness of any incident involving a firearm and understand the concern and public discussion that the circumstances have generated.”

Ben says that beyond the headlines, he is a son, a family man, a friend, a colleague, and someone who has dedicated all of his life to building something meaningful through hard work and perseverance.

“Like anyone else, I have people who love me, believe in me, and depend on me. Knowing the worry and disappointment that the past few days have brought to some of those closest to me has weighed heavily on my heart.

To my family, friends, colleagues and clients, I sincerely regret the concern, uncertainty, and disappointment that this situation has caused,” he said.

Ben added that he has worked hard to build meaningful relationships, create opportunities, contribute to his community, and earn the confidence of those around him.

He further reassured his clients of his commitment to honoring his obligations, delivering the quality of work they expect, and maintaining the professional relationships they have built together.

Ben thanked everyone who reached out and offered words of encouragement and said that this incident served as a reminder of what really matters, his faith and family.

“I cannot change the attention or circumstances of the past few days, but I can determine how I carry myself moving forward.

With faith in God, humility in my heart, and a renewed appreciation for the people and responsibilities in my life, I intend to move forward with dignity and purpose,” he expressed.

World.title: Who were the sons of the Baymen?
World.content:
Who were the sons of the Baymen?

The views expressed in this article are those of the writer and not necessarily those of Breaking Belize News.

By Nuri Muhammad: Rethinking the History Behind Our National Anthem

The phrase “sons of the Baymen’s clan” in Belize’s National Anthem has led some to argue that it glorifies British settlers while ignoring the Maya, Garifuna, Mestizos and other communities. But the history is more complex.

The Baymen were mainly British woodcutters who established the early settlement. Its development, however, depended heavily on enslaved Africans, who cut timber, navigated rivers and endured the hardships of the forest. Europeans controlled the settlement, but Africans provided much of its labor.

The Maya were already here and resisted colonial expansion. The Garifuna arrived in the early nineteenth century, while Mestizos and Yucatec Maya refugees came in larger numbers after the Caste War of Yucatán began in 1847. These communities became essential to Belize, but they did not participate in the original British logging settlement in the same way or at the same time.

This history matters when considering Samuel Alfred Haynes, the anthem’s author. Haynes was a Black Belizean, World War I veteran and critic of colonial discrimination. Connected to the unrest of 1919 and influenced by Marcus Garvey’s message of Black pride and self-reliance, he may not have intended “sons of the Baymen’s clan” to glorify British colonialism.

Perhaps the phrase referred not only to European settlers, but also to the descendants of Africans whose labor built the settlement. Haynes may have been reclaiming a history whose Black contributions had long been minimized.

His original composition, Land of the Gods, later became associated with the nationalist movement led by George Price and the People’s United Party. At independence in 1981, it was adopted as Land of the Free. Its use by the nationalist movement suggests that the song expressed Belizean self-determination rather than loyalty to the British Empire.

We must also remember that the Battle of St. George’s Caye in 1798 did not end slavery. Enslaved Africans may have helped defend the settlement, but they remained enslaved until emancipation was completed in 1838. Victory over Spain was not freedom for them.

Their descendants oopĺĺĺĺlĺl and social development. This gives added meaning to the anthem’s words: “No longer shall we be hewers of wood.” The line speaks to a people determined not to remain defined by their ancestors’ forced labor.

We can recognize the contributions of the Maya, Garifuna, Mes1izos and other communities without erasing the central role of African labor in the early settlement. The British settlement and the Belizean nation are related, but they are not identical historical processes.

The Baymen did not build Belize alone. Africans helped create the settlement, and their descendants have every right to claim that history. When we sing the National Anthem, we should remember not only colonial beginnings, but also our people’s long struggle to transform oppression into freedom.

World.title: El Salvador’s Ambassador promotes National tree during visit to Minister of Agriculture
World.content:
El Salvador’s Ambassador promotes National tree during visit to Minister of Agriculture

By Zoila Palma: El Salvador’s Ambassador to Belize, Graciela Perez, met with Minister of Agriculture, Food Security and New Growth Industries Rodwell Ferguson and Minister of State Luis Alex Balona on October 13 to promote the propagation of El Salvador’s national tree, “Tabebuia rosea”, known in El Salvador as Maquilishuat.

The visit formed part of a diplomatic initiative aimed at promoting environmental sustainability, agricultural exchange and stronger cultural ties between Belize and El Salvador.

During the meeting, Ambassador Perez shared informational packets and a small glass jar containing fresh Maquilishuat seeds as a gesture of goodwill and ecological partnership.

The Maquilishuat tree can provide shade in open areas and may also be incorporated into silvopastoral reforestation initiatives, which combine trees with livestock and pasture management. The tree is known for its beautiful pink flowers, which typically bloom once a year during the dry season, primarily between January and May.

World.title: International News: Mexico moves to protect children from violent and sexual content online
World.content:
International News: Mexico moves to protect children from violent and sexual content online

By Zoila Palma: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has announced plans to sign a presidential decree requiring digital platforms, including social media networks and streaming services, to protect children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content.

The measure will increase government oversight of major technology companies operating in Mexico, Latin America’s second-largest economy, Reuters report.

The decree follows an attack in early October at a high school in the northern state of Coahuila, where two 18-year-old former students reportedly killed one person and wounded three others. The government’s announcement comes as concerns grow over the protection of minors and their exposure to harmful material online.

Government adviser Luisa Maria Alcalde said digital platforms will have one month to comply with the new requirements.

Sheinbaum warned that if companies fail to follow the decree, her administration would support legislation to impose penalties. Officials said they had already met with representatives of Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei to discuss the proposed measures.

The announcement comes as Governments in Europe and Australia are tightening oversight of digital platforms, while several U.S. states are pursuing child-safety measures.

World.title: Halo BPO hiring work from home sales agents in Belize
World.content:
Halo BPO hiring work from home sales agents in Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Looking for a job you can do from home? Halo BPO is hiring sales agents across Belize.

The position offers a pay structure that grows quickly. Agents start at $8.50 an hour on day one, move to $9.00 an hour by week two and reach $10.00 an hour by day thirty.

Pay is weekly, with commission and performance bonuses on top.

An SSD is preferred, and Chromebooks are not allowed. A quiet, distraction free workspace is required.

To apply, send your resume to [email protected] with your full name in the subject line.

World.title: Diddy rushed to hospital after prison fight with Dudus — report
World.content:
American rapper P Diddy and Jamaican drug lord Christopher 'Dudus' Coke a

American music mogul Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs was reportedly rushed to hospital on Wednesday after allegedly getting into a physical altercation with convicted Jamaican drug lord Christopher ‘Dudus’ Coke.
