World.title: Russian propaganda outlet moves to Budapest – and lists a familiar Hungarian name as editor-in-chief
World.content:
A Russian media outlet accused of spreading Kremlin-friendly narratives has moved its editorial address to Budapest, but its contact page lists a surprising name as editor-in-chief: Mária Schmidt, the former director of the House of Terror Museum, a close friend of former PM Viktor Orbán. She denies any connection to the publication and says she had never heard of it.

Govorit Europa, a multilingual website presenting itself as an independent European media project, has moved its listed editorial address from Berlin to Budapest. The outlet regularly publishes content criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, questioning Ukraine’s political independence and portraying Western policy towards Russia as a threat to European security.

Investigative outlet Átlátszó noticed that the website’s contact page names Mária Schmidt as editor-in-chief. Schmidt, the historian and former director of Budapest’s House of Terror Museum, told the publication that she had nothing to do with the outlet.

“I am not the editor-in-chief of the newspaper. Until now, I did not even know that such a publication existed,” she said.

From Berlin to Budapest, with servers in Kazakhstan

Govorit previously operated under the govorit.eu domain and listed a Berlin address. It subsequently moved to govorit.tv, while its editorial contact address was changed to one in Hungary. Its servers were reportedly relocated to Kazakhstan.

The outlet says European authorities pressured the project, forcing it to leave EU-based hosting services. It claims the move was necessary because of restrictions on its content, which it presents as a matter of freedom of expression.

However, its activities have attracted interest from foreign authorities. In May 2026, the British government imposed sanctions on Govorit, identifying it as part of a Russia-linked foreign information manipulation network whose activities were intended to destabilise Ukraine.

The measures include asset freezes and restrictions relating to internet services. The British designation concerns the outlet’s alleged role in information operations, rather than simply its publication of pro-Russian opinions.

If you missed it: Orbán missing from Fidesz’s big 23 October event? Former president Áder to take the stage instead

Links to previously sanctioned media platforms

Govorit’s history is connected to two earlier platforms, Golos and Euromore. According to the British government, these websites presented themselves as independent media outlets while distributing material serving Russian state interests.

British authorities have also pointed to possible financial support through Pravfond, a Russian organisation officially dedicated to protecting the rights of Russians living abroad. Estonian authorities have identified the organisation as a front linked to Russian military intelligence, the GRU.

The UK subsequently sanctioned Govorit and Euroview, a related platform, in May 2026.

Govorit publishes content in numerous languages, including Hungarian, English, German, French, Ukrainian and Russian. This allows similar narratives to reach audiences across different countries, with locally targeted websites potentially appearing in search results in their respective languages.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Who is behind the Budapest operation?

Despite the change of address, key details about Govorit’s Hungarian presence is unclear. It has not been established which legal entity operates the Budapest office, who finances its activities in Hungary, how many people actually work in the country or how the operation is connected to its previous operators.

Átlátszó also visited the address listed on the website, on Paulay Ede Street in Budapest, but found no identifiable editorial office or publishing company.

The outlet’s editor-in-chief could not be reached for comment. Schmidt’s name therefore remains an unexplained feature of the website rather than evidence that she is involved in its operation.

World.title: PM Magyar to meet Zelenskyy for first time as prime minister this week
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar is due to hold his first official one-to-one meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday, following a major breakthrough on Hungarian-language education in Ukraine.

Magyar announced the planned meeting in a Facebook post on Wednesday as he travelled to Brussels for a key European Union summit. Before the summit, he is also scheduled to meet the leaders of the Visegrád Four countries and attend several other high-level discussions.

The talks with Zelenskyy are expected to take place on Friday morning and will mark the two leaders’ first official meeting.

A long-awaited meeting after strained relations

Since Hungary’s change of government, a meeting between Magyar and Zelenskyy has repeatedly been discussed. Relations between Kyiv and the previous Hungarian government were highly strained, making direct talks between the two leaders a long-awaited step for both sides.

A major development came on Monday, when Ukraine announced a historic legislative move to guarantee education in Hungarian for the country’s Hungarian-speaking minority. The announcement appears to have helped pave the way for Friday’s meeting.

The rights of ethnic Hungarians in Ukraine, particularly in Transcarpathia, have long been a source of tension between the two countries. Disputes over minority-language education contributed to the difficult relationship between Kyiv and the previous Hungarian government.

If you missed it: Interview: PM Magyar could meet Zelensky as early as next week

EU summit to focus on borders, energy and funding

Magyar said the Brussels summit would address several issues crucial to Hungary’s future, including strengthening the protection of the EU’s external borders, tackling the energy crisis and negotiating the bloc’s next seven-year budget.

His schedule also includes talks with the prime ministers of the Visegrád Four — Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and the Czech Republic — as well as a meeting of European People’s Party leaders and a cohesion policy discussion convened by Italy’s prime minister.

The EU’s long-term budget is particularly important for Hungary, as it will shape the funding available for development and investment across the bloc in the coming years.

Magyar is expected to return to Hungary late on Friday night. Until then, Deputy Prime Minister Bálint Ruff will coordinate the government’s work, according to the prime minister’s announcement.

Featured image: Facebook/Péter Magyar

World.title: Orbán-era business giant could go bankrupt with 16 thousand employees
World.content:
B+N Magyarország, a major contractor responsible for cleaning and maintaining most Hungarian hospitals, is facing serious financial and operational difficulties, according to a Hungarian report. The company’s owners have reportedly offered to sell it to the state, while the national hospital authority says it is preparing for the possibility that the contractor can no longer fulfil its obligations. The company, however, insists that wages are being paid on time and that most of the problems have been resolved.

B+N Magyarország Kft., a major facilities management company with thousands of employees working in Hungary’s healthcare sector, is experiencing significant operational difficulties, Hungarian newspaper Magyar Hang has reported.

According to the newspaper, the company, which took over contracts previously held by B+N Referencia Zrt., may have sufficient funds to pay its employees only for October and November. The owners have reportedly offered to sell the business to the Hungarian state.

The company’s difficulties have also been acknowledged by the National Directorate General for Hospitals (OKFŐ), which told Magyar Hang that it had already developed contingency measures to reduce risks to healthcare services.

However, B+N Magyarország has disputed the suggestion that employees’ wages are at risk, saying that salaries and related contributions remain a priority and are paid on time. The company also said that most of the problems had since been resolved.

Why does B+N matter to Hungary’s hospitals?

B+N Magyarország is responsible for cleaning and facilities management at the vast majority of Hungarian hospitals. Its work includes cleaning hospital premises and contributing to technical maintenance. The company also provides cleaning services for Hungarian railway operator MÁV and carries out work in hundreds of state-owned buildings.

Magyar Hang initially reported that the business employed more than 14,000 people. In its response to the newspaper, however, B+N Magyarország put its workforce at more than 16,000, including nearly 7,000 people working in healthcare services under a framework agreement with the Directorate General for Public Procurement and Supply (KEF).

The potential disruption therefore extends beyond the company itself. If B+N were unable to fulfil its contracts, hospitals and other public institutions could face difficulties maintaining essential cleaning and operational services.

If you missed it: PM Magyar announces wealth and small-business tax details

How did the company become a major state contractor?

B+N Magyarország was established on 1 October 2025 through the separation of part of the business of B+N Referencia Zrt. The new company took over work linked to public procurement contracts previously won by the original business.

B+N Referencia did not disappear. It continued operating under the name LIWO FM Zrt., focusing primarily on international investments and strategic management. The wider LIWO Group operates across nine European countries and employs tens of thousands of people, according to the company and media reports. B+N Magyarország is one of its group members.

The business has frequently been described in the Hungarian press as close to the former Orbán-era political and economic establishment, largely because of its substantial state contracts and rapid growth over the past decade.

According to the reports, B+N Referencia dramatically increased its after-tax profits between 2010 and 2022, while the wider group expanded into a major regional facilities management provider. Its client base includes public institutions as well as major companies and transport hubs.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Could the Hungarian state take over the company?

According to Magyar Hang, the owners have already offered B+N Magyarország to the Hungarian state for purchase. The report draws a parallel with businessman Gyula Balásy, whose companies were also reportedly offered to the state amid financial and business developments.

No state acquisition of B+N Magyarország has been confirmed, however, and the company has not publicly stated that a sale is imminent.

World.title: Fidesz claims Péter Magyar has given up EUR 2.1 billion in EU funds
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar has given up on 2.1 billion euros from the funds “secured by [former prime minister] Viktor Orbán during tough negotiations”, the Fidesz-Christian Democrats European parliamentary group said on Wednesday.

The group said that further details of the “Brussels-Tisza Pact” had come to light. They added that in 2022 the European Commission initiated the freezing of 6.3 billion euros in EU funding from the cohesion funds due to Hungary.

MEPs from the former governing coalition said that President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen had made it clear in early 2024 that 20 billion euros in EU funds due to Hungary would remain frozen until “our country meets Brussels’ politically coercive conditions”.

They added that the reasons for the suspension of the funds included concerns regarding LGBTQ rights, academic freedom and the right to asylum.

“Following the change of government, Péter Magyar’s administration fulfilled all of Brussels’ political conditions,” they said.

“Brussels cannot formulate a demand that Péter Magyar and his colleagues would not fulfil enthusiastically, diligently and obsequiously. The question is what will be Brussels’ next demand?” the Fidesz-KDNP group added in its statement.

The Council of the EU decided on Tuesday to conclude the conditionality procedure against Hungary, allowing Hungary access to 4.2 billion euros in funding.

Fidesz MEP Csaba Dömötör said that the Fidesz-Christian Democrats delegation demands full transparency regarding the contents of the political agreement between the Tisza government and the European Commission.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Speaking to Hungarian journalists, Dömötör said “it has become clear in recent weeks that, in exchange for EU funds, the Tisza government is expected to meet demands formulated by the European Commission over the past few years, demands that the previous government consistently rejected.”

The new Hungarian government is implementing the “list of demands” that the previous government was also well aware of but had resisted, he said.

“The only question remaining is what are the as-yet-unknown demands? Will they alter the personal income tax system, tamper with family benefits, and actually raise the corporate tax?” he asked.

Since these measures affect the lives, livelihoods, and jobs of millions of Hungarians, “we demand full transparency”: all key details of the agreement must be made public, Dömötör said.

World.title: French President Macron is coming to Budapest for Hungary’s 23 October celebrations: PM Magyar reveals plans
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron will join foreign leaders in Budapest for Hungary’s 23 October commemorations, Prime Minister Péter Magyar has announced. The government is planning a full day of events across the country, with major programmes in the capital, a special performance at the Hungarian State Opera and a reception for visiting dignitaries.

French President Emmanuel Macron will visit Hungary on 23 October to attend the commemorations marking the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution and War of Independence, Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced in an interview with independent Hungarian outlet Partizán on Tuesday.

Several other foreign heads of state and government, as well as parliamentary speakers, are also expected to attend the events. Magyar said he would welcome the visiting dignitaries at the Museum of Fine Arts in Budapest as part of the celebrations.

“French President Emmanuel Macron will be here, as will EU leaders and leaders from neighbouring countries and even the Balkan states,” the prime minister said.

Hungary plans a full day of events for 23 October

Magyar promised a different kind of national commemoration this year, with events extending beyond the traditional wreath-laying ceremonies and flag-raising. The programme will include activities both in Budapest and elsewhere in the country, with several locations in the capital hosting events throughout the day.

These include Kossuth Square, Andrássy Avenue, the Danube embankment and Bem Square. A major gathering is planned for Kossuth Square, followed by a gala performance at the Hungarian State Opera. The prime minister said he would then host the invited heads of state and government and parliamentary speakers at the Museum of Fine Arts.

The anniversary marks seven decades since the 1956 uprising against Soviet rule, which began on 23 October and became one of the defining events in modern Hungarian history.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Israeli President Herzog to visit, but Netanyahu will not attend

Magyar also addressed the expected Israeli presence during the commemorations. Israeli President Isaac Herzog is due to visit Hungary a few days before 23 October, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will not attend the anniversary events, Magyar said.

Tisza has not decided whether to support the new chief prosecutor nominee

During the Partizán interview, Magyar was also asked whether his Tisza Party would support Péter Fejes, the candidate nominated by President András Baka for Hungary’s chief prosecutor. Magyar said the party’s parliamentary group had not yet discussed the nomination and still needed to gather information about Fejes, who was put forward on Monday.

He acknowledged that Fejes had worked under former chief prosecutor Péter Polt, but argued that this was true of almost every prosecutor. The Tisza Party had previously announced on the day of the nomination that it could not support Baka’s earlier candidate, Zoltán Szathmáry. It has not made a similar declaration regarding Fejes so far.

If you missed it: Interview: PM Magyar could meet Zelensky as early as next week

Magyar comments on press access to Parliament

The prime minister was also asked about the decision to deny Partizán access to Parliament earlier in October. The broadcaster was reportedly refused entry because its website did not publish news articles and therefore did not meet the relevant legal definition of a press outlet.

Partizán has since begun publishing news on its website but continues to oppose the regulation. Magyar said he had reservations about the rules but stressed that Parliament was a separate branch of power and that his government did not interfere in its decisions on access.

He also noted that more journalists were present in Parliament than ever before, according to his assessment. Magyar added that Partizán would be the first Hungarian media outlet to take a seat in the prime minister’s office.

World.title: Hungarian energy state secretary resigns after controversy over battery industry conference – UPDATE: Kapitány reacts
World.content:
András Tótth has resigned from Hungary’s Ministry of Economic Affairs and Energy for personal reasons, but his departure came after controversy over a planned battery industry conference in Debrecen. Reports also suggest that Minister István Kapitány’s own resignation was discussed, although the ministry denied this.

András Tótth, the state secretary responsible for energy at Hungary’s Ministry of Economic Affairs and Energy, has resigned, with his appointment officially ending on 13 October at the recommendation of Prime Minister Péter Magyar.

The ministry, led by István Kapitány, announced the departure in a brief statement on Tuesday evening, citing personal reasons. However, the timing of the resignation has attracted attention following a public dispute over a battery industry conference planned for Debrecen, one of Hungary’s key battery manufacturing centres.

Resignation follows dispute over Debrecen battery conference

The controversy centred on the Hungarian Battery Days conference, scheduled to take place at Debrecen’s Kölcsey Centre on 4 and 5 November. Several Chinese battery manufacturers, including senior executives from CATL, are expected to attend the event.

On Tuesday evening, Zsolt Tárkányi, a Tisza Party politician, published a Facebook post criticising the conference and the portrayal of Debrecen as a European battery industry hub. He argued that local residents had not wanted the factories and had so far experienced their disadvantages rather than the benefits promised by the industry.

“For the people of Debrecen, battery factories do not represent sustainable, environmentally conscious, modern mobility,” Tárkányi wrote, pointing instead to distrust surrounding factory operations, fears of pollution and concerns about the future of the city and its residential areas.

The politician also objected to plans for a Hungarian government state secretary to speak at the event without prior public information about the appearance. According to an update to his Facebook post, Tárkányi was informed just minutes after publishing it that the state secretary concerned had resigned.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Who was András Tótth?

Tótth was appointed state secretary for energy at the end of May 2026. He began his career as an energy expert at Boston Consulting Group before taking senior positions at E.ON Földgáz and the MVM Group, working primarily in strategy, regulation and trading.

When announcing his appointment, Kapitány said Tótth’s professional experience provided a strong foundation for managing the challenges facing Hungary’s energy sector.

His immediate priorities included preparing energy-related measures needed to secure the return of EU funding. In the medium term, he was expected to help develop an energy strategy aimed at improving energy efficiency, self-sufficiency and competitiveness.

Tótth also took on a prominent role at state-owned energy company MVM, where he was appointed to lead the board of directors responsible for determining the group’s strategic direction.

If you missed it: Fidesz accuses Tisza government of pushing Hungarian firms out of major projects to benefit foreign companies

Reports raise questions about Minister Kapitány’s position

The resignation also fuelled speculation about the leadership of the ministry itself. According to HVG, several sources indicated that Kapitány’s resignation as minister had also been discussed on Tuesday. The ministry officially denied this, however, and no confirmed ministerial departure was announced.

István Kapitány. Screenshot from Telex/YouTube.

HVG reported that Tótth was more than a senior official responsible for preparing energy policy. He had been selected partly for his professional background and his reputation for determination, with responsibility for advancing policy proposals and helping redirect a sector facing the consequences of earlier government decisions.

The publication also raised questions about the concentration of authority surrounding Tótth’s roles at MVM and within the government. The ministry previously explained that he had inadvertently been granted the government’s shareholder rights over the state-owned company through an administrative oversight, adding that he had neither made nor countersigned decisions in that capacity.

UPDATE: Kapitány reacts

“I haven’t resigned,” the Minister for Energy responded to the HVG article.

“I haven’t resigned, and I won’t! It’s pointless for a newspaper that has seen better days to keep spreading this, despite the rebuttal,” said István Kapitány, Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy, in a Facebook post, responding to HVG’s report (confirmed by several sources) that his resignation had been mooted on Tuesday.

World.title: Albanian President Urges Calm as Street Protest Clashes Continue
World.content:
Albanian students protesting on October 14, 2026. Photo: LSA.

Clashes in Tirana between anti-government protesters and police officers intensified on Wednesday, as police used tear gas and water cannon against groups of mainly student demonstrators who threw stones, fireworks and Molotov cocktails at officers, damaging public institutions and private businesses.

The ground floor of one building was set on fire, while several traffic lights were destroyed.

Protesters chanted: “You don’t have enough handcuffs for everyone” and “Rama into prison, Berisha into prison”, referring to Prime Minister Edi Rama and opposition leader Sali Berisha. Two opposition MPs from Berisha’s Democratic Party who joined the protest were told to leave.

One second-year law student told BIRN he was protesting so that “corrupt politicians can be brought to justice”. Another young protester said they were demonstrating “for freedom, to overthrow the government”.

President Bajram Begaj said in a statement that he was “following with concern” the escalation of tensions in Tirana’s streets and called on “all parties to act with responsibility and restraint”.

“At this moment, the country needs more responsibility. The constitution and the law must remain the boundary for all, without exception. I remain ready to listen to all concerns,” Begaj said.

Based on preliminary information from the police, at least 20 protesters have been arrested.

“Violent acts and the destruction of property by fire directly endanger the lives of citizens, as well as public and private property,” police said in a press release.

According to the Ministry of Health “three protesters and two police officers are currently receiving emergency treatment; all are conscious and in good health”.

Euronews Albania journalist Alice Taylor said that while she was taking photos, a police officer took her phone without warning.

The Association of Journalists of Albania, AGSH, condemned the act, calling it “a direct obstruction to the reporting and documentation of the protest. This incident adds to other reported cases of violence, intimidation, and obstruction of journalists over the past two days.”

At least five journalists were injured on Tuesday during earlier clashes between the police and protesters.

The EU Delegation in Tirana expressed concern about police over-reaction and called for calm.

“Freedom of assembly and expression are fundamental rights and core European values. They should be respected and exercised peacefully. We take note of the allegations of excessive violence by the police against protestors and journalists,” the EU Delegation said in a statement.

“We expect police action to be proportionate and respect fundamental rights and expect these cases to be investigated as a matter of priority. ⁠We encourage all sides to de-escalate the tension,” it added.

Wednesday’s protest was the continuation of a rally from the previous day, when students were called upon to demonstrate in Tirana by the so-called “Flamingo Revolution” protesters.

The students came to voice their discontent over university conditions and the cost of living. They also called for Prime Minister Rama’s resignation – a key demand of the Flamingo Revolution protests, which started in June as environmental demonstrations but evolved into an anti-government movement.

World.title: Kosovo to Boost Support for Ex-KLA Leaders Ahead of War Crimes Appeal
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Bos/Hrv/Srp



Kosovo government meeting on October 14, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

Kosovo’s government on Wednesday approved the establishment of a working group to support the four former Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, leaders appealing against their war-crimes convictions, issued by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague on September 16.

“We consider the first-instance verdict against the former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army to be legally and morally unjust, as well as factually and historically inaccurate; therefore, we are working to have it corrected on appeal,” Prime Minister Albin Kurti said.

Kurti said the working group would be led by First Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca, and would include institutional and parliamentary representation. “With this decision, we are acting on our pledge to use the means at our disposal to strive for justice and to defend the historical truth of our liberation war,” he said.

Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci, former parliament speakers Kadri Veseli and Jakup Krasniqi, and former MP Rexhep Selimi were found guilty of arbitrary detention, cruel treatment, torture and murder during the Kosovo war from April 1998 to June 20, 1999, in Kosovo and several locations in Albania.

Thaci and Krasniqi were each sentenced to 25 years in prison, Veseli to 18 and Selimi to 13 years in prison. The defence teams have announced they are preparing a legal challenge.

The verdict triggered protests in Kosovo, which turned violent on October 5 as protesters demanded that parliament adopt law changes to curtail the jurisdiction of the court. MPs voted for the changes on October 6. Critics, however, claim the changes, which are yet to be enforced, will not necessarily have an impact.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers is a hybrid court, part of Kosovo’s judiciary but located in The Hague and staffed by internationals. The court was established in 2015 under pressure from Kosovo’s Western allies, with Thaci as one of its main supporters.

A month after the verdict convicting Thaci, criticism of the Specialist Chambers has continued unabated. On Wednesday, Kosovo’s Ombudsperson, Naim Qelaj, held a discussion event in Pristina to demand external oversight of the EU-funded court.

Qelaj claimed that the court “has not been subject to democratic monitoring and control by the institutions of the Republic of Kosovo, creating a lack of transparency and accountability towards the citizens and institutions of Kosovo”.

He said it should report to the Kosovo authorities and that the Ombudsperson institution should be able to have access to its work.

“I don’t want to believe the Council of the EU and other donor countries are interested in this court continuing with such standards,” Qelaj said, announcing that he had sent his concerns to parliamentary speaker Albulena Haxhiu, Prime Minister Kurti, the president of the Specialist Chambers, Ekaterina Trendafilova, and Kosovo’s President Justina Shiroka Pula, as well as the Council of the EU.

BIRN contacted the court and the Council of the EU for a comment but received no response by the time of publication.

World.title: Insider Blows Lid on Serbian Ruling Party’s Use of Hired Thugs
World.content:
‘Ready to use violence’

One of the characteristics of the SNS’s 14 years in power has been the use of hired muscle – informal security structures of burly, black-clad men.

Marjanovic was a veteran of those informal structures, deployed to defend party offices from protesters or coordinate security at major party events.

Men like him have become notorious, fuelling fears of yet more violence when Serbia votes on October 25.

As far back as 2014, two years after the SNS rose to power, election monitors from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, OSCE, cited “credible reports of voter intimidation cases”, “vote-buying, pressure and intimidation of voters”.

There has been little improvement since. When a concrete canopy at a newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad collapsed on November 1, 2024, killing 16 people, men like Marjanovic were once again thrust to the fore.

The protests that erupted have been marred by reports of violence meted out by informal security structures affiliated with the SNS, as well as by police.

Hired muscle, said Predrag Petrovic, research director of the Belgrade-based think-tank Belgrade Centre for Security Policy, “can do what the police, at least openly and without consequences, cannot”.

“Among them are people from the criminal underworld, ready to use violence and take on risks that state actors want to avoid,” Petrovic told BIRN. “In this way, the regime gets an informal instrument of coercion, with the ability to deny responsibility for its actions.”

For their services, Marjanovic said he doled out cash given to him by the director of the Novi Sad heating utility, Nenad Barac. He also received a monthly salary through an intermediate employment agency engaged by another utility company, Lisje, in charge of the city’s cemeteries. Barac declined to comment.

“Those are phantom jobs, that’s what they call them,” he told BIRN. “But I’m not the only one, unfortunately.”

“I never went to work, but, of course, I received a regular salary.”

Lisje did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

From history student to ruling party ‘security’

World.title: Sex Tapes Scandal Shows Albania’s Still Stuck in Patriarchal Mindset
World.content:
A series of intimate videos circulating on WhatsApp, featuring well-known figures engaged in sexual encounters, has caused disquiet here in Tirana. The scandal exposed a disturbing pattern involving both prominent and lesser-known singers and actresses who had allegedly been filmed in secret at the studio of Adrian Hila, a composer regarded as influential enough to shape or derail careers.

On September 30, the footage appeared online and, despite being quickly removed, continued to circulate across social media platforms and messaging apps. Reports suggest the recordings were captured using hidden cameras, without the knowledge or consent of those filmed. As the scandal widened, there were indications that about 17 performers and other public figures, both women and men, may have been affected.

Public opinion turned into persecution, with social media acting as judge and jury, publicly crucifying the women involved. Albania is still not ready to acknowledge women as sexual beings, and the scandal was largely approached through a moralistic lens.

World.title: How North Macedonia’s Inheritance Tax Policy Penalises Childless Heirs
World.content:
Liljana Matic, a 70-year-old who lives in North Macedonia’s capital, was surprised when she received a tax assessment from the City of Skopje at the end of August for inheriting the apartment where she had lived for decades with her husband, who is now deceased.

She had expected not to pay anything to transfer the apartment into her name, as they had lived there together from the day they received it as socially owned housing, back in 1986. After Macedonia gained independence from Yugoslavia in the early 1990s and the country transitioned into capitalism, her husband was able to purchase the apartment in 1995. It was registered in his name in the Land Registry the same year.

Immediate family members are generally exempt from inheritance tax, so Liljana Matic had no reason to assume she would be treated differently from anyone else.

She was not even aware that, under the Law on Inheritance, adopted three decades ago, in 1996, she was classified as a second-order heir. The reason the legislation placed her in this category was that she and her husband had no offspring.

World.title: Bosnia’s New Government was Being Built as Votes Were Still Being Counted
World.content:
People in Bosnia and Herzegovina voted in elections on October 4, but even as the count went on, the politicians had stopped waiting.

Only three days after the election, the chairmen of the Party of Democratic Action, SDA, the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina, SBiH, and the Democratic Front, DF, in Sarajevo Canton announced that they would form the cantonal government in the capital. Power was being assembled before the final results were even in.

Other leaders were assembling alliances on the road. On October 9, Dragan Covic, leader of the Croatian Democratic Union, HDZ BiH, the main Bosnian Croat party, was in Mostar with Nermin Niksic, leader of the Social Democratic Party, SDP.

Covic then went on to Sarajevo, where Bakir Izetbegovic, leader of the SDA, received him. On Saturday, Izetbegovic welcomed Semir Efendic, leader of the SBiH, at SDA headquarters. On Monday, Covic was in Banja Luka, in Republika Srpska, sitting across from Milorad Dodik, leader of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats, SNSD, the main Bosnian Serb party.

Dodik is currently barred from holding public office because of a court conviction. Yet he emerged from the meeting as half of a partnership, already issuing joint conditions to everyone else. Thanks to the good election results their parties enjoyed, both Covic and Dodik are now key to making the government at any level.

It was a striking contrast with the dull election campaign. “This campaign is very anaemic,” Adnan Huskic, a professor at the Sarajevo School of Science and Technology, told BIRN before the vote.

World.title: Albanian Student Protesters Clash with Police Outside Ministry of Education
World.content:
Albanian police at the students’ protest in Tirana on October 13, 2026. Photo: BIRN/Fjori Sinoruka.

A student protest outside the Ministry of Education in Tirana erupted into serious clashes with police officers on Tuesday, as protesters threw rocks and eggs at the building and police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse them.

The rally was called as part of the ongoing ‘Flamingo Revolution’ anti-government protests. As well as chanting slogans against Prime Minister Edi Rama’s administration, students voiced demands for better conditions at educational establishments and adequate financial support.

“We come to Tirana to study, and we are forced not to study but to work,” one student said at the protest.

Police announced that 23 protesters were apprehended while six police officers sustained injuries.

“During the rally, a group of participants committed violent acts, damaging the external fence and then, in order to enter the courtyard [of the ministry building], they also damaged the entrance gate. They also continued to break and damage the windows and facade of the building with stone slabs and hard objects,” police said in the statement.

“Police officers called on them to stop the attack on the institution, but they continued to attack the police officers with Molotov cocktails, cans, stones and hard objects,” the statement added.

The Association of Journalists of Albania reported that a journalist sustained physical injuries at the hands of the police and a crew was prevented from reporting from the protest.

“The Association calls on State Police to immediately stop attacks on media and journalists… This is unacceptable and requires urgent addressing from the Police Oversight Agency and prosecution,” the Association of Journalists said in a statement.

Albana Kociu, Albania’s Deputy Prime Minister, posted a video on Facebook showing a protester clashing with a group of police officers during the protest, with a message saying that “violence has not been, is not and will never be the solution”.

The ‘Flamingo Revolution’ demonstrations have seen large numbers of people protesting against planned construction projects in protected environmental areas and demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Rama, accusing his government of institutional corruption and lack of transparency.

The protests in Tirana began on May 31, a day after a member of the public was assaulted by private security guards during a demonstration in Zvernec against the construction of a luxury tourism project in a protected area linked to US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

World.title: New Dinosaur Species Discovered in Croatia
World.content:
October the 14th, 2026 – An apparently brand new, previously unknown and uncategorised dinosaur species has been has been discovered in Croatia.

An incredible underwater dinosaur bone site has just been discovered in Croatia. An international team of scientists is currently extracting remains from the sea that are about 130 million years old, and according to the paleontologists’ initial assessments, the bones belong to a previously totally unknown species, HRT reports.

Poslovni reports that the fascinating remains found belong to a large, long-necked herbivorous dinosaur. Paleontologist Frano Vidaković compared it to a scene from the film Jurassic Park. “Do you remember that dinosaur from the beginning of Jurassic Park, when the paleontologists get out of the jeep in disbelief? Well, one like that – a long-necked dinosaur, large, with pillar-like legs, a long tail and neck, that fed on vegetation from the tops of trees,” Vidaković said.

American paleontologist Matthew Lamanna confirmed that this is an exceptionally important site. “The dinosaur we are excavating is without doubt a new species,” he emphasised. Scientists have so far found parts of the cervical spine, lumbar bones and ribs, and Lamanna explained how a fossilised bone differs from stone.

“To many this would look like a stone, but one detail tells us that this is a dinosaur bone. These are these small pores called trabeculae. They tell us that this is much more than a stone, that this is a dinosaur bone 130 million years old,” he explained.

croatia is home to a truly unique site

This is the only site in the world where dinosaur bones have been found in the sea, at depths of one and a half to six metres. Paleontologist and geologist Aleksandar Mezga highlights the uniqueness of the location. “This is the first such case in the world. People who have visited all the sites say they have never seen anything like this anywhere,” Mezga emphasised.

The site is located within the Datule-Barbariga paleontological reserve. 130 million years ago, the land that today forms Istria was part of a completely different landscape and was located roughly in the area of present-day North Africa. The first dinosaur bones in this area were discovered back in 1993, and completely by chance. Andrea Deklić from Natura Histrica recounted how it happened. “Mr Boscariolli was extracting date mussels here and breaking rocks to get to the shells. By chance, he came across a bone in the rock. Fortunately, his acquaintance was Fabio della Vecchia, a well-known Italian paleontologist,” Deklić said.

That is how Istria got its first dinosaur, named Histriosaurus Boscariollia. The newly discovered remains belong to a related but definitely different species. Scientists believe that the seabed near Bale hides more remains of Istrian dinosaurs that are still waiting to be discovered.

World.title: Huge Croatian Tourism Projects Are Springing Up, But There’s a Big Problem…
World.content:
October the 14th, 2026 – Some huge Croatian tourism projects are springing up, but with that come some major problems that don’t point quite towards sustainable tourism…

Thousands of new beds are planned across southern Croatia. Although those in power like to say that the country is moving towards sustainable tourism, what is happening on the ground paints a different picture. Paula Klaic Saulacic reports for Dnevnik that from the Dubrovnik littoral all the way down to Konavle – over a road distance of 60 kilometres, around 5,000 new beds are planned. They’re all connected by one single road, the Adriatic Highway, which during the summer months is bursting at the seams – and all roads ultimately lead to Dubrovnik. That city is still teeming with tourists even in October, and precisely by those visitors who come at that time because they want to avoid the summer crowds.

ecological, technological and workforce issues…

“One road, yes, we drove for a long time. It’s nice here, but any more would be too much,” commented Toby from Australia. Thousands of new beds from the Dubrovnik littoral to Konavle are not only a problem when it comes to crowds and the number of guests; the problem is with infrastructure, the workforce, and also with ecology. Some experts believe that even drinking water is under threat. Civil engineer Tomislav Paviša, in an open letter to local leaders as well as the Government, warns that projects such as Tri Sestrice, the Resort in Cavtat, Kupari and others are endangering the water supply.

“We’re witnessing that dry periods are getting longer and longer and that, consequently, there will be less and less water at the springs for a regular water supply. In order for the Dubrovnik region to approach the realisation of these projects ready, it is necessary to form a competent institution composed of hydrogeologists, hydrologists and hydraulic engineers that would deal with this vitally important problem, as well as with protection against water pollution due to accelerated urbanisation in the neighbouring country,” he said.

the water supply

Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković was not available for comment today, while the mayors of Konavle and Dubrovačko primorje earlier said that for Cavtat and Doli they see no concern for the water supply.

“There were three important conditions that had to be met, which the Municipality requested from the investor. The first is to enable the western entrance to Cavtat, the second to secure a water reservoir that will be sufficient for the next 30 or so years so that Cavtat and all the hotels have a secure water supply. The third is that all ecological standards be respected to the utmost,” said Božo Lasić, Mayor of the Municipality of Konavle (HDZ), at the end of September. “As for water, water comes from three directions: one is Doli itself with its wells, from Ston via the Oko spring, and the third from Slano via Banići, so water should not be a problem either,” said Nikola Knežić, Mayor of the Municipality of Dubrovačko primorje (HDZ), a few days later.

When asked whether, given the dry summer, golf courses and new capacities, he thinks this can be infrastructurally sustained in the future, he replied: “It can.”

The Mayor of Župa dubrovačka says that restrictions are necessary. In a municipality that is home to 8,000 inhabitants and the same number of beds, tourism has reached its peak. “These are all real and objective questions and we have to seek answers from the profession; in spatial plans all tourist zones need to be revised,” said Marko Miloslavić, Mayor of Župa dubrovačka (ŽUPKA). There are many questions, and the answers are urgent because all these projects, at least according to the investors, are proceeding according to plan – some are even of national interest. Nevertheless – water, the environment, space and the quality of life of the local community should be the only real national interest.

World.title: Natural Disaster Declared for Municipalities of Milna and Nerežišća
World.content:
October the 14th, 2026 – A natural disaster has officially been declared for the municipalities of Milna and Nerežišća on the island of Brač after the recent fire.

Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban has issued a Decision on the declaration of a natural disaster caused by fire for the area of the municipalities of Milna and Nerežišća. Morski reports that all affected people and legal entities are invited to report any and all damage to their properties as soon as possible, and no later than the 20th of October.

The Prefect issued the Decision on the declaration of a natural disaster caused by fire for the area of the Municipality of Milna and the Municipality of Nerežišća on Monday the 12th of October, according to a statement from Split-Dalmatia County.

By the Prefect’s decision, the municipal commissions for assessing damages in the affected municipalities are tasked with urgently carrying out all actions prescribed by law, processing the reports and entering the data into the national Register of Damages.

The fire that struck the wider Milna area caused extensive damage and directly threatened human and animal lives, homes, cars and other property, not to mention hotels and resorts who were forced to evacuate their tourists. It marked a summer in which the Croatian coast burned in a way that was deeply concerning.

Despite wildfires being the unfortunate norm in the tinder dry, scorching hot Dalmatian landscape in summer, the situation both on the island of Brač and across the channel on the mainland in Omiš stood out in all the wrong ways. Fires up in Zadar which were deliberately caused also threw a new angle onto an already tragic summertime reality.

World.title: Total Renovation Coming for Zagreb Railway Station
World.content:
October the 14th, 2026 – A total renovation is on the cards for the iconic Zagreb Railway Station, with new facilities and much needed modernisation coming as part of it.

Zagreb Main Railway Station is one of the most recognisable places in Zagreb. It was opened back in 1892, at a time of strong development of railway traffic and modernisation of the city, according to a design by the Hungarian architect Ferenc Pfaff. Poslovni reports that while the beautiful station has served as a backdrop for many series and films, passengers frequently complain about the lack of facilities, as well as the fact that the space should be renovated. That is precisely what is about to happen.

“HŽ Infrastructure, together with the consortium of bidders Intekonzalting d.o.o. and PlanAxis d.o.o., has signed a contract for the preparation of technical documentation for the complete renovation of the Zagreb Main Railway Station building. The preparation of the conceptual and main design, including the obtaining of all necessary permits, is currently underway. The preparation of the technical documentation is proceeding according to the planned dynamics, and its completion is scheduled by the end of 2027,” they say at HŽ.

protected cultural property

They note that the project envisages a complete structural, energy and architectural renovation of the Zagreb Main Railway Station building.

“A comprehensive rehabilitation and strengthening of the load-bearing structure will be carried out, and the selected methods will be minimally invasive in order to preserve the structural system, original materials and design elements. The architectural and construction renovation covers the façades, roof structure and interiors under conservation supervision in order to preserve the cultural and historical value of the building, which has the status of a protected cultural property. Special emphasis is on the energy renovation, which includes the replacement of existing windows and doors and the installation of heat pumps with the possibility of using renewable sources,” they explain at HŽ Infrastructure.

a brand new underpass? maybe…

The start of construction works on the Zagreb Main Railway Station building is planned after the completion of the project documentation and the implementation of the procurement procedure for the execution of the works. The planned duration of the construction works is around three years, and completion of the works is expected in 2031.

“During the renovation of the Main Railway Station building it will be necessary to close certain parts of the building, and depending on the organisation and phases of the works it is also possible to close the entire building. The organisation of passenger movement, train traffic and everyday use of the station zone will be adapted to the needs and dynamics of the renovation, taking into account passenger safety and the uninterrupted flow of railway traffic. As part of the project, the possibility has been left open for the construction of a new direct underpass beneath the Main Railway Station building, i.e. beneath the vestibule, which would directly connect the building with Tomislav Square. Further elaboration and possible realisation of the underpass are within the competence of the City of Zagreb,” our interlocutors say.

World.title: Delicious Zagreb: How the Capital’s Food Scene Became an Attraction
World.content:
October the 13th, 2026 – Zagreb is known for its market stands selling fresh, locally grown produce, but it has since managed to merge that perfectly with Michelin mentions and a blossoming international scene. Here’s how Delicious Zagreb can guide you through this impressive gastronomic maze.

Not so long ago in Zagreb (and in Croatia as a whole, if we’re being really honest) a common joke from foreign nationals was that all menus across the country must have been printed in the same factory. You could predict the options with absolute certainty depending on where you were located, and the international culinary scene in the capital was restricted to the odd Chinese restaurant.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

delicious zagreb as the capital’s food map

Sime Modric/TZGZ

Fast forward to 2026, and the food landscape is entirely unrecognisable in comparison. Zagreb has undergone a full-scale culinary revolution in a relatively short time, transforming from a continental gateway into a highly dynamic, self-assured gourmet destination. The home of various food and drink festivals and a growing number of international eateries, the capital’s food scene is no longer just an add-on to its historic architecture or Christmas markets. In fact, for around 37 percent of modern global travellers, the primary motivation for picking a destination is the food on offer at their chosen place.

Sime Modric/TZGZ

Taking this massive shift in traveller mindsets into consideration, the Zagreb Tourist Board (TZGZ) has just revealed a gastronomic offensive of sorts, entirely designed to put the capital city’s culinary identity firmly on the international map. At the heart of this push are two distinct milestones: the launch of the first-ever Gault&Millau guide exclusively dedicated to the City of Zagreb, and a whole wave of fresh, immersive digital content on the Delicious Zagreb platform.

the new gault&millau zagreb guide

Sime Modric/TZGZ

The cornerstone of Zagreb’s new culinary era is the premiere of the standalone, bilingual (Croatian/English) Gault&Millau Zagreb guide. Curating a (very) extensive list of 108 local addresses, the guide spans everything from fine-dining establishments and modern urban bistros to authentic street food stalls and traditional neighbourhood eateries that have resisted any wind of change and remain popular precisely because of that.

Sime Modric/TZGZ

What makes this release so critical for the city is Gault&Millau’s core philosophy: “Luxury lies in quality, not in price.” As Rudolf Štefan, the chef-owner of Šibenik’s Michelin-starred Pelegrini and a collaborator on the project, noted during the presentation at the Tač restaurant: “Nowadays, tourists are travelling with their palates in mind. They want a relaxed atmosphere, genuine local products, and genuine experiences. Above all, they look for honesty.”

Sime Modric/TZGZ

Zagreb’s new food scene delivers exactly that. The Croatian capital is known as a “little big city” where a modern visitors, wherever they come from, can watch a local hand over fresh cheese and sour cream at a wooden stand in the morning, and then see those exact same local ingredients completely re-imagined on a contemporary plate just a street or two away.

the way to a person’s heart is through their stomach, and zagreb has no issues there…

Crochef/TZGZ

The only “problem” anyone could run into in this sense in Zagreb is the sheer choice you have in a relatively small area. That has been taken well and truly into account, and Zagreb Tourist Board’s digital platform, Delicious Zagreb, has rolled out a suite of brand-new thematic content, gourmet routes, and specialised video series to help you work out where to begin. This platform takes everything a step far beyond generic directories, connecting visitors with the actual stories, local wine makers, confectioners, and heritage producers shaping the city’s modern flavours.

Crochef/TZGZ

The platform perfectly complements global trends toward “eat-seeing”, a concept in which dining out replaces traditional sightseeing as the main cultural lens. Through newly curated culinary routes, tourists can systematically explore Zagreb’s unique dual identity. It gives plenty of attention to the heavy, comforting continental traditions of old Zagreb, such as slow-baked štrukli, ajngemahtec (try saying that after a rakija or two) soup, and turkey with mlinci. It also spotlights Croatia’s grill cultures and creative Mediterranean influences that flow steadily inland from the coast and the islands.

Crochef/TZGZ

Zagreb’s global footprints are expanding via strategic partnerships between TZGZ and massive international culinary media. From targeted destination campaigns with Expedia to cultural deep dives in Smithsonian Magazine, not to mention high-profile features across TasteAtlas, Falstaff, and the Michelin Guide, Zagreb is consistently being spotlighted as a capital of diverse tastes.

delicious zagreb will take you seamlessly to old zagreb and into the modern international scene

Crochef/TZGZ

Whether you’re planning a city break in Zagreb or you’ve been on the coast and got a bit sick of fresh fish (it seems unbelievable, but it happens!), Delicious Zagreb is your best friend. You can build your food itinerary through the lens of what the Croatian capital is really all about. To get a true taste of how the old and new school coexist, make sure to add these essential spots to your list.

Crochef/TZGZ

Rome and Italy, the food capital of the world, might lie just across the Adriatic, and Croatia might well be famed for its seafood, but there’s so much more to it than that. Zagreb, once entirely overlooked, is no longer playing catch-up to the coast and the islands or to other European capitals. Powered by an honest culinary identity, top class talent, and excellent infrastructural support from projects like Delicious Zagreb, the quirky Croatian capital has claimed its spot under the sun as a more than worthwhile destination for the modern foodie.

World.title: Why Ancestry.com Is Not Enough to Get You a Croatian Passport
World.content:
October the 13th, 2026 – With the rise of the likes of Ancestry.com becoming a huge social media trend, many are running into an obstacle that surprises them – proof of Croatian ancestry through this service is not enough to apply for a Croatian passport.

For the modern diaspora in the age of (perhaps too much) technology at our fingertips, tracing family history has never been easier. With a few clicks on platforms like Ancestry.com, MyHeritage, or FamilySearch, you can uncover ship passenger manifests from Ellis Island, old federal census data, and digitised draft registration cards. It’s an exhilarating feeling to see your great-grandfather’s name handwritten on a 1910 immigration log, neatly indexed in a searchable digital database.

Very many descendants assume that printing out these beautifully rendered PDF records is the ticket to securing an EU passport. Then begins the imagining of freedom of movement, no endless airport queues and buying a fishing cottage somewhere on a Mediterranean island. They bundle their internet printouts, fill out the basic forms, and head to the nearest Croatian consulate, confident that their lineage is proven… Then comes the cold shower (or rather tsunami) of bureaucratic reality.

why digital records and family mysteries always fail legal standards

The Croatian Ministry of the Interior doesn’t accept internet printouts, digitised screenshots, or family tree charts generated by commercial software. In the complicated world of European Union citizenship law, there is a massive, unforgiving gulf between discovering an ancestor online and legalising a genuine lineage for a citizenship application. If you’re relying entirely on digital databases to claim your Croatian citizenship by descent, here is why you will hit a brick wall, and what it actually takes to cross the finish line.

Croatian citizenship by descent relies on proving an unbroken, entirely legal chain of bloodline from you to the ancestor who once emigrated from Croatia elsewhere. To formally satisfy the strict requirements laid down by law, every single link in that chain must be verified by a certified, physical vital record. Commercial genealogy websites are excellent tools for historical research, but they hold no legal weight. A passenger manifest showing that an otherwise unknown “Ivan Radić” arrived in New York back in 1912 from Dalmatia proves that a man by that name travelled. It doesn’t legally prove that he is your specific biological great-grandfather, nor does it establish his exact birth status or nationality in the eyes of the modern Croatian state, which is much more complex than it seems by today’s standards. In order to build a legally compliant application package, you must transition from online search bars to physical government institutions. You need an array of documents for that.

croatia wants certified, legalised everything

First comes properly, lawfully certified records. These are physical, state-issued birth, marriage, and death certificates for every single generation connecting you to the emigrant. Then comes the chain of international authentication: Every single document issued outside of Croatia (such as an American or Canadian birth certificate) must be authenticated with an Apostille from the appropriate government authority to prove its international validity. Then comes sworn Croatian translations by an executed by a court-appointed translator, ensuring that names, dates, and legal terms align perfectly across languages.

The biggest hurdle for the DIY applicant is obtaining the foundational document: the original birth or baptismal record of the ancestor from Croatia. It simply isn’t enough to have online documents when the most important ones are typically physical pieces of paper. While very many Western countries have digitised a vast portion of their historical records, a significant amount of Croatia’s local history remains locked away in gigantic physical volumes. Millions of vital records are stored exclusively in local municipal registries, regional state archives or historic parish church books scattered all over the country.

If your grandfather was born in a small (likely now totally empty) village somewhere in the Dalmatian hinterland or a town in Slavonia back in 1905, his birth record is highly unlikely to be indexed on a commercial American genealogy site. To find and claim it, someone has to know exactly which local registry office or parish holds the historical volume, communicate with local clerks in Croatian, and physically or administratively extract a certified copy.

For an American applicant sitting in New York, Toronto, or Sydney, navigating this local, ground-level bureaucracy from thousands of miles away and in a language they’re likely unfamiliar with can stretch a DIY project from a few months into endless years of administrative limbo that never budges.

croatian by descent – bridging the gap between online research and physical, acceptable results

If you’ve used Ancestry.com to map out your family tree, it would be wrong to say you haven’t done excellent foundational work. You now have the names, the approximate dates, and the names of the home villages of your ancestors in Croatia. However, in order to turn that complex historical spider’s web into a successful application for citizenship, you need to transition to professional administrative execution.

This is precisely where specialised diaspora services like Croatian By Descent become essential to those unfamiliar with the (often intense) world of Croatian bureaucracy in navigating such choppy waters.

Instead of letting your application stall and begin gathering dust at the digital research phase, their dedicated team acts as the physical bridge to your ancestral homeland. They take your online clues and utilise ground-level access to pull certified vital records directly from Croatian records and archives. They manage the meticulous paperwork, from securing the correct American apostilles to coordinating court-certified translations, ensuring your package meets the exact standards required by the Ministry of the Interior in Croatia and preventing you being ignored and chucked to the back of a long (and dog-eared) queue.

They handle the heavy administrative lifting so you don’t waste years in a loop of consular rejections, turning your internet search history into a verified, bulletproof submission package.

If you’re ready to move past the search bar and secure your Croatian and therefore European Union passport? Explore your options and skip the DIY headaches with comprehensive support from the team at Croatian By Descent who are diaspora members with personal experience with the intricacies of this journey themselves.

World.title: Minor Says Croatian Priest Abused Her in 2021, Bozanić Allegedly Did Not Report Him
World.content:
October the 13th, 2026 – A minor said she was physically abused by a Croatian priest in 2021, yet Bozanić allegedly failed to ever report him.

Index has reported that the Zagreb Archdiocese reported a priest accused of abusing a minor to the police allegedly only five years after receiving the complaint. This occurred only after Dnevnik.hr sent an inquiry about the case. A minor female person accused the priest of abuse back in 2021. The Archdiocese submitted the report to the Zagreb police only on the 9th of October this year, two days after Dnevnik.hr sent them an inquiry about the entire case. They have refused to answer any further questions about the case.

Zagreb police confirmed their receipt of the report. “The police received a report from a church legal entity, following which it has begun a criminal investigation,” they stated in their response. They added that, in accordance with the law, the inquiries are confidential and that they cannot disclose any specific details. According to unofficial information, after the 2021 complaint the priest was relieved of his duties as administrator of one Zagreb parish and banned from public activity. The Archdiocese then appointed a new administrator. It seemed that the priest had indeed been withdrawn from public life for several years.

the case should have been reported immediately – it was not

However, by decision of Archbishop Dražen Kutleša in September 2024 he was appointed parish vicar in one parish, and in August this year as a chaplain in an institution on the territory of the Zagreb Archdiocese. It is interesting that neither the decision on his relief from duties in 2021 nor the later appointments were published in the annual reviews of appointments and dismissals of priests in the Archdiocese. Information about his new duties was found in the parish’s posts on social networks and in the media. The case arose during the term of Cardinal Josip Bozanić, who was Archbishop of Zagreb from 1997 until April 2023, when he was succeeded by Dražen Kutleša.

One priest, who wished to remain anonymous, explained that Bozanić should have been the first to report the case to the police. Since he did not do so, the obligation was taken over by Kutleša, because the new archbishop is at the beginning of his term informed about all open cases, especially accusations of abuse of minors.

whether or not the vatican has been notified is unknown

The guidelines of the Croatian Bishops’ Conference for the protection of minors oblige reporting to the competent state authorities. They state that the church authority, when it receives a report, must inform the victim or parents that they are obliged to report everything to the state authorities. If, after a preliminary investigation it is established that the accusation is credible, the church authority has the obligation to forward the report to the state authorities. Given that the Archdiocese ultimately did submit a report, this suggests that it considers the accusations credible.

According to church laws, the Archbishop of Zagreb, after the preliminary investigation, should also have informed the Vatican’s Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith about everything. It is not known whether Bozanić or Kutleša did so. Independently of church regulations, according to Croatian laws everyone is obliged to report suspicion of a criminal offence.

World.title: Environmentalist: Every Country Has a Mafia, in Croatia, the Mafia Has a  Country
World.content:
October the 13th, 2026 – An environmentalist has issued a damning message that while every country has a mafia, in Croatia, the mafia has a country. He added that people are “lobotomised by football” as Croatia slowly disappears into oblivion.

Environmentalist Vjeran Piršić recently spoke about pollution, waste management and habits that harm nature. Index reports that the well known mathematician and computer scientist who has been involved with environmental protection for decades assessed that Croatia is, as a nation, merely turning into a geographical concept and that the Croats will simply disappear as a people if the attitude towards resources does not change. He said that in Croatia, the mafia has the country and that people must wake up, reports HRT.

from maths to ecology…

Piršić’s story about ecology began back in 1980 on the island of Krk, where during the winter holidays in a cold house, he started thinking about energy efficiency. “It was absolutely freezing. I realised I couldn’t heat the house. I was under two blankets for seventeen days, listening to Pink Floyd and dreaming of living in an energy-efficient house, that the bura wouldn’t blow through and that I would be able to produce my own energy,” he said. Four decades later, he realised that idea and today lives in an energy-renovated house that produces more electricity than it consumes. At the beginning of the 2000s, his interest turned into a concrete struggle. The turning point was the Družba Adria project in 2002, which planned the export of Russian oil via Omišalj. Piršić, together with a group of like-minded people, decided to oppose it and founded the association Eko Kvarner.

“That would’ve been five million tonnes of muddy waters, with a heap of dangerous microorganisms and invasive species. A small group of us met at my home and we realised we had three options. The first was to move away, the second was to ignore the problem, but then it would only explode later. Or, we could try to fight. And us six lunatics decided to put up resistance to a project behind which stood Bush and Putin and Mesić and everyone else,” he said. After four years of struggle, with the help of other associations and people, the project was stopped.

“people in croatia are totally lobotomised”

Piršić warned about a system in which environmental impact studies, he claims, often serve to justify projects instead of objective assessment. As one of the hardest examples he cited Vranjic and the remediation of asbestos waste. “Vranjic is the evil of evils. That is the bottom of the bottom. I cried there many times,” he said. He was particularly affected by the absence of a wider public reaction to a problem that directly endangers people’s health. “One hero, Grgo Mandić, stands in front of a truck to stop a vehicle that is not for hazardous waste and is transporting it to a landfill that is not intended for that. And the police arrest him. There were maybe ten citizens, five activists. At the same time, a few kilometres away, at Poljud, thousands of Split residents were celebrating Niko Kranjčar’s transfer from Dinamo to Hajduk. I have nothing against Niko Kranjčar or Hajduk. But that is the madness. What matters is that Kranjčar came to Hajduk,” Piršić said.

Such a disproportion led him to the conclusion that citizens are reacting less and less to important problems, for which he also holds the media responsible. “People in Croatia are completely lobotomised. They are lobotomised by football, Turkish soap operas, Big Brother, by who anointed whom,” he said.

“this poison must be removed from the land”

He also spoke about the waste scandal from Gospić and explained that the proposal for temporary relocation to the area of Udbina arose after consultations with Swedish experts. He believes the first step is to remove the waste from the existing location, and then separate it and seek a long-term solution.

“You have poison under your skin. Those 35,000 tonnes of waste is poisoning this land. And believe me, it is poisoning everything,” he said. According to his proposal, the waste would be moved into appropriate bags and temporarily placed in the area of abandoned military infrastructure in Udbina. After that separation would be carried out, and as one of the options for storing the remainder he mentioned a protected part of the Željava tunnel complex, with appropriate protection and controls.

Piršić said that thermal treatment of waste is often presented as a simple solution, although its effectiveness depends on the whole system. “I don’t understand incinerators, but I have seen that in all countries where a proper waste management system has been set up, incinerators have nothing to burn. Those are huge and expensive facilities,” he said. He emphasised that even after incineration slag and ash remain which also need to be disposed of, and he warned about the importance of technology and supervision, mentioning reports of irregularities in Croatian cement plants. “So an incinerator is not the Joker so that we’ve solved everything,” he concluded.

“croats seem unable to understand very basic, elementary concepts”

He also commented on the problem of illegal dumps. He assessed that such a state shows serious shortcomings of the system, but also insufficient awareness of the general public. “That we are barbarians. That we are heavy barbarians who don’t even understand very basic, elementary things. Secondly, this is the crowning proof of my thesis that the environmental protection system has collapsed,” he said. As key steps he highlighted the education of young people, reduction of consumption, repairing of devices and proper waste separation. “If we really separate waste and teach children that the environment must be protected, then such ‘filth’ will not exist after some time. And there is no other way,” he said.

He also spoke about food waste. He said that this problem can be significantly reduced by better meal planning, thoughtful shopping and proper separation of biowaste. He explained that organic residues in landfills create methane, a greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change. He also shared his own experience, where his family by planning weekly meals and shopping according to a list significantly saves money and reduces waste. He considers food waste an environmental, ethical and financial problem.

“croats will simply disappear as a people”

Using the example of plans for the construction of large poultry farms, Piršić asked the question of who such projects benefit. He believes that development must not be based on megaprojects that neglect small producers, but on the preservation of space and domestic agriculture.

“Every country has a mafia. In Croatia, the mafia has an entire country. The key question is: who needs this? For whom was this Croatia created? Is this country intended for ordinary people with family farms or for big players with mega-projects that will wipe everything and everyone out? Croatia is disappearing. It is turning into a geographical concept. Croatian agriculture is destroyed, even though billions have been invested in it. Now, they will destroy Dalmatia and the Adriatic as well by seizing space and mega resorts. And the Croats will disappear as a people. Demographically, we’re already broken,” he said.

He was asked whether or not there is hope for Croatia, given the clear statement that in Croatia, the mafia has the entire country. Piršić drew a parallel with historical periods of national awakening. “People in Croatia tend to wake up every 100 years. For the protest in Gospić, we gathered in the square where the monument to Ban Jelačić is. So… the Croatian revival did something good. A hundred years after that there was Stjepan Radić. Maybe the time has come for us to finally wake up and realise that the point is not football, Turkish soap operas or Big Brother,” he concluded.

World.title: Foreign minister: No sign of Russian forces massing at NATO borders
World.content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte told Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) there are no signs of Russian preparations for an imminent confrontation with NATO, Tsahkna said Wednesday.

Tsahkna said Russia is nonetheless testing allies through sabotage and cyberattacks, and that NATO remains ready to defend every inch of allied territory.

The NATO chief was in Tallinn Wednesday and met with the foreign minister. The two discussed implementation of decisions taken at the NATO summit in Ankara in July, continued support for Ukraine, regional security, and Russia's acts of sabotage against allies.

"During today's visit, the NATO Secretary General emphasized what Estonia has consistently said: there are no Russian forces or other signs of preparations for an imminent military confrontation with NATO at NATO's borders," Tsahkna said. "At the same time, Russia is testing NATO allies through acts of sabotage and cyberattacks, but the alliance remains vigilant and united," he continued, via a ministry press release.

According to Tsahkna, NATO has taken highly practical measures in recent years demonstrating its readiness to defend allies decisively and in line with NATO plans.

"The Secretary General confirmed that NATO is ready and able to respond to any threat and defend every inch of allied territory. Article 5 of the NATO Treaty, which states that an attack against one ally is an attack against all Allies, remains in force," said Tsahkna. "NATO has demonstrated this repeatedly in recent years. It has responded to airspace violations and damage to critical infrastructure with concrete measures, confirming that the Alliance is ready to act."

NATO has consistently demonstrated its readiness to defend every inch of Allied territory. To ensure this remains true in the years ahead, we discussed today in Tallinn with @SecGenNATO Mark Rutte how to turn growing defence investments into real capabilities and keep NATO's deterrence and defence strong. We also discussed support for Ukraine. A just and lasting peace must be the goal, and Ukraine needs continued military assistance to defend itself against Russia's aggression. @NATO's PURL mechanism remains crucial, and Estonia will contribute an additional €10 million to Ukraine through this initiative. — Margus Tsahkna (@Tsahkna) October 14, 2026

Tsahkna said the two also discussed how NATO can ensure it remains capable of countering future threats. "Increasing defense investment by European Allies and Canada will enable NATO to meet its capability targets more quickly and strengthen its deterrence and defense posture," he said.

The discussions also covered expanding defense industry production capacity, applying lessons from Russia's war against Ukraine, and further support for Ukraine.

"It is in the long-term security interests of all NATO Allies that Russia's aggression against Ukraine ends with a just and lasting peace. For now, the priority is to equip Ukraine ahead of its fifth winter of war so that it can effectively protect its population and civilian infrastructure from Russia's increasingly brutal aerial terror and continue fighting for its independence and sovereignty," Tsahkna said.

He added that NATO support, including through the PURL mechanism, remains crucial to providing military assistance to Ukraine. "Estonia has so far contributed €21 million to Ukraine through the PURL initiative and will soon provide an additional €10 million through this mechanism."

"Estonia will continue to provide military assistance to Ukraine amounting to at least 0.25 percent of GDP each year, and our own defense investment already exceeds 5 percent of GDP," Tsahkna said.
