World.title: New Language Board chief to focus more on prevention than on fining businesses
World.content:
Minister of Education and Research Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) has appointed Martin Eessalu as director general of the Language Board.

Eesalu was proposed by the Government Office's senior appointments committee and replaces Ilmar Tomusk, who recently stepped down.

Eessalu's five-year term begins on January 1, 2027. The board needs to focus more on prevention and support, and less on fines, which the board can issue for instance in the case of customer-facing businesses failing to meet language requirements.

Eessalu also noted strengthening the board's capacity is the task for the coming years, and the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) will also be in focus.

"Alongside supervision, there is an increasing need to focus on prevention and support. The state's aim is not to issue fines, but to promote the use of Estonian and increase its vitality," he said.

"Second, I consider the use of language technology and artificial intelligence very important. A third significant direction is a greater contribution to Estonian language reputation activities and communication. Finally, it is important to take a fresh look at what institutional form can fulfill the expectations set. The team is small and the task is large, and there is also great potential for more substantive cooperation with other agencies, above all the Institute of the Estonian Language," Eessalu went on.

Since 2023 Eessalu has worked as director of R&D at the Institute of the Estonian Language (EKI). Prior to that he spent nine years at the Ministry of Education and Research in various language and research roles, most recently as head of the research infrastructure field, and served as acting director of the Estonian Literary Museum (Eesti kirjandusmuuseum) 2020-2021.

Eessalu takes over from Ilmar Tomusk, who had led the Language Board and its predecessor, the Language Inspectorate, for over 30 years. Tomusk did not apply for a new term when his previous one expired.

The Language Board (Keeleamet) is a government agency under the Ministry of Education and Research. Its main task is implementing Estonian language policy and state supervision of compliance with the Language Act and other legislation governing language use.

World.title: Publishers: Libraries' survival as important as national defense
World.content:
The Estonian Publishers' Association has issued an open letter urging the state and local governments to pay greater attention to libraries and literature as pillars of education, culture and mental well-being.

"The Ministry of Culture recently announced that state funding allocated to public libraries for purchasing books and other materials will be cut by €100,000. As the average price of books has also risen due to small print runs and increased costs, this will significantly reduce libraries' ability to purchase new books and make them available to readers," the Estonian Publishers' Association stressed in its open letter.

The association is calling on both the state and local governments to pay greater attention to libraries and literature as essential pillars of education, culture and mental well-being.

"The decline in deep reading among children and young people is not merely a cultural issue. It affects vocabulary, concentration, imagination, academic performance and the ability to understand oneself and others. These skills are essential for learning, working and participating in society as informed citizens."

"The 2025 reading survey 'Estonians Read 2025,' co-authored by Marju Lauristin, highlights a generational concern: 22 percent of people aged 50 to 60 and older are active readers with diverse literary interests, compared with just 11 percent of those aged 15 to 24. A strong interest in books among young people generally develops in homes with plenty of books. Public libraries must therefore help bridge disparities between households by providing every child with free, age-appropriate reading materials, good recommendations and opportunities to discover books, even when their family's book collection or financial circumstances do not allow it," the association explained.

According to the association, libraries are essential for readers of all ages who want to keep up with literature but find new books too expensive or live far from bookstores.

"Libraries are also important community centers. Without libraries and literature in our native language, it is impossible to ensure the survival of the Estonian language. This requires sufficient funding for libraries to maintain up-to-date and diverse collections of newly published works, support readers, authors and publishers through book purchases, and ensure that libraries do not become yet another disappearing community service."

The association said supporting the survival of libraries and access to literature in Estonian is just as important as what is traditionally understood as national defense.

"If we have no culture in our native language, what exactly are we defending?"

World.title: NATO chief in Tallinn: Estonia a benchmark for what a member state should be
World.content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Estonia does not merely meet the alliance's defense spending requirements — it sets the standard on it and other contributions.

Rutte was on an official visit to Estonia Wednesday. Speaking at a press conference in Tallinn, Rutte said "You don't just rely on the alliance – Estonia strengthens it," Rutte said.

"Estonia doesn't just meet its commitments, it sets the standards," he went on noting Estonia's defense spending at 5 percent of GDP is among the highest of member states, and its "exceptional leadership" in support for Ukraine.

The NATO Secretary General also called Russia's hybrid attacks, such as the Milrem Robotics arson attack, an attempt to force attention onto Putin and his problems rather than onto Ukraine's fight.

"Putin is trying to weaken our resolve and stop our support for Ukraine, but Russia is failing – it is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine, and we will not be intimidated."

"These hybrid attacks … are a sign of weakness. What they love us to do is to talk about it all day, and to be rattled, and to have press conferences on it. We're not going to do that. We will react where we need to react," noting that while some high profile responses to Russia's hybrid attacks, for instance Baltic Sentry, is highly publicly visible, other responses are not.

In response to a journalist's question, Rutte said NATO is a defensive alliance and there is no evidence Russia would attack a NATO ally.

"We don't think so, and we so no imminent threat against NATO territory. If we would see a build up, we will react to it."

Also appearing at Wednesday's press conference was Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform), who said Ukraine's NATO membership would in the long term be Estonia's strongest security guarantee, and that NATO itself would benefit.

Michal said supporting Ukraine represents a part of Estonia's own security, as Russia's aims have not changed. He said Russia is testing allied unity with hybrid attacks and trying to draw attention away from Ukraine — to make allies focus on their own problems and tire of supporting Kyiv.

Michal said Estonia will continue its military support, with aid this year amounting to 0.28 percent of GDP, down from 0.35 percent last year. He said Estonia has contributed €21 million to NATO's PURL initiative, and announced a new €10 million contribution.

The Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) initiative is a NATO-coordinated scheme under which allies and partners pay for weapons bought from the U.S. and sent to Ukraine. The U.S. itself has largely paused weapons donations to Ukraine under President Donald Trump, though it continues to share intelligence with Kyiv — as General Secretary Rutte pointed out in response to a question Wednesday.

The Estonian prime minister added Ukraine needs more weapons and, above all, more effective air defense, and that Estonia learns from Ukraine daily. He said Ukraine's experience is invaluable for developing Estonia's own defense capability and defense industry, whose revenues are growing at around 44 percent per year.

Ukraine's NATO accession is not currently on the table, largely due to opposition from several countries, chiefly the U.S.. Membership would also require Article 5 to apply, obliging all allies to come to the defense of an attacked member, and also requires a new member not be in a state of conflict at the time of joining, a condition which Russia has ensured cannot be fulfilled.

Asked about the claim that NATO could close Russia's access to the Gulf of Finland, and even the whole Baltic Sea, in the event of a conflict, Michal said that when it comes to the Baltic Sea, everyone can look at the Strait of Hormuz to imagine what would happen here if Russia attacked.

Rutte is visiting Estonia as part of his tour of NATO's eastern flank.

World.title: Defense minister: Estonia should consider acquiring light jet fighters
World.content:
Estonia should consider acquiring light fighter jets to counter Russia's increasingly fast and sophisticated long-range attack drones, Defense Minister Martin Herem told Postimees in an interview.

Speaking to Postimees after visiting Ukraine, Herem said Estonia must improve its air surveillance, command systems and multilayered air defenses, including machine guns, cannons, interceptor drones and potentially aircraft. He suggested that Estonia could explore arming its existing L-39 training aircraft with machine guns or small cannons, emphasizing that the aim would be to intercept drones rather than engage enemy fighter jets.

According to Herem, Ukraine's interception rate for Russian Shahed-type long-range drones has fallen from approximately 90 percent to 70 percent, significantly increasing the damage caused by Russian attacks.

The minister said Estonia should strengthen military cooperation with Ukraine by systematically collecting battlefield data, purchasing Ukrainian-made equipment and exploring joint defense production. Priority areas include electronic warfare, air defense, surveillance systems, drones and digital command-and-control capabilities.

A Czech-built Aero L-39 Albatros trainer jet in Air Force service. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

Herem warned that Russia's defense industry shows no signs of slowing down despite economic difficulties and could continue expanding even if the war ends.

During a roughly 30-minute meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Herem learned that Ukraine's most pressing air defense problem is a shortage of interceptors capable of destroying Russian ballistic missiles. He also stressed the importance of protecting critical infrastructure and providing adequate shelters for civilians, drawing on Ukraine's experience of surviving Russian attacks.

Herem warned that advances in drone warfare mean Estonia must prepare for a conflict in which the entire country could become an operational zone, with no safe rear areas.

Read more in Postimees.

World.title: Swedish prisoners in Estonia: No motivation to strive for a more law-abiding life
World.content:
An unannounced inspection of Tartu Prison by the chancellor of justice's advisers has revealed concerns among Swedish inmates over detention conditions.

One of the chancellor of justice's duties is to regularly inspect detention facilities and the conditions in which prisoners are held. On August 27, advisers to the chancellor of justice therefore made an unannounced inspection visit to Tartu Prison to examine detention conditions for inmates, including Swedish prisoners.

At the time of the inspection, Tartu Prison was holding 15 Swedish inmates. The chancellor's advisers interviewed eight inmates, spoke with prison officials, toured the prison facilities and reviewed selected documents.

"The inmates confirmed that no restraints were used on them during their journey to Estonia and that they were able to drink, eat and use the toilet during the trip," according to a report prepared following the inspection. Upon arrival at the prison, the inmates agreed to undergo medical examinations and were satisfied that they were promptly provided with the medication they needed.

Inmates did not agree to be transferred to Estonia

Most of the inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers said they had opposed their transfer to Estonia. According to the inmates, they were given very little advance notice of the transfer — in some cases about two weeks and in others just a few days.

The inmates had an opportunity to raise objections, but they felt the responses they received were vague and brief, in some cases consisting of just a few sentences. They believed they had not been given a genuine opportunity to defend their positions and that their personal circumstances had not been taken into account when the decisions were made.

The inmates explained that they had reportedly been well-behaved and motivated prisoners in Swedish prisons. They therefore believe that the purpose of transferring them to Estonia is not to support their reintegration into society, but to portray the prison rental arrangement as a success story.

They see their transfer to Estonia as a double punishment and say they have lost their previous motivation to work toward a law-abiding life. Concerns were raised that dissatisfaction among inmates could lead to more serious problems at the prison, particularly if the number of prisoners transferred from Sweden increases.

All the inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers claimed that, while in Swedish prisons, they had received information about detention conditions in Estonia primarily through an information brochure. They believed that the information provided in Sweden differed significantly from the actual conditions at the Estonian prison.

Some inmates claimed they had been assured in Sweden that they would continue serving their sentences at Tartu Prison under Swedish law. They also said they had been told that inmates at Tartu Prison would enjoy at least the same privileges as those in Swedish prisons, if not more. According to the inmates, this is not the case.

In addition, the inmates were unclear about what types of requests and complaints they were entitled to submit while at Tartu Prison, to whom they should address them and how to do so.

"The chancellor of justice does not know and cannot confirm what information was provided to the inmates in Sweden or how it was communicated, but all the inmates had similar impressions and understandings of the information they had received," the report stated.

Language barrier a problem

According to information gathered during the inspection, the inmates had not been given sufficient information about detention conditions and prison rules at Tartu Prison before being brought to Estonia. Once at Tartu Prison, language barriers have made it difficult for them to understand the information they receive and communicate with prison officers and other staff.

The inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers had some command of English. The report noted that language barriers could become particularly significant when discussing more complex matters.

The inmates said they believed not all prison officers spoke fluent English, which meant they had little communication with the officers and that officers had struggled to answer their questions. This increases the risk of misunderstandings, which the inmates said could lead to unnecessary conflicts.

For example, one inmate was prohibited from using an item that some other inmates were allowed to use. The inmate perceived this difference in treatment as hostile and believed it was due to his skin color and ethnic background.

However, subsequent discussions with prison officers revealed that the inmate had not been allowed to take the item into his cell because security stickers first needed to be attached to it. The allegation of discriminatory behavior by prison officers was not substantiated. The situation and the unnecessary tension it caused could have been avoided if the inmate had received a timely explanation in a language he understood.

The report also noted that prison officers had not yet used translation apps when communicating with inmates. Although an interpreter was present during medical examinations, the interpreter translated explanations from Estonian into English rather than Swedish.

For example, one inmate was found to have a heart-related health condition during a medical examination. The inmate said he would like to receive more information about his condition in Swedish and have the opportunity to ask questions about the complex medical issue and receive answers he could fully understand.

Fees to high to keep in touch with family

Based on information gathered during the inspection, the chancellor of justice's advisers questioned how thoroughly the family ties of Swedish inmates transferred to Tartu Prison in August, as well as the rights and interests of their children, had been assessed.

Several inmates who spoke with the advisers said their loved ones lived in Sweden and that they had maintained regular contact and visits with them before being transferred to Estonia. According to the inmates, the transfer has made communication with their loved ones considerably more difficult and in-person visits impossible.

One younger inmate said he was very close to his mother and two younger sisters, both minors. He said the transfer to Estonia had been extremely difficult for both him and his family, as they had been a major source of support and had encouraged him to lead a law-abiding life.

Another inmate said he had a child around 10 years old in Sweden and that, before his transfer to Estonia, he had hoped to reach an agreement with the child's mother that would allow the child to visit him in prison. According to the inmate, his transfer to Estonia has made such visits impossible.

A third inmate said his approximately 2-and-a-half-year-old child lived about 20 minutes from the Swedish prison where he had been serving his sentence. He had received regular weekly visits from his child since the child was 3 months old. The inmate was deeply concerned that his relationship with his child would be irreparably damaged and that the child would become estranged from him.

The inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers said they believed calling their loved ones from Estonia was more expensive than calling from Sweden. As a result, they may no longer be able to maintain contact with their families as frequently as before. At the time of the inspection, inmates transferred from Sweden to Estonia were not yet able to make video calls.

All the inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers said their loved ones could not afford to travel to Estonia because of travel and other costs associated with visits. Most inmates said neither they nor their family members had been informed whether financial assistance was available to cover travel and other visit-related expenses or, if so, how to apply for it. Only one inmate interviewed mentioned having heard that such assistance might be available.

Wrong placement of TVs

The inmates were also dissatisfied with the placement of two televisions side by side in cells at Tartu Prison. In Swedish prisons, televisions are mounted on the walls opposite the beds, allowing cellmates to watch television without disturbing each other.

Although inmates are allowed to use headphones, they find it distracting to watch two different programs simultaneously on adjacent screens. The inmates believed this arrangement could easily lead to conflicts.

Several inmates also raised concerns about the safety of sleeping in the upper bunk because it has no guardrail. They said they were afraid of falling out of bed while asleep and acknowledged that their sleep had been disrupted as a result.

The inmates explained that they had raised their concerns with prison officers and had subsequently been placed in cells on their own, allowing them to sleep in the lower bunk. However, they said the problem could arise again when more inmates arrive at the prison and two people are assigned to each cell.

No privacy while showering

The inmates who spoke with the chancellor of justice's advisers pointed out that the shower room in their prison unit has three showerheads positioned close together, intended to serve approximately 40 inmates. The inmates felt their privacy was not adequately protected while showering because there were no partitions between the showers. As a result, they currently shower one at a time.

The inmates explained that showering individually is manageable when there are seven or eight inmates in the unit, but becomes very difficult as the number increases. It is unrealistic to expect approximately 40 inmates to be able to use the shower room individually every day.

Muslim inmates noted that they had not yet had an opportunity to meet with an imam or participate in communal prayers. Prison officers acknowledged that inmates must be given the opportunity to practice their religion. However, it remained unclear whether arranging access to Muslim religious leaders was the responsibility of Estonia or Sweden.

The report stated that the problems could only be resolved through cooperation between Estonia and Sweden and that the findings would therefore also be forwarded to the relevant Swedish authorities.

World.title: Ambassador: Russia aims to make winter unbearable for Ukrainians
World.content:
Russia aims to make the coming winter unbearable for Ukrainians, and while there is no risk of famine, people are prepared for a difficult winter, Estonia's new ambassador to Ukraine said.

At the time Ambassador Tiina Intelmann, who presented her credentials to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy last month, moved to the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv once again came under heavy fire, with Russia launching large-scale strikes on the city.

According to Intelmann, however, a major problem is that attacks are now taking place both at night and during the day.

"Some time ago, it was still viable to live relatively peacefully during the day and take shelter at night. Another thing is that, of course, there are fast drones, but there are also missiles, including ballistic missiles, so the security situation is quite complicated. Naturally, I am also concerned about ensuring that my team can work safely. How much I can actually guarantee that is another matter, but it is clear that we cannot take any reckless risks," Intelmann said.

According to Intelmann, it has become normal for air raid alerts to sound three or four times a night, making sleep impossible.

"This is a situation where people simply cannot sleep. One alert comes at midnight, just as someone has fallen asleep, another at around three in the morning and then another at six. Generally speaking, for people who have access to a shelter, I think it is wise to simply sleep there, because nobody can keep running up and down to a shelter three times a night for a fifth year. As for the daytime, today we again had an unusual situation where a missile attack took place right in the middle of a Saturday afternoon. These things do not happen every day," the ambassador said.

Intelmann believes Russia wants to terrorize people behind the front lines because there has been no progress on the battlefield.

"They are trying to make people flee the cities, perhaps even flee to other countries, to European Union countries. This is all intimidation and terrorist tactics, nothing else can be said about it," Intelmann said.

"They are attacking civilians and, of course, energy infrastructure and water systems to make the winter as difficult as possible. The Russian Foreign Ministry's advance warnings that diplomats should leave because the security situation is going to become very, very bad are also part of the intimidation and pressure," the ambassador added.

According to Intelmann, Kyiv is already experiencing electricity and water outages, but people have prepared for them.

"Naturally, people already have independent systems to supply themselves with electricity. As for water, people simply have to stock up on water in their apartments. This is not the first time these things have happened," Intelmann went on.

Intelmann believes Russia's threats of nuclear war should be taken seriously, but there is no reason to panic, as the enemy uses various methods to create anxiety.

Ukraine's economy is currently stable, the ambassador added.

"If we consider that this is wartime, Ukrainians are not actually facing starvation. They are able to feed themselves. We also know that they cannot currently export their produce, so there is no need to fear hunger. However, the problem is that the Russians are destroying warehouses. Much of the food and medicine that has been imported and stored in warehouses is being destroyed. Ukrainians now have to consider how much they import, bringing in smaller quantities and perhaps keeping necessary reserves somewhere in other countries. In short, their own people will not starve. It will certainly be a difficult winter, and it will be cold," Intelmann said.

Intelmann has also served as Estonia's representative to the United Nations. At the recently concluded UN week, Ukraine once again had high hopes and delivered a powerful speech, but no major promises were made.

"The UN's best years are behind it. I do not know where this organization is heading, but it has funding problems and, more generally, a political problem because there is no political consensus. If we look at the Security Council meeting on Ukraine, the expression of solidarity took place outside the Security Council chamber. Yet we know that the Security Council is supposed to be the body that resolves questions of war and peace. Now we see attempts to resolve these questions of war and peace outside the Security Council chamber. This clearly shows that the organization is unable to fulfill the tasks entrusted to it," the ambassador said.

"The strength of this organization depends on how willing its member states are to work together, and right now we do not see that willingness. There are large countries that simply do not want to contribute to multilateral cooperation, and small countries that are willing to contribute but lack the leverage to do so," Intelmann concluded.

World.title: Tallinn City Archives restore historical goods hoist
World.content:
The historic freight hoist was restored and brought back into working order in the attic of the Tallinn City Archives building on Tolli tänav.

The wheel, which measures 3.4 meters in diameter, is believed to be the only functioning historic hoist in Tallinn. In the Middle Ages, however, almost every building had one.

Juhan Kreem, a researcher at the Tallinn City Archives, said every medieval building needed a hoisting mechanism in its attic because storage areas were located on the second and third floors.

"This particular example is much more recent. The building was in ruins in the 17th century and was not renovated until the 18th century when it was converted into a warehouse for the customs authorities. They needed a hoisting mechanism again, so they began assembling one from various components, the oldest of which may have come from a shipwreck or leftover materials at the harbor," Kreem said.

The freight hoist preserved at the City Archives dates back to the 19th century and has a 34.5-meter-long lifting rope.

During reconstruction work carried out in 2025, access to the historic hoisting mechanism was improved, making it possible to demonstrate how it works to visitors and conduct lifting demonstrations in the future.

World.title: Iraqi PM condemns Riyadh airport attack
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi met with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on Wednesday to discuss regional developments and efforts to enhance security and stability in the region.

Al-Zaidi reiterated the Iraqi government’s condemnation of the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as any harm perpetrated on individuals and facilities during conflicts.

He noted that such acts endanger regional stability, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi prime minister restated Iraq’s unequivocal opposition to actions that jeopardize the security of Saudi Arabia and other nations in the region.

He reaffirmed Iraq’s commitment to good neighborliness and respect for the sovereignty of Iraq and neighboring countries.

The meeting focused on strategies to enhance Iraqi-Saudi relations across various sectors, particularly through collaboration on security matters to address regional security challenges.

The Saudi crown prince reaffirmed Saudi Arabia’s support for the Iraqi government’s efforts to promote dialog and achieve stability in the region.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that the Iraqi-Saudi ties are important due to the political and economic weight of both countries, as well as Arab linkages and shared geographic, economic, and security interests.

Both Iraq and Saudi Arabia have made notable progress in rebuilding trust and promoting collaborative initiatives, which are vital for strengthening their bilateral relations, according to Al-Zaidi.

The prime minister added that Iraq’s security and Saudi Arabia’s stability are both critical to the peace of the Gulf States and the balance in the region.

World.title: Iraq calls on foreign firms to invest in Mosul International Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on foreign firms specializing in airport management and operations to invest in Mosul International Airport and develop its services.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his visit on Monday to the city of Mosul to launch the Watan Initiative (Homeland Initiative), a nationwide housing and development program aiming to tackle the country’s housing crisis, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Mosul International Airport, according to al-Zaidi, is more than just a service project; it is a critical gateway for the province and Iraq as a whole.

“We do not want the participating companies to merely construct a service terminal; rather, we want them to collaborate in turning the airport into an important service landmark,” al-Zaidi said.

Mosul International Airport, which was previously destroyed by ISIS terrorists, is the third most important airport in Iraq, following Baghdad International Airport and Basra International Airport.

December 2, 2007, marked the airport’s reopening following substantial runway and facility upgrades. It was first created as a civil airport in 1990.

The airport became a key military site after it was overrun by the terrorist organization ISIS in June 2014. They held it until the Iraqi army took it back on February 23, 2017.

Following its liberation, Mosul International Airport underwent renovations. By November 2019, de-mining activities were finished, and plans for a thorough reconstruction were initiated.

To complete the airport’s renovation, the Iraqi government inked contracts with SEA Milan Airports and Aeroports de Paris Ingenierie in December 2020.

Rehabilitating the northern Iraqi airport is considered critical for improving regional connections and assisting the local economy’s revival after years of conflict.

World.title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosque in occupied West Bank
World.content:
Mikhmas – Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque and graffitied its outside walls on Wednesday in the occupied West Bank village of Mikhmas, Palestinian sources and the Israeli military said.

Atta Kanaan, a Palestinian resident of Mikhmas who lives 50 metres from the mosque, told AFP that he heard the sound of breaking glass shortly after midnight on Wednesday and immediately went to the building.

“A fire was burning fiercely, and we called the fire brigade. Young men rushed to help us with fire extinguishers, and we managed to contain part of the fire before the flames engulfed the entire mosque,” he said.

Israel’s military told AFP that soldiers were dispatched to Mikhmas following a report of graffiti and arson at the mosque, as well as damage to a vehicle.

“No suspects were identified,” it said, adding an investigation had been opened.

AFP video footage showed that the fire had burned down the mosque’s interior carpeting and blackened the walls.

An AFP journalist reported that slogans were spraypainted in Hebrew on the exterior walls, including “just because we are quiet doesn’t mean we are asleep”.

Settlers also set fire to a car, Kanaan said, adding that in recent weeks villagers had formed night-watch patrols out of fear that settlers might torch homes, particularly those on the outskirts of the village.

Mikhmas is located in the central West Bank between Ramallah and Jerusalem, near several Israeli settlement outposts whose residents have attacked the community on several occasions in recent months.

Rouhi Fattouh, president of the Palestinian National Council, described the arson attack on the mosque as “a barbaric act and a dangerous escalation in settler terrorism”.

The Palestinian National Council serves as the parliament of the Palestinian Liberation Organisation.

Settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank has soared in recent months. Settler attacks have included physical assaults, land and crop theft, and vandalism of places of worship, homes and other buildings.

Excluding east Jerusalem, around three million Palestinians live in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, alongside more than 500,000 Israelis residing in settlements considered illegal under international law.

World.title: Saudi league postpones three matches after Houthi attacks
World.content:
Riyadh – The Saudi Arabian football league (SPL) has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr, following the dramatic escalation in the country’s war with the Houthis.

The matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for “logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches”, according to a statement published on Tuesday on the SPL’s website.

The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo’s Al Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.

The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures “will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes”.

On Monday, Al Nassr’s AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.

A violent battle between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen’s Houthis has erupted in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.

The latest round of fighting was triggered by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s international airport at the weekend that left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

World.title: Fulham manager Arbeloa fined £25,000 after Man Utd outburst
World.content:
London – Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been fined £25,000 ($33,000) by England’s governing Football Association after he claimed officials would “not let Manchester United lose”.

Arbeloa made his remarks following Fulham’s 1-1 draw with United in the Premier League at Craven Cottage in September.

Matheus Cunha equalised for visitors United in the 89th minute.

Arbeloa, who admitted the charge, has also received a warning for his comments, with the FA saying the Spaniard “acted in an improper manner by making comments in a post-match interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official”.

London club Fulham are currently bottom of the Premier League with just two points from their opening six games.

World.title: Iraq’s PM Al-Zaidi meets Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh
World.content:
Riyadh (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi met with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on Wednesday to discuss increasing regional trends and increased collaboration between Baghdad and Riyadh to promote Middle Eastern security and stability.

According to a statement from the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office, the two leaders reviewed the current regional events and how to coordinate their nations’ responses.

The meeting represents a crucial diplomatic interaction between Iraq and Saudi Arabia at a time of rising tensions in the Gulf, after fatal strikes on Riyadh’s international airport and ongoing disruption to regional energy and commercial lines.

During the meeting, al-Zaidi expressed the Iraqi government’s condemnation of the targeting of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as attacks and other actions that harm civilians and civilian infrastructure during armed conflicts.

The condemnation comes after a series of Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s international airport over the past week, raising concerns over the security of civilian aviation and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi’s visit comes as the regional war puts increasing strain on Iraq’s economy, notably via disruptions to oil exports and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The discussions come after several days of high-level Iraqi participation in international energy conferences sponsored by Saudi Arabia.

Iraq’s Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair and Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Waheeb attended the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh, where they met with Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman to explore ways to improve energy cooperation.

The two nations have been looking into ways to develop energy infrastructure, electrical cooperation, and economic relations, as regional instability has drawn attention to alternate trade and oil export routes.

Al-Zaidi’s meeting with Mohammed bin Salman elevates Iraq-Saudi ties to the forefront of broader diplomatic attempts to handle the effects of the regional crisis.

World.title: Two Iraqi army officers killed after explosive device left  by ISIS detonated
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi Army brigadier general and a warrant officer were killed on Wednesday after an explosive device left behind by ISIS exploded in the northern province of Kirkuk.

The Iraqi Ministry of Defense named the victims as Brigadier General Ahat Yasser Khudair Hussein, commander of the 11th Infantry Division’s Communications Command, and Warrant Officer Mutaz Shahid Abbas.

The incident took place in Wadi Zghaitun (Zghaytun Valley), which is located between Rashad and Daquq, around 80 kilometers (50 miles) south of Kirkuk.

The officers were performing a thorough search and inspection at an Islamic State (ISIS) hideout a day after Iraqi Air Force F-16 fighter jets had targeted the bunker.

The blast also injured two other soldiers, who were later evacuated for medical treatment.

This incident marks the second major attack on Iraqi security forces in Kirkuk during October 2026, occurring just days after US forces completed their military withdrawal from Iraq on September 30.

Last week, ISIS claimed responsibility for an attack targeting Iraqi police forces southwest of the city of Kirkuk, which killed one police officer and injured others.

Prior to the international coalition’s withdrawal from the country, Iraqi security officials cautioned that ISIS still has sleeper cells across Iraq, despite its defeat and the collapse of its rule in 2017.

The US withdrawal raised concerns about a potential security vacuum that could give ISIS an opportunity to regain its strength, as some officials warned that Iraqi forces would now be compelled to contain the organization without foreign military presence.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Pope recovering after lung cancer operation that rattles Church
World.content:
Rome – Pope Leo XIV began post-surgery recovery Wednesday after a tumour removed from his lung was found to be cancerous, plunging the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty.

Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in the operation and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is awaiting the results of tests to determine if the cancer has spread.

“The pope passed a calm night,” the Vatican said, without providing details.

The sporty 71-year-old, who was elected as the first American pope only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers.

He underwent the 90-minute operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on Tuesday, after which the Vatican said he “woke up normally”.

“The hospital is doing everything it can to help him get better, so let’s hope he recovers soon,” student Chiara Ruvolo told AFP outside the hospital north of the Vatican, where a banner read “Long live the pope!”

Experts said much would depend on how advanced the cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it was detected early and was localised.

“When caught in early stages, then it has a very very good prognosis, which is what we’re hoping and praying for with Pope Leo,” Juanita Mora, medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association, told AFP.

The Vatican has said it expects the pope’s recovery to take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20.

– Up and about –

Leo is staying in a room on the 10th floor of the building, next to a papal suite with a private chapel that is currently under renovation.

Professor Federico Venuta, head of Thoracic Surgery at the Policlinico Umberto 1 hospital in Rome, told AFP he expected Leo to be up and about immediately.

“Generally, on the first day, patients undergoing this type of procedure are mobilized immediately,” he said.

“They have a follow-up X-ray, resume eating with a light breakfast, and then start physical therapy right away — the sooner they get out of bed, the better,” he added.

Chicago-born Leo, a keen tennis player, had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday.

In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation.

– New uncertainty –

The shock news of his illness has rattled the Catholic Church, according to Vatican watchers.

“The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy,” expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP.

Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, said it was “a new phase”.

“We have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic… Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image,” he told AFP.

“This might prompt him to speed up certain matters,” such as personnel appointments.

“If he also has to undergo medical treatments, we don’t know if they might affect his pace or his ability to get things done, so there are many questions being raised today,” he said.

Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”.

Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, the dean of the College of Cardinals, is due to celebrate an important mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday that was to have been presided over by the pope.

The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades.

The surgery marks Leo’s first hospitalisation since he became pope on May 8, 2025.

The Vatican has historically been very secretive about the health of popes, but began to be more transparent during the illness of Leo’s predecessor, Francis, an Argentine who freely discussed his ailments.

World.title: As Canada minister calls on him, PM Modi backs momentum in ties

Wednesday and also held a meeting with her counterpart S Jaishankar.

NEW DELHI: India and the US are heading towards a landing point on the trade deal that they have been negotiating for over 18 months, Union external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Wednesday reviving optimism about the successful conclusion of the ongoing talks soon.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had suggested earlier this month there was a deadlock in the talks, with both sides reaching a point where it would be difficult to concede any further ground. However, Jaishankar said both sides continued to iron out differences. "I think we are waiting on a few things," he said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum.Jaishankar said India's trade minister, the US Trade Representative (USTR) and other officials are engaged in talks to move forward on the bilateral trade agreement. I think the trade ministers, USTR and our commerce and industry minister are working on that... Therefore, what is happening is every significant economy is getting into a negotiation with the US on this issue... In our case, we are pretty far advanced in that process of negotiation. "

World.title: ED seizes assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore of Reliance Power
World.content:
New Delhi: The

(ED) Wednesday said it has seized Indian assets worth Rs 2,033 crore belonging to Reliance Power Ltd (RPL), an entity of the Reliance Anil Ambani Group, under Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), for the alleged siphoning of assets worth an equivalent amount to tax havens of British Virgin Islands (BVI) and Cayman Islands.

The attached assets include bank balances of RPL and its shareholding in Sasan Power Limited. "The Headquarter Investigation Unit has seized assets worth â¹2,032.81 crore in India belonging to RPL, which are equivalent to the foreign exchange held outside India in contravention of FEMA," ED said. ED has already attached assets worth thousands of crores of the Anil Ambani group, including his residences in Mumbai, in multiple money laundering cases involving over Rs 40,000 crore.

ED said its investigation into findings of Sebi, pertaining to write-offs/provisions aggregating â¹2,101.46 crore made by RPL in its books of account, had revealed that "these write-offs were related to overseas investments and advances made to companies in the British Virgin Islands (BVI) and the Cayman Islands".

In a statement released to BSE and NSE Tuesday, RPL said the ED order of seizure of assets "relates to foreign currency convertible bonds issued in 2006, i.e.





20 years ago, and the related overseas investment made in 2008, i.e. 18 years ago, in a subsidiary in Singapore with all applicable approvals. The seizure primarily pertains to the shares held by the company in its wholly owned subsidiary Sasan Power Ltd, which are already pledged in favour of Power Finance Corporation Ltd (a govt undertaking) under security arrangements for more than 10 years, as well as certain bank balances of the company".

ED had conducted related searches in March and seized "several pieces of incriminating evidence", recording statements of several persons. "Investigation has revealed that Reliance Natural Resources Ltd (since merged with RPL) raised $300 million through foreign currency convertible bonds in 2006. Of this, $275 million was invested in its wholly owned Singapore subsidiary Reliance Natural Resources (Singapore) Pte Ltd (RNRL-S).

"RNRL-S placed these funds on deposit with Deutsche Bank (Suisse) SA, Geneva. The deposits were used as collateral for loans extended to entities incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. The investigation found that the BVI entities were controlled and managed from India by the Reliance Anil Ambani Group (RAAG) through front persons, who acted as per the group's directions," ED said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Further, the loan proceeds were utilised for varied purposes, including temporary round-tripping of funds to India through foreign entities based in Mauritius, the central agency said, adding that this was done to benefit the RAAG.

"The BVI entities failed to repay the loans extended by Deutsche Bank. As part of cover-up, documents were fabricated to show that RNRL-S and Indonesian subsidiaries of RPL had made advances to these BVI entities for apparently genuine business purposes. During investigation, it was found this documentation was backdated and prepared in order to project these transactions as genuine business transactions," ED said.

Further investigation is in progress.

World.title: SC: Order to clear Form 6 anomaly will come October 28
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Wednesday assured voters complaining of irregular deletion from the Delhi electoral roll during SIR that on Oct 28 it will take care of their predicament caused by being asked to fill Form 6, which required a declaration that they are seeking inclusion in the voter lists for the first time.

When advocate Prashant Bhushan sought urgent hearing on a petition to this effect by RTI activist Anjali Bhardwaj, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, "We are thinking of passing an order that will take care of it (the anomaly)."

Deleted voters canât claim to be first-timersâ

The bench proposed listing of Bhardwajâs application for hearing on Oct 30. Bhushan said that it needs to be heard earlier given that EC has set Oct 30 as the last date for correcting the discrepancy in the draft voter list.

SC agreed to hear the application on Oct 28.

Draft electoral roll of Delhi, published on Aug 31, noted that of the 1,45,10,299 voters who were on the rolls before SIR began, 97,53,577 have submitted enumeration forms, while 47,56,722 were excluded from the draft roll under absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories. EC had extended the time for filing claims and objections from Sep 30 to Oct 30.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Bhardwaj said the only mechanism prescribed for the âirregularlyâ deleted voters to re-enter their names in electoral roll is by filling Form 6, which makes it mandatory for the applicant to make a declaration that he/she is seeking inclusion in the voter list for the first time, which will be factually incorrect.





Of the 47.56 lakh excluded, nearly 32 lakh are categorised as permanently shifted. Bhushan suggested that EC could be directed to allow those seeking reentering of names in voter lists to apply using Form 8 or use another appropriate mechanism to restore/include names of existing electors that do not figure in the draft rolls.

World.title: ATC software glitch behind Air India false hijack scare? Probe on
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A false hijack alert created a real scare for security agencies and the 306 people on board Air Indiaâs Frankfurt-Delhi flight on Wednesday, with the Boeing 787 getting diverted to Jaipur as a result where everyone had to wait for hours before they could fly to their destination.

It is reliably learnt pilots operating the flight, AI 2030, did not squawk the code 7500 used to convey a hijack or unlawful interference, which has to be punched on a keypad like four letter code to unlock phones.

Still the recently installed air traffic control radar system at Mumbai, which is now an enroute ATC due to longer routes taken by Indian aircraft flying between Delhi and the west, somehow conveyed that scary message for the erstwhile Vistara B787-9 (VT-TSE).

âOnce that happened, Mumbai ATC spoke to the pilots who reported that all operations were normal on the flight. But protocols have to be followed in situations like this and so the plane was asked to divert,â said people in the know.

Why the false scare happened is now the subject of a probe by both aviation and security agencies, with Mumbai ATCâs new systems being looked at closely. Incidentally, air traffic control has been headless as Airport Authority of Indiaâs position of member (air navigation services) has been vacant for some time now and AAI itself does not have a regular chairman.





It remains to be seen how headless AAIâs headless ANS tackles the issue of reportedly false scares that have such an impact on passengers, crew members, security agencies and airline schedules apart from added costs.

On landing in Jaipur around 11 am, the plane was parked on a remote bay. For about two hours everyone remained on board before being asked to alight so that security agencies could check them all, the baggage and aircraft before clearing it to take off for Delhi after 2.30 pm with the same set of crew.

Senior B787 pilots say there is a âone in a trillionâ chance of the code being set to 7500 on the aircraft inadvertently or due to some error. âEach digit has to be physically entered. There is no button that can be inadvertently pressed. So from the pilot or plane side some error to happen is highly remote,â they say.

Senior air traffic controllers say Mumbai ATC has a new system. When a pilot squawks 7500 (hijack), then the colour of this aircraftâs dot on the radar screen turns red and an alarm goes off.

In a statement, Air India said: âAir India flight AI2030 operating from Frankfurt to Delhi on Oct 14 was diverted to Jaipur following a perceived security concern. The aircraft landed safely in Jaipur. The relevant security agencies carried out the necessary checks and have cleared the aircraft and crew. All passengers disembarked, underwent security checks, and have since reboarded the aircraft. The flight is expected to continue its journey to Delhi shortly.

âAir India teams worked proactively with authorities to minimise passenger inconvenience. We sincerely regret the inconvenience caused to our passengers due to this unforeseen disruption and appreciate their patience and understanding. The safety and security of our passengers and crew remain Air India's highest priority,â AI statement added.

World.title: Govt renames flagship social assistance scheme, drops Indira Gandhi tag
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday approved the continuation of its flagship social security scheme National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years until 2031, while renaming it Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana and dropping former PM Indira Gandhiâs name from three of its sub-schemes.

Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the âcomprehensive social security netâ will cover vulnerable groups, including the elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore is expected to benefit 3.2 crore people.

The revamped programme revises the eligibility criteria for pension for persons with disability (PwD) and increases the assistance provided under the sub-scheme.

As per the official release, Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme has been renamed PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana, the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme is now PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme becomes PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana.

This comes after the Cabinet approved a new rural employment guarantee scheme, Viksit BharatâGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in December last year, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).





Under the revised disability pension sub-scheme, monthly assistance will increase to Rs 375 for beneficiaries from birth to 79 years and to Rs 625 for those aged 80 and above. Till now, beneficiaries aged 18â79 received Rs 300 per month, while those aged 80 and above received Rs 500.

The eligibility threshold for benchmark disability has also been reduced to 40% from 80%, bringing the scheme in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

Govt said the revision was necessitated by the law, which has also mandated that disability-related assistance be at least 25% higher than that provided under comparable schemes for other categories. The revised scheme is expected to cover more than 27.48 lakh beneficiaries.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The pension amounts under the old-age and widow pension schemes, as well as assistance under the National Family Benefit Scheme, will remain unchanged.

The old-age pension ranges from Rs 200 to Rs 500 per month and covers 221.31 lakh beneficiaries, while the widow pension ranges from Rs 300 to Rs 500 per month and covers 67.38 lakh beneficiaries.

Under the National Family Benefit Scheme, a one-time financial assistance of Rs 20,000 is provided to a household following the death of its primary breadwinner, provided the deceased was aged between 18 and 59 years. The scheme covers up to 3.59 lakh beneficiaries.

World.title: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
World.content:
The Delhi government has approved a new industrial policy that outlines a ten-year roadmap for developing a clean, knowledge-based industrial economy in the Capital, with a focus on high-value, non-polluting sectors, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said on Wednesday.

The Industrial Policy, 2026, approved in a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, also allocated Rs 1,000 crore under Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana for five years to promote new industries and create jobs, said the statement.

Under the new policy, special incentives will be given for 10 priority sectors, including Information Technology (IT), global capability centres, data centres, healthcare, research and modern manufacturing, as per the CMO.

“Women-led micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will receive additional support for business modernisation and expansion. Employers hiring women will receive higher incentives for each woman recruited. Women and young people will also receive special attention under skill development programmes. These provisions aim to expand business and employment opportunities for women entrepreneurs and employees,” said the statement.

Advance technology hub

Ms. Gupta said the policy focuses on making better use of the Capital’s economic potential by encouraging advanced technology, research, specialised services and high-value-added industries. “Over the next 10 years, it aims to create an investment-friendly environment, provide necessary support to entrepreneurs, promote women-led enterprises and generate new employment opportunities for young people. It will also seek to steer Delhi’s industrial economy towards a more modern, cleaner and knowledge-based model,” she said.

Ms. Gupta said that considering the needs of different sectors, tailored incentives would be provided for capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new hiring, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy conservation and skill development. The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction, she added.

For instance, for IT and digital services a 25% incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to ₹10 crore (₹12 crore for women), will be available for three years. Also, an office rental assistance of 40%, up to ₹2 crore, will also be provided for three years, as per the statement.

World.title: Citizens asked to detail demographic changes in their areas through MHA portal
World.content:
The demography panel set up by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has launched a portal to allow government bodies, members of the public, NGOs, and even “international organisations” to submit their input on “frequent demographic changes in the country,” preferably post-2011.

The portal said that while these changes are most visibly concentrated in border districts, their impact has extended to affect urban centres, industrial corridors, tribal regions, and other socially and economically sensitive areas, severely impacting public service delivery, local governance, resource distribution, and social cohesion.

It said that these changes are “not attributable to normal fertility or mortality trends but are instead emerging due to external abnormal factors, including illegal immigration, irregular population mobility, and administrative laxity.”

Analysing demographic change

The MHA said that the inputs will help the panel to analyse and identify the causes of demographic changes and to recommend a well-organised and permanent operational system for the “legal, fair, and time bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants residing in the country.”

The portal mandatorily seeks the mobile phone number, address, and e-mail ID of the respondent, and seeks their consent for the processing of their personal data and review and analysis of the information provided.

The portal — https://demography.mha.gov.in — says that the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes (HLCDC), chaired by retired Supreme Court Judge Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar, was constituted on May 26 to study the “nature, causes and consequences of demographic changes being observed in various parts of the country.”

The respondents have been divided into three categories: Central government Ministries, departments, and organisations; State governments and Union Territory administrations; civil society organisations, non-governmental organisations, academic institutions, industry and business associations, international organisations, and think tanks; and individual citizens, public representatives, students, and others.

Public recommendations sought

There are eight questions under the individual citizen/public representative/student/others category. One of the questions asks the respondent to “describe the major demographic changes” observed or studied over the past 15 years in the geographical areas the respondent is familiar with, such as villages, towns, cities, districts, States/UTs, regions, or “across India.”

The survey seeks views on the principal drivers behind these changes and their impact on sectors such as employment, education, healthcare, housing, infrastructure, public services, the environment, social harmony, and local economies. It also invites respondents to identify challenges arising from demographic trends, highlight successful interventions by governments, local bodies, NGOs, community organisations or academic institutions, and share any research, reports, datasets or other evidence relevant to demographic issues.

In addition, participants are asked to provide their top five recommendations for addressing demographic challenges in India and submit any further comments, suggestions or supporting documents for the committee’s consideration.

States asked for religion-wise data

On September 28, The Hindu reported that the committee had sent State governments a 35-point questionnaire seeking extensive data on demographic changes over the past 15 years.

A significant portion of the information has been sought both district-wise and religion-wise, covering Hindus, Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Parsis.

The panel’s questionnaire sought a religion-wise break up of birth registrations, school enrolment, ration cards, vehicle registrations, property transactions, and voter registration. The committee has also asked States to identify unusual increases in Aadhaar enrolments, voter IDs, and ration cards, and furnish information about forged identity documents.

World.title: Electric mobility – the way ahead, says Taranjit Singh Sandhu
World.content:
The transition towards electric mobility is often discussed as a shift from one type of vehicle to another. In reality, it is a much broader transformation. E-mobility is the way forward for the nation’s strategic, growth, and ecological trajectory and Delhi as the national capital will have to take the lead on this road ahead.

It concerns how we produce and consume energy, how our cities are planned, the technologies we develop, the industries we build and, ultimately, the quality of life we provide to our citizens.

India’s mobility requirements are expanding rapidly. At the same time, we have to address energy security, air quality, urban congestion and climate change. This makes the transition, towards cleaner mobility, both an environmental necessity and an economic opportunity.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has observed that “clean mobility, powered by clean energy, is our most powerful weapon in our fight against climate change”.

Electric mobility, therefore, cannot be considered in isolation. An electric vehicle is part of a larger ecosystem, involving batteries, charging infrastructure, electricity generation, storage, manufacturing, recycling, and digital systems.

For India, the objective must be to develop this ecosystem in a manner that is economically viable, technologically capable, and accessible to citizens.

There has already been significant progress in this direction. Government initiatives such as the FAME programme and the PM E-DRIVE scheme have supported the expansion of electric mobility. PM E-DRIVE with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore supports electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, and related testing infrastructure.

But policy support is only one part of the transition. We must also develop the capabilities required to sustain electric mobility at scale. Battery technology, alternative materials, energy storage, and recycling will be particularly important.

A strong domestic EV ecosystem can create opportunities across engineering, electronics, software, battery manufacturing, component production, logistics, and related specialised services.

There is also a clear connection between electric mobility and India’s broader industrial ambitions. The automobile sector can be an important platform for investment, technology partnerships, and participation in global value chains.

India has already begun moving in this direction with Made-in-India electric vehicles entering international markets.

Immediate significance

For Delhi, the transition has an even more immediate significance. As one of the world’s major metropolitan regions, Delhi faces the interconnected challenges of mobility, air quality, congestion, and urban expansion. Cleaner public transport and personal vehicles can, therefore, contribute not only to reducing emissions but also to improving the everyday experience of citizens.

Delhi has already seen growing adoption of electric buses and other forms of cleaner mobility. The next step is to build an integrated system in which public transport, last-mile connectivity, charging infrastructure, and intelligent traffic management work together. This is particularly important for a city, where millions of people depend on public and shared transport every day.

The transition also presents an opportunity to strengthen Delhi’s position as a centre for innovation and sustainable urban solutions.

Our universities, research institutions, entrepreneurs, and technology companies can contribute to developing solutions suited to the specific needs of Indian cities.

At the same time, electric mobility must remain accessible. The success of the transition cannot be measured only by the number of electric vehicles on our roads. It must also be measured by whether citizens have reliable public transport, convenient charging facilities, and cleaner and more efficient ways of moving around the city.

Delhi, with more registered vehicles than the other three metropolitans put together, provides an important platform for bringing these perspectives together. The next stage of India’s electric mobility journey will require collaboration between government, industry, academia, and financial institutions. We need innovation that can be deployed at scale, investment that builds long-term capabilities, and infrastructure integrated with wider urban and energy systems.

Above all, we need a mobility transition centred on the citizen.

Electric mobility is ultimately not only about the vehicle. It is about cleaner air, efficient movement, technological capability, economic opportunity, and a more sustainable urban future.

I hope the efforts being undertaken in Delhi contribute to this larger conversation and importantly to practical solutions that can move from discussion to implementation.

Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Lieutenant-Governor, Delhi

World.content:
New Delhi

A Meerut court on Wednesday sentenced Muskan Rastogi and her partner, Sahil Shukla, to death for murdering her husband, Saurabh Rajput, whose dismembered remains were found in a cement-filled plastic drum in March 2025. Saurabh, a merchant navy officer, was killed on March 3 last year, and the body was discovered two weeks later. District and Sessions Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the sentence after convicting the duo of murder and destruction of evidence. The case, which drew widespread attention because of the brutality of the crime, saw more than 100 hearings and the examination of 22 prosecution witnesses. Prosecution lawyer K.K. Chaubey told reporters that the judge referred to the Mahabharata while explaining the punishment, observing that “justice required punishment proportionate to the gravity of the offence”. “Apart from the death sentence, the court also imposed fines totalling ₹70,000 on each convict for murder and the offence related to the disappearance of evidence,” Mr. Chaubey said. The two accused, who attended the proceedings via video conference, reportedly broke down after the verdict was announced. Lawyers present in the courtroom distributed sweets following the pronouncement. The detailed court order is awaited. The crime Saurabh, 35, returned to Meerut from London in late February 2025. According to the police investigation, when his family failed to trace him for several days, they approached the police, who recovered his dismembered remains from a cement-filled drum at the house he shared with Muskan. The couple’s six-year-old daughter allegedly pointed to the container when asked about her father’s whereabouts. In the chargesheet filed in May 2025, the police claimed that Muskan and Sahil drugged Saurabh before stabbing him to death and dismembering his body. They allegedly placed his remains in the drum, sealed it with cement and sand, and left for a vacation in Himachal Pradesh. The police used industrial equipment to break through the hardened cement and retrieve the remains. The police filed a nearly 1,000-page chargesheet detailing the evidence against the duo, including forensic reports, call records, CCTV footage and witness statements. Muskan, who was pregnant at the time of the crime, later gave birth to a girl while in jail.

World.title: Telangana govt. giving less than 8 hours power supply with interruptions to farm needs: Harish Rao
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Former minister and Deputy Leader of the BRS Legislature Party T. Harish Rao has alleged that the Congress government is not giving even eight hours of power supply to the agriculture without interruptions, and the logbook maintained at the Gattu substation in Jogulamba-Gadwal district is a testimony.

During a visit to the substation on Wednesday, he went through the power supply details recorded in the logbook and it had clearly stated that the farm connections were given power for 7 hours 50 minutes with three interruptions in between on October 13.

He stated that the consumers in urban areas and those of industrial category were being given sufficient power supply, while farmers were giving only a few hours of supply, that too with low-voltage. Earlier, Mr. Harish Rao along with the party leaders visited farm fields where standing crops dried due to erratic power supply.

Mr. Harish Rao said coming days would be even worse to the farm sector as the government had transferred all farm connections to the new Discom and allocated 85% of energy needed from solar and hydel sources. While solar power would be available only during the day time, hydel power was purely seasonal which could be generated only when the reservoirs have ample water.

During a visit to Induvasi village to console the families whose members died in a road accident near Yadgir in Karnataka while going there in search of wage work, two of them died and two suffered serious injuries, he demanded that the State Government announce an ex-gratia payment of ₹10 lakh each to the families of the deceased since it had failed to provide wage employment here and made them to migrate.

He stated that their (BRS) government had completed 80% of head works of the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme but the Congress Government had failed to complete the remaining works. Completion of small works in Package-3 would have allowed lifting of 50 tmc ft water this year to fill online and balancing reservoirs since reservoirs, tunnels, pump-houses and sub-stations were completed in the past itself.

Neighbouring Andhra Pradesh was taking Krishna water from Srisailam reservoir to areas 700 km away outside the basin but the Telangana Government had failed to utilise water despite having the network, he stated.

World.title: Sally Rooney's books no longer sold in U.K. over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
World.content:
Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be sold in Britain over her ​plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action, a ‌pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney ​and her publisher said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

The bestselling ⁠author, known for novels including “Normal People” and “Conversations with Friends”, has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after it was ‌proscribed by the British government under terrorism laws last year.

Ms. Rooney previously said in a witness ‌statement submitted to London’s High Court, in support ‌of ⁠a legal challenge over the ban on Palestine ⁠Action, that her plans could lead to her books being withdrawn from sale in Britain.

Her publisher Faber said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) that ​it had agreed with Rooney ‌that “we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format”, though it would sell her works elsewhere.

“Current legislation in the UK ‌has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on ​UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work,” Faber said in a statement.

“To sell ⁠a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.”

Ms. Rooney ‌said in a statement: “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences.”

Palestine Action, which had increasingly targeted Israel-linked defence companies, was banned shortly after a June 2025 break-in ‌at the Royal Air Force’s Brize Norton base.

Last year, Palestine ​Action’s co-founder Huda Ammori challenged the ban and the High Court ruled in her favour ⁠in February, before the Court of Appeal overturned that decision ⁠in June. The Supreme Court is due to hear an appeal next month.

More than 3,000 ‌people have since been arrested for holding signs in support of Palestine Action and its proscription ​has been criticised by civil liberties groups.

World.title: Engineering, management courses offer diverse career opportunities, says Expert
World.content:
Engineering and management graduates have diverse career opportunities across traditional industries, emerging technologies, research and business leadership, said Dr. Mitrabarun Ghosh, Assistant Professor at Paari School of Business, SRM University-A.P.

He was delivering a career guidance session titled “Career Directions: Engineering & Management” for final-year B.Tech students at Tirumala Engineering College, Narasaraopet, on Wednesday. The seminar on “Careers in Management & Sciences” was organised by The Hindu Future India Club in association with Paari School of Business, SRM A.P., in collaboration with Tirumala Engineering College. R. Satyanarayana, Secretary and Correspondent of Tirumala Engineering College, Dr. Y.V. Narayana, Principal, and V.V.S. Pradeep of SRM University were present at the programme.

Dr. Ghosh explained the opportunities available through technical careers and management education, emphasising that neither path was inherently superior and that students should choose according to their interests, skills and long-term aspirations.

While engineering offers opportunities in technology, research, design and innovation, management opens avenues in leadership, strategy, marketing, finance and business operations. Combining engineering experience with an MBA can help graduates pursue careers in product management, consulting and leadership roles, he said.

He highlighted employment opportunities in information technology, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, semiconductors, manufacturing and global capability centres. Government career options through GATE, UPSC Engineering Services, ISRO, DRDO, Indian Railways and public sector undertakings were also discussed.

The speaker drew attention to emerging sectors, including electric vehicles, green energy, space technology, defence startups and chip design. Alternative career options such as technical writing, patent analysis, research, public policy and entrepreneurship were also explained.

Dr. Ghosh guided students on higher education opportunities in India and abroad through examinations such as GATE, CAT, GRE and GMAT. He advised them to consider institutional rankings, accreditation, placement records, faculty expertise, industry connections and return on investment while selecting colleges.

He encouraged students to identify a primary career path and a backup option, prepare strategically for competitive examinations, and strengthen their profiles through projects, internships and certifications.

World.title: Marco Rubio to skip Delhi, visit Mumbai and Jamnagar next week
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India for his second visit in six months, with energy and trade relations at the top of the agenda as he visits Mumbai and Jamnagar, the U.S. Department of State announced on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

However, Mr. Rubio, who is expected to visit India from October 19 to 22 after travelling to Samarkand in Uzbekistan for a regional conference, will skip Delhi.
